English: WRONG — verb must have a resultative element

English: WRONG — stative/emotional verbs cannot take 把
Notes: Stative verbs (是, 有, 像), mental-state verbs (喜欢, 爱, 恨, 讨厌, 知道, 认识, 觉得), and perception verbs (看见, 听见, 闻到) cannot be used in the 把 construction. The 把 construction requires an agent who deliberately acts on a concrete object with a physical or tangible result.

The object of 把 must be definite , a specific, known thing. An indefinite object (a book you haven't mentioned before, an unspecified amount) generally cannot be used. The construction implies you are taking hold of a particular thing and doing something to it.

English: WRONG — unaffected objects cannot take 把
Notes: The object of the 把 construction must be affected by the action , it must undergo a change, be moved, be consumed, be transformed, or be disposed of. Perception and cognition verbs (看见 see, 听见 hear, 闻到 smell) involve objects that are registered but not physically affected.

安全 ānquán (safety) + 第一 dì-yī (first). A fixed slogan ranking safety as the top priority. Here 第一 means "the foremost concern," not a numbered position.

放 fàng (to place; put) + 下 xià (down; into a lower position). A simple directional 把 sentence , the object (bag) is moved to a lower location. 下 here signals downward movement or lowering into position. The 把 foregrounds the deliberate, targeted nature of the placing.

English: to open the window (strike it into an open state)
Notes: 打 dǎ (to hit; to strike , used as a general action verb with many objects) + 开 kāi (open; apart; into an open state). The combination 打开 means "open" , the object is moved into an open or separated state. 开 as a resultative complement implies separation, opening, or dispersal.

English: to close the door (shut it into the closed position)
Notes: 关 guān (to close) + 上 shàng (up; into a closed/attached state). Here 上 is a resultative complement indicating that the door has been moved into the closed, shut position.

English: to put the book away properly
Notes: 放 fàng (to place; to put) + 好 hǎo (well; properly; in the right state). The 好 signals the object reaches a satisfactory, correct, or complete state. 放好 is not just "put down" , it's "place in a way that is done properly." 好 as a resultative complement implies care, correctness, and readiness.

English: take the book out (bring it out into the open)
Notes: 拿 ná (to take; to hold in the hand) + 出来 chūlái (out-coming; out toward the speaker). The book is extracted from some container or location and brought into the present space. 出来 implies emergence from a hidden or enclosed place toward an open, accessible position.

English: bring the chair inside (move it in-coming direction)
Notes: 搬 bān (to move heavy things; to transport) + 进来 jìnlái (in-coming; into this space). The directional complement 进来 specifies both the direction (in) and the orientation toward the speaker (来). The 把 construction signals the chair is a definite, specific object being moved as a deliberate act.

English: to finish the homework (do it through to completion)
Notes: 做 zuò (to do) + 完 wán (to finish; to exhaust; resultative complement). The 完 is the result , the homework has been completely done. Without 完, the sentence would be ungrammatical: *把作业做. 完 is one of the most common resultative complements in the 把 construction.

Notes: 本 běn (this; one's own) + 人 rén (person). The very person concerned, as opposed to a representative or a rumor. On forms and in formal speech it means "I myself": 本人同意 "I personally agree."

English: ability; skill; what one is capable of

本 běn (root; origin; this) + 土 tǔ (soil; native place). Native, local, domestic, contrasted with 外来 wàilái (from outside) or 进口 jìnkǒu (imported). 本土品牌 = domestic brand. 本土文化 = local culture.

本 běn (root, origin) + 性 xìng (nature). The nature one is born with, deep and hard to change: 本性善良 "good-natured at the core." Often invoked when surface behavior gives way to what a person really is, as in 本性难移, that one's nature is hard to alter.

必 bì (certainly) + 定 dìng (settled; fixed; determined). A speaker's confident prediction about the future or about something not yet observed. The certainty is in the speaker's judgment, not a rule or law. Closer to "I am certain that" than to "you are required to."

Notes: 必 bì (certainly; without exception) + 然 rán (so; thus; naturally so , the word for "naturally" or "as it must be"). Together: that which is naturally and necessarily the case, which could not have been otherwise. The register is philosophical, historical, or scientific.

English: certain to win; victory is assured
Notes: 必 bì (certainly; without exception) + 胜 shèng (to win; to overcome). A morale-building formula rather than a measured prediction. English: one must admit; it must be acknowledged that
Notes: A common rhetorical move in essays and serious conversation, conceding ground before pivoting. The 必须 here is not commanding the listener; it is the speaker acknowledging an inescapable point. English equivalent: "it has to be said that," "one must concede that."

English: must comply with; must abide by (rules, laws)
Notes: The standard pairing in legal, regulatory, and policy language. 必须遵守法律 (must comply with the law). The phrase carries the formal-rules register that 必须 lives in: every Chinese workplace handbook, public notice, and company memo will use this collocation rather than its softer alternatives.

English: necessary; required; essential (for a given purpose)
Notes: 必 bì (certainly; without exception) + 要 yào (to want; to need; required). Necessity defined by a purpose or goal: if you want the outcome, this is what the outcome requires. The conditionality is built in.

Notes: 毕 bì (to finish; to complete) + 业 yè (studies). To complete one's course of study: 大学毕业 "to graduate from university," 毕业典礼 "graduation ceremony." A separable verb, so the object slots in the middle: 毕了业 "have graduated."

Notes: 变 biàn (to change) + 成 chéng (to become; to complete; to succeed), the directional complement. The standard compound for completed transformation: X has fully become Y. 成 is the result complement, indicating the transformation has landed somewhere definite.

English: to change the laws; political-legal reform (historical term)
Notes: 变 biàn (to change) + 法 fǎ (law; method; the Dharma, depending on context). The classical Chinese term for fundamental legal and institutional reform: changing the very rules by which a state operates.

变 biàn (to change) + 革 gé (to reform; leather, the image of tanning a hide and stripping away the old surface). 变革 carries more structural weight than 变化: it implies change to systems, institutions, or fundamental arrangements, not merely surface conditions.

English: changing hexagram; colloquial: to change one's mind, go back on one's word
Notes: In the 易经, 变卦 biànguà is the technical term for the resultant hexagram, the second hexagram produced when changing lines (爻 yáo that have reached their extreme) transform. The 变卦 reveals where the present situation is moving.

变 biàn (to change) + 化 huà (to transform; to dissolve into something new). The most general and most frequent word for change in modern Mandarin. Where 变 alone is the verb of transformation, 变化 is the noun: change as a thing that happens, can be observed, measured, discussed.

English: to debate; to argue (a formal case)
Notes: 辩 biàn (to dispute, to argue points) + 论. To debate opposing positions, each side marshalling arguments to win. The standard word for a debate competition (辩论赛 biànlùnsài) and for adversarial argument generally.

English: a marker; a label; to mark
Notes: 标 biāo (to label, to mark out) + 记 jì (a mark). A marker or tag that identifies a thing, and the act of placing it: 在地图上标记位置 "to mark a location on a map."
标 biāo (to mark; label) + 题 tí (heading). The title line printed at the top of an article, book, or section: 新闻标题 "a news headline," 大标题 "a big banner headline." Literally the marked heading.

English: to express: to convey; to articulate (thoughts and feelings)
Notes: 表 biǎo (to bring to the surface) + 达 dá (to reach; to arrive at; to get through). To convey thoughts or feelings so that they reach another person clearly. The 达 element adds the sense of successful transmission: not just showing something, but getting it across.

English: form: a table; a chart; a grid laid out for filling in
Notes: 表 biǎo (a chart; a surface where data is laid out) + 格 gé (a grid; a square; a cell). A printed or digital form, table, or grid: anything with rows and cells to be read or filled in.
表 biǎo (outer; to show) + 面 miàn (face). The outer surface of a thing, and by extension the surface meaning as opposed to the truth beneath: 表面上 biǎomiàn shàng "on the surface, ostensibly."

English: outer skin: the epidermis; the outermost layer or rind
Notes: 表 biǎo (outer) + 皮 pí (skin; hide; rind). The outermost layer of a living thing: the epidermis of human skin, the rind of a fruit, the bark-like surface of a plant. A precise term used in biology, medicine, and everyday talk about peels and surfaces.

English: to express: to indicate; to show (a feeling, attitude, or position)
Notes: 表 biǎo (to bring to the surface) + 示 shì (to show; to indicate; to make manifest). To express or indicate an attitude, opinion, or feeling, often through a word, gesture, or symbolic act. 表示 frequently introduces what someone states or signals: 表示同意 (express agreement), 表示感谢 (express thanks).

English: to show; to display; (noun) performance, conduct, showing
Notes: 表 biǎo (outer; to express) + 现 xiàn (show). To make an inner quality visible on the outside. As a noun it is one's showing or conduct: 他今天表现很好 "he did very well today."

English: to perform: to act; a performance; a show
Notes: 表 biǎo (to show outwardly) + 演 yǎn (to act; to perform; to develop). To perform before an audience, and the performance itself: music, dance, drama, magic, acrobatics.

宾 bīn (guest) + 馆. A house for guests, that is, a hotel. The word keeps the old hospitality sense of 馆 right on its sleeve.

English: to die of illness; to pass away from sickness
Notes: 病 (bìng, illness) + 故 (here, to pass away). A measured, somewhat formal way to say that someone died of illness, used in obituaries, official notices, and dignified speech. The 故 draws on the deceased sense: the dead belong now to what has passed.
病 + 菌 (jūn, bacterium, fungus): a disease-causing germ. Where 病毒 names a virus, 病菌 names the bacterial culprit, the everyday word a parent uses when telling a child to wash their hands.
病 + 情 (qíng, situation, state): the state of a sickness, how the illness stands. Doctors use it to report whether a patient is stable, worsening, or improving.

病 + 人 (rén, person): a sick person, the general word for a patient in a hospital or clinic. It names the person by their condition rather than their role, unlike 患者 (huànzhě), which is the more clinical register used in medical writing.

打 dǎ (to hit) + 破 pò (broken; shattered , resultative complement). The 破 is the result that makes the sentence grammatical. Breakage is typically undesirable , a window, a vase, a screen. The 被 construction here makes the glass the focus: it is the thing that suffered the breaking.

Notes: The flat negation, "impossible, no way." 这不可能 ("this is impossible"), 不可能的事 ("an impossible thing"). It is strong and absolute, unlike the softer 不太可能 ("unlikely") which leaves a sliver of chance. As an exclamation, 不可能！means "no way! / that can't be!"

不 bù (negation) + 快 kuài. The heart is not flowing freely , something is blocking it. Milder and more internal than 不高兴 (visibly in a bad mood); 不快 often describes a quiet dissatisfaction or sense of offense that hasn't been expressed.

Notes: 不…了 is the negation of sentence-final 了 , it signals a reversal of an expected or prior state. The 了 here paradoxically signals a new situation: the new situation is "not doing X anymore." English: one who gains without working; one who reaps without effort
Notes: 不劳而获 (to gain without labor) + 者. A full predicate (verb phrase plus adverb) nominalized by 者. The resulting noun phrase can serve as subject, object, or object of a preposition. Notes: 不 bù (not) + 然 rán (so). Literally "if it is not so," hence "otherwise." Warns of the alternative outcome: do this, 不然 the bad thing happens. Close to 否则 fǒuzé but more colloquial.

English: inhumane; callous; morally numb — also: physical numbness (limbs without sensation)

English: it wasn't me who said it (correcting the agent)
Notes: The classic defensive use of 不是…的: denying agency for a known past statement or action. Both parties know something was said , the 不是…的 corrects the attribution. This is one of the most practically useful forms of the construction in daily social life.

English: it wasn't bought yesterday (correcting the time)
Notes: Time correction: both speakers know the item was bought , the correction is about when. 不是昨天 denies the specific time; the speaker may then supply the correct time with 是…的.
Unwell: "not comfortable." The all-purpose symptom, the polite sick-day excuse, and the doctor's opening question in negative form: 哪里不舒服?

English: not very; not too; not quite
Notes: 不 bù (not) + 太 tài (very). The gentle negative, softer than a bare 不: 不太喜欢 "don't really like it," 不太方便 "not very convenient." The standard polite way to decline or downplay.

不 bù (not) + 同 tóng (same). The standard word for "different": 不同的意见 "differing opinions." As a noun it names the difference itself: 两者的不同 "the difference between the two."

English: not OK; won't do; no good; (terminally) declining
Notes: 不 bù + 行 xíng. The everyday refusal: "no, that won't work." 行 on its own as an interjection means "OK, fine, that'll do" , and 不行 is its negation. Notes: 参 cān (to take part) + 观 guān (to view). To visit a place in order to see it: a museum, factory, school, or exhibition. Reserved for touring sites, not for visiting people, where 看望 kànwàng or 拜访 bàifǎng is used instead.
Silk thread , literally "silkworm thread." The raw fiber before weaving. 蚕 is the silkworm; 丝 is the thread.
原材料仓 raw-material store, 成品仓 finished-goods store. A tidy warehouse with labelled batches (标识 biāoshí) is a good sign of traceability.

English: Cao Cao — the archetype of cunning ambition
Notes: The warlord of the north, in the novel the great villain: a brilliant general, administrator, and poet, but ruthless and treacherous, the man who declares he would rather betray the world than let the world betray him.

Notes: 草 cǎo (grass) + 地 dì (ground). Any stretch of ground covered in grass, from a park lawn to an open meadow. 在草地上 "on the grass."
草 cǎo (rough) + 稿 gǎo (manuscript). The first, unpolished version of a piece of writing or a plan. 打草稿 "to make a draft," to sketch something out before committing.
草 cǎo (rough; hasty) + 率 shuài (rate; rashly). Done quickly and without care, like grass thrown up overnight. 做事草率 "to do things carelessly."
草 cǎo (straw) + 帽 mào (hat). A hat woven from dried straw, the broad-brimmed shade of farmers and summer beaches. 戴草帽 "to wear a straw hat."

English: cursive script — the most expressive and wild form
Notes: 草 cǎo (grass; rough; draft) + 书 shū. "Grass writing" , like wild grass, cursive is fast, flowing, and irregular. Individual strokes merge; some characters are radically abbreviated. Legible mainly to trained readers. The style most associated with artistic expression and emotional intensity.

Notes: 草 cǎo (herb) + 药 yào (medicine). Medicine made from plants, the leaves and roots brewed in traditional Chinese pharmacy. Often expanded to 中草药 zhōng cǎoyào, Chinese herbal medicine.
草 cǎo (grass) + 原 yuán (plain). A vast open plain of grass, the wind-rippled steppe of Inner Mongolia or the prairies of the world. 内蒙古大草原 "the great grasslands of Inner Mongolia."

English: the heart of compassion / commiseration — sprout of 仁 humaneness
Notes: 恻隐 cèyǐn: the feeling of alarm and pity , specifically the involuntary distress one feels at another's suffering. The child-at-the-well example demonstrates this sprout. It is the first beginning of 仁 rén (humaneness/benevolence), the master virtue.

English: to measure: to survey, to gauge with an instrument
Notes: 测 cè (to gauge, to fathom) + 量 liáng (to measure). The formal verb for taking precise measurements: surveying land, gauging distance, recording temperature or pressure with an instrument. 测量土地 (to survey land), 测量距离 (to measure distance).

After vacuuming, each bottle is filled with hot water and its outer wall checked by hand or infrared (红外 hóngwài) to catch failed vacuums. It catches gross failures on the day, not slow leaks, which is why a sample is also held for a longer test (放置 fàngzhì, left to stand) before shipment.

English: to butt in; to insert oneself into someone else's affair
Notes: 插 chā (to insert) + 一 yī (one) + 脚. To stick a foot in where it wasn't invited , usually meddlesome but sometimes opportunistic. Cousin of English "to put one's foot in." Often pejorative.

English: wearing zhuyu sprigs — apotropaic plant, festival shorthand
Notes: 插 chā (to insert; to wear tucked in) + 茱萸 zhūyú (Cornus officinalis; Japanese cornelian cherry). The zhuyu shrub, with its fragrant berries and pungent scent, was believed to repel evil and disease. On Double Ninth, people wore sprigs tucked into their hair or carried them in small pouches.

Notes: Cha chaan teng: the quintessential Hong Kong casual restaurant, serving a fusion menu of Cantonese and Western-influenced dishes: milk tea, pineapple buns (菠萝包 bōluóbāo), egg tarts, congee, rice dishes, and Hong Kong-style French toast.

Notes: Teahouse: a social institution especially important in Sichuan and Guangdong, where one goes not just to drink tea but to play mahjong, listen to storytelling, or simply spend a morning reading the paper.

English: tea down — fine white hairs on young leaves
tea display dish — for showing the dry leaf

Notes: Teapot. The Yixing purple clay teapot (紫砂壶) is the prestige form, prized because it absorbs tea oils over time and improves with use.

English: theaflavins — the brightness compounds of black tea
tea tongs — for handling hot cups
Ancient Tea-Horse Road — the trade route that carried tea to Tibet
tea tray — the base of the gongfu setup
Tea leaves , the dry product before brewing
Notes: Tea leaves , the dry product before brewing. 茶 alone can refer to the beverage, the plant, or the leaves.

English: tea art; the art and ceremony of tea
Notes: 茶 chá + 艺 yì (art; skill, the same character as in 艺术 fine art). The performance and aesthetic dimension of tea preparation. 茶艺师 cháyìshī = tea master; a professional practitioner of the ceremony. 茶艺表演 = a tea ceremony performance.

English: a slip, an error; a mishap going wrong
Notes: 差 chā (off, deviating) + 错 cuò (error). A small slip or accidental error, and by extension an unforeseen mishap: 万一出了差错 "in case something goes wrong." Both halves mean "off the mark," doubling the sense of deviation.

English: to abdicate in favor of the worthy
Notes: The shàn reading's flagship: throne-yielding on the Yao-and-Shun model, the Confucian ideal of succession by virtue rather than blood, and the polite fiction wrapping most actual dynastic seizures.

English: Chan Buddhism — meditation, direct transmission, sudden enlightenment
Notes: The most distinctively Chinese Buddhist school. Chan (from Sanskrit dhyāna, meditation) rejected scripture-based study in favor of direct mind-to-mind transmission between master and student, the use of paradoxical dialogues (公案 gōng'àn, kōans), and the possibility of sudden enlightenment 顿悟 dùnwù i…

Notes: Output per day or month. 排产 (páichǎn) is scheduling an order onto the line; 旺季 (wàngjì) is peak season, when capacity disappears. In the months before Chinese New Year lines fill up and many workers leave early, so lead times stretch.

认证 rènzhèng (to certify, certification , 认 recognize + 证 proof/certificate). The system by which products are officially verified to meet standards. 3C认证 (China Compulsory Certification) is the mandatory certification for electronics, appliances, and vehicles sold in China.

质量 zhìliàng (substance + quantity → quality) is the standard word for quality in both the everyday and technical sense. 产品质量 is the fixed phrase for product quality , appearing in consumer protection law (产品质量法), manufacturing standards, and marketing.

Made on the production line with production materials, after tooling and before bulk starts. Hand samples can be perfect while line samples are not; insisting on a 产前样 catches the difference before thousands of units exist.

English: to produce; to give rise to; to emerge
Notes: 产 chǎn (to produce; output) + 生 shēng (arise). For abstract and concrete creation , ideas, problems, emotions, consequences arising. 产生影响 "to have an effect" · 产生误会 "to give rise to a misunderstanding."
The reduplicated 常. A common, conversational adverb for frequent action. Its negative is usually 不常 bùcháng "not often," since 不常常 is avoided.
常 cháng (constant; common) + 识 shí (knowledge). The basic knowledge that holds across a community, what one is expected to know: 生活常识 "everyday know-how," 缺乏常识 "to lack common sense."

English: to deliberately disagree; to sing a different tune
Notes: 唱 chàng (to sing) + 反调 fǎndiào (an opposing tune). To voice the contrary position on purpose, to be the one who always sings against the prevailing note. Colloquial and faintly critical.

唱 (sing) + 歌 (song). The social institution attached is KTV (卡拉OK), where 唱歌 is what colleagues, classmates, and business contacts do together; declining every song is borderline antisocial, and one rehearsed number is sound survival strategy.

Notes: 唱 chàng (to sing) + 片 piàn (a thin flat piece). A singing-disc: the physical record that holds recorded sound. 唱片公司 chàngpiàn gōngsī is a record label. The word predates and survives digital formats.

English: Vocal style , the melodic and tonal patterns of a particular role type. Different roles use different vocal registers and melodic conventions.
Notes: Vocal style , the melodic and tonal patterns of a particular role type. Different roles use different vocal registers and melodic conventions.

钞 chāo (paper money) + 票 piào (slip; note). A banknote, paper currency, cash in hand. This compound shows 票 at its purest: a printed slip of paper that stands for money. Closely related is 支票 zhīpiào (a cheque), where 支 zhī (to pay out) marks the slip as an instrument of payment.

English: to surpass; to exceed; to transcend
Notes: 超 (chāo, to overtake; to exceed) + 越. The figurative summit of the family: surpassing a competitor, exceeding a limit, transcending a category. Used in business, sport, philosophy, and self-development contexts.

English: dynasty: a reigning house and its era
Notes: 朝 cháo (court, reign) + 代 dài (generation, age). The standard word for a dynasty, the span during which one ruling house held the throne. Chinese history is told as a sequence of 朝代, each with its own name, capital, and character.

English: youthful spirit: vigor, the lively air of a new day
Notes: 朝 zhāo (morning) + 气 qì (air, energy). The energy of morning seen in people, a fresh, lively spirit. Said of the young or of any group full of drive: 充满朝气 "brimming with vigor." Its opposite is 暮气 mùqì, the listlessness of dusk.

English: forward; toward the front; facing ahead
Notes: 朝 cháo (toward) + 前 qián (front). Directed at the space ahead: 朝前走 "walk forward," 朝前看 "look ahead." A close everyday counterpart to 向前.

English: the imperial court: the ruler and the central government
Notes: 朝 cháo (court) + 廷 tíng (court hall). The ruler together with the ministers and offices around the throne, the seat of central power. To act 代表朝廷 is to act in the name of the throne itself.

English: morning and evening: every hour, day after day
Notes: 朝 zhāo (morning) + 夕 xī (evening). The two ends of the day standing for all of it: from dawn to dusk, every hour. 朝夕相处 "to be together morning and evening," to live in close daily company; 只争朝夕 "to seize every moment."

English: to face toward; the aspect or facing of (a building)
Notes: 朝 cháo (to face) + 向 xiàng (toward). To face a given way, or the facing itself. Common in describing buildings: 这套房子朝向南 "this flat faces south," a prized aspect for sunlight in Chinese homes.

English: the morning sun: the rising sun, dawn light
Notes: 朝 zhāo (morning) + 阳 yáng (sun). The sun as it rises, and the fresh light it brings. Used figuratively for anything new and full of promise: 朝阳产业 "a sunrise industry," a sector on the rise.
Tags: dynasty history direction characters cosmology yin-yang nature

English: toward; in the direction of (with sustained motion)
Notes: 朝 cháo (toward) + 着 zhe (the durative marker). The preposition with a sense of ongoing facing or movement toward something: 朝着大海 "facing the sea," 朝着目标努力 "to work toward a goal." Common in figurative aims as well as physical ones.

English: to mock; to ridicule; to jeer at
Notes: 嘲 cháo (to taunt; to deride) + 笑 xiào (laugh). To laugh at someone with scorn. This is the cruel edge of 笑: the same sound aimed downward at a target. Takes a direct object, the person mocked.
炒 (chǎo, to stir-fry) + 蛋: eggs broken into a hot wok and pushed around until they set in soft curds. The same 炒 powers most Chinese cooking, so 炒蛋 reads as plainly as English "scrambled eggs."
G-trains are the fastest, D-trains next. 检票口 (jiǎnpiàokǒu) is the boarding gate, shown on the screens next to the train number; 车厢 (chēxiāng) is the carriage, 座位号 the seat number.
Named by process: 冲压车间 stamping, 焊接车间 welding, 注塑车间 injection molding, 喷涂车间 painting, 组装车间 assembly, 包装车间 packing. 无尘车间 (wúchén chējiān) is a clean room.

English: travel ticket: a ticket for a bus, train, or coach
Notes: 车 chē (vehicle; car; train) + 票 piào (slip; ticket). A ticket for ground transport: a bus ticket, a train ticket, a coach ticket. The slip that proves you have paid your fare and may board. By the same pattern, 机票 jīpiào is a plane ticket and 船票 chuánpiào is a boat ticket.

English: carts made to the same track
Notes: Qin standardized the gauge of cart axles so that all wheeled vehicles fit the same ruts. The empire-wide road system, including the 直道 (zhídào, "straight roads") radiating from the capital Xianyang, depended on this.

Notes: 车 (chē, vehicle) + 站 (stop): the place where buses or trains halt and passengers board. The base word for any ground-transit station; specify with 火车站 huǒchēzhàn (train station) or 汽车站 qìchēzhàn (bus station).

陈 (chén, to lay out; stale, old , grain stored too long; also the Chen state of the Spring and Autumn period) + 旧 (old). Old in the sense of having overstayed its usefulness: 陈旧的观念 (outdated concepts), 陈旧的设备 (obsolete equipment).
To weigh. 称一下 ("weigh it, please") hands the fruit to the vendor. The same character read chèn means "to fit," as in 称心如意, suiting one's heart's wishes.

Notes: 成 chéng (to accomplish; to become) + 功 gōng (achievement). Literally "to complete the achievement." Both verb (to succeed) and noun (success). One of the most common words in modern Chinese, the natural opposite of 失败 shībai (failure). 成功人士 = a successful person. 取得成功 = to attain success.

English: grades; results; achievement (in study or work)
Notes: 成 chéng (accomplished; finished) + 绩 jì (achievement; spun work). The measured outcome of effort, most often school marks: 考试成绩 "exam results," 成绩单 "a report card." The finished score that shows how the work turned out.

English: to start a family; to marry and establish a household
Notes: 成 chéng (to become; to accomplish; to complete) + 家 jiā. The moment a household comes into being, through marriage and setting up a home together. One of the defining life-stage transitions in Chinese culture, paired with 立业 (establish a career) in the famous set phrase 成家立业.

成 chéng (accomplished) + 就 jiù (to attain). The lasting result of effort, the achievement one can point to: 巨大的成就 "a great achievement," 学术成就 "academic accomplishments." Weightier and more public than a single completed task.

Notes: 成 chéng (fully formed) + 熟 shú (ripe; cooked). Ripe in the literal sense for fruit and crops, and mature in the figurative sense for people, plans, and technologies: 成熟的苹果 "a ripe apple," 想法还不成熟 "the idea is not yet fully developed."

成 chéng (to accomplish; to become; to complete) + 为 wéi (to be; to serve as). The standard verb for transformation into a new state or role. Followed directly by a noun: 成为医生 (to become a doctor), 成为朋友 (to become friends), 成为问题 (to become a problem).

Notes: 成 chéng (to become; set; established) + 语 yǔ (speech; phrase). Set phrases , the four-character classical idioms that are one of the most distinctive features of Chinese. 成语 are compressed narratives, mostly four characters, encoding a story from history or classical literature.

English: to grow up; to mature; personal development
Notes: 成 chéng (to become; to complete) + 长 zhǎng (to grow). The compound for the full arc of development: physical, psychological, and social maturation. 成长故事 = coming-of-age story. 成长经历 = formative experiences. Also used for adult development: 这段经历让我很成长 "this experience helped me grow a lot."

English: to admit, to acknowledge, to recognize formally
Notes: 承 chéng (to bear; to receive; to assume) + 认 rèn. To shoulder the recognition of something , a fact, a fault, a state's legitimacy. Spans personal admission ("I admit I was wrong") and formal recognition (one country recognizing another diplomatically).

English: integrity; honesty and trustworthiness; good faith
Notes: 诚 chéng (sincerity; genuine; true to one's heart , 诚 is itself 言 + 成 chéng, words that have been completed, words that have come to pass; sincerity as the alignment of word with reality) + 信 xìn (trustworthiness).

城 chéng (wall; fortified place) + 堡 bǎo (fort; stronghold). A castle or fortress, the walled stronghold of a lord. 城堡 is the standard translation for the European castle, and the word most readers meet first in fairy tales and fantasy.

English: the City God — divine magistrate of the underworld
Notes: 城隍 (lit. "city wall and moat") is the divine magistrate of a city or county, presiding over both the living city and its deceased residents in the underworld. He holds court in his temple (城隍庙 Chénghuáng miào), trying the souls of the recently dead to assign their afterlife fate.

Notes: 城 chéng (city; wall) + 门 mén (gate; door). The controlled opening in the wall, the single point where the inside and outside of a city legally met. City gates were closed at night, manned by guards, and named individually; a walled capital might have a dozen, each a landmark in its own right.

城 chéng (city; wall) + 墙 qiáng (wall). The original sense of 城 made explicit. Where 城 alone once meant the wall, modern Mandarin pairs it with 墙 to specify the physical structure as opposed to the city it encloses.

城 chéng (walled settlement) + 市 shì (market). The most ordinary modern word for "city," and a fossil of how cities formed: a wall (城) for defense, a market (市) for exchange. The two together make the thing.

Notes: 城 chéng (city) + 镇 zhèn (town). A collective term spanning the whole range of urban settlement, from large cities down to market towns, used especially in contrast to the countryside (农村 nóngcūn).
吃 (chī, eat) + 饱 (full) as a resultative pair: to eat until satisfied. The negative is 没吃饱 (méi chī bǎo, did not eat enough), and a question often takes 吃饱了吗 (chī bǎo le ma).

English: to be jealous (in love); to eat vinegar
Notes: 吃 chī + 醋 cù (vinegar). Eating vinegar: romantic jealousy. The origin story: a Tang dynasty concubine had to drink vinegar as punishment when she defied orders, giving rise to this vivid metaphor. Exclusively romantic jealousy (not professional envy, which is 嫉妒 jídù).

English: To eat a meal , literally "eat cooked grain
Notes: To eat a meal , literally "eat cooked grain." Used as a general term for eating any meal regardless of whether rice is served. 吃 means "to eat"; 饭 means cooked grain or, by extension, any meal.

English: to endure hardship; to eat bitterness
Notes: 吃 chī (eat) + 苦 kǔ (bitter; hardship). To eat bitterness , to endure difficulty without complaint. One of the most culturally loaded compounds in Chinese. 能吃苦 (able to endure hardship) is a major virtue. 吃苦耐劳 = endure hardship and labor without complaint.

English: to suffer a loss; to be at a disadvantage; to get the short end
Notes: 吃 chī + 亏 kuī (deficit; shortfall). To eat a shortfall , to come out worse, to be cheated or disadvantaged. 吃亏是福 chī kuī shì fú (suffering loss is a blessing) is a common proverb: the Daoist wisdom that accepting disadvantage builds character.

English: ate; has eaten (the action is complete)
Notes: The most basic post-verb 了 construction. The 了 immediately follows the verb and signals that the action was completed. With a bare monosyllabic object, the 了 sits between verb and object. With a quantified object, this placement is even clearer and more natural.

就 in habitual statements describes characteristic immediate sequences , what this person always does right after something else. Often used with mild commentary (it might be a bad habit, or an endearing one). The 就 here encodes: no delay at all between finishing dinner and falling asleep.
Named after two old units of length, 尺 and 寸. 外径 (wàijìng) is outer diameter, 内径 (nèijìng) inner diameter, 壁厚 (bìhòu) wall thickness, 高度 height.

Notes: 赤 chì (red; bare; naked) + 脚. Bare-footed. Famously the term in 赤脚医生 chìjiǎo yīshēng, the "barefoot doctors" of the Mao-era rural healthcare program , village paramedics with minimal training who made primary care available across the countryside.
充 chōng (to fill) + 分 fèn (measure; share). Filled to the proper measure, fully sufficient: 充分的准备 "ample preparation," 充分利用 "to make full use of." Note the fèn reading.

English: substantial; enriched; full (of a life or content)
Notes: 充 chōng (to fill) + 实 shí (full; substantial). Filled to fullness, with nothing hollow: 生活很充实 "a full, rewarding life." As a verb it means to enrich or strengthen: 充实内容 "to flesh out the content."

充 (chōng, to fill; to be full) + 足 (sufficient). Filled to sufficiency , not merely enough but abundantly enough. 阳光充足 (ample sunlight); 准备充足 (fully prepared); 充足的理由 (compelling reasons). Stronger than 足够 zúgòu (merely enough).

English: to publish; to put out an edition
Notes: 出 chū (emerge; emit) + 版 bǎn (board; printing plate; edition). To emit a printing plate , to send a text out into the world as a published work. The metaphor is the woodblock or copper plate of traditional printing, the fixed form from which copies emerge.

出 chū (emerge; put out) + 产 chǎn (produce; give birth to; output). To yield products from a source , a region produces goods, a field yields a crop, a factory puts out units. Used for natural resources, agricultural yield, and manufactured goods. As a noun: the output, the produce.

English: to go wrong; to make an error
Notes: 出 chū (to come out) + 错 cuò (error). For an error to surface, often in a process or system: 系统出错了 "the system threw an error," 计算出错 "a miscalculation came up." Common in technical and procedural contexts.

English: to set out; to depart; to start from (a position or principle)
Notes: 出 chū (exit; emerge from) + 发 fā (to send out; to dispatch; to start moving). The moment of departure , leaving a point of origin for a destination. Physical: a train, a traveler, a team setting out.

English: to leave home; enter monastic life
to export; an exit; to speak
Notes: 出 chū (exit; emerge) + 口 kǒu (mouth; opening; port). Three interlocking meanings from the same compound. As trade: to export , goods going out through the port. As architecture: the exit of a building or tunnel. As speech: 出口成章 (words emerge perfectly formed , to speak with eloquence).

English: a way out; prospects, future direction
Notes: 出 chū (to go out, to exit) + 路 lù (road). Literally "the road out." Used for both physical exit (the way out of a building) and, more often, figurative prospects: career options, an escape from a bad situation, the future of an industry. 没有出路 méiyǒu chūlù = no way forward, no prospects.

English: to go out; to leave home; to set off on a trip
Notes: 出 chū (to exit) + 门 mén (door). To step out the door, whether for the day or for a journey: 我出门了 "I'm heading out." Its opposite is 回家 huí jiā or 进门 jìnmén.

English: to become famous; to make a name for oneself
Notes: 出 chū (emerge) + 名 míng (name; fame; reputation). To emerge into collective naming , to become the person or thing that others talk about and recognize by name. The 出 marks the transition: previously unknown, now known. 出名 carries no inherent judgment of whether the fame is deserved or welcome.

English: to go out; to head outside
Notes: 出 chū (to exit; to emerge) + 去 qù (away from here). To exit and move away from the speaker's reference point. Contrast: 出来 chūlái (to come out , exiting toward where the speaker is). 出去 is used by someone inside sending someone outside, or by someone outside talking about leaving an enclosed space.

Notes: 出 chū (emerge; stand out) + 色 sè (color; appearance; quality). "Emerging in color" , a vivid presence that distinguishes itself against its background. The color metaphor is apt: something outstanding has a quality that registers immediately, the way a saturated color stands out on a pale surface.

English: to enter trance; to be rapt

Notes: 出 chū (emerge) + 生 shēng (life; to be born; raw). Emergence into life: the original threshold crossing. 出生 is used for persons: 他在北京出生 (he was born in Beijing). The date is 出生日期 chūshēng rìqī (date of birth).

English: a problem occurs; something goes wrong
Notes: Here 问题 is unambiguously "problem": 出 chū (to emerge, arise) + 问题 = "a problem crops up, something breaks down." Used for malfunctions, complications, and things going wrong. Contrast 解决问题 (solve a problem) and 发现问题 (spot a problem).

English: to appear; to emerge; to come into view
Notes: 出 chū (emerge) + 现 xiàn (appear; manifest; current). To emerge into visibility , applicable to everything from a rainbow appearing after rain to a new problem appearing in a system. One of the most common verbs in news language and everyday description.

English: out of politeness; for the sake of courtesy
Notes: 出于 chūyú (proceeding from; out of) + 礼貌. Names the motivation behind a polite-but-not-sincere act: doing something not because you want to but because not doing it would be rude. Useful for marking the gap between social form and personal preference.

English: to stand out from the crowd; exceptional
Notes: 出 chū (emerge) + 众 zhòng (crowd; the many; multitude). To emerge from the mass of people , to be the one figure that rises above the surrounding level. Often used for talent, appearance, or personal quality that is genuinely rare rather than merely good.
除 chú (except) + 非 fēi (not). Literally "except if not," hence "unless." Often paired with 否则 fǒuzé or 才 cái: 除非下雨，否则我们就去 "we'll go unless it rains."
厨 (chú, cooking, the cook) plus 房. The room where food is prepared. One of the most frequent 房 compounds in daily life, and usually among the first room words a learner needs.

English: to handle; to deal with; to process
Notes: 处 chǔ (to manage; to dispose of) + 理 lǐ (to put in order). To take a matter in hand and see it through: 处理问题 "to deal with a problem," 处理数据 "to process data."

Notes: 川 chuān (Sichuan) + 菜 cài (cuisine). The cooking of Sichuan, famous for the numbing-spicy 麻辣 málà of Sichuan peppercorn and chili. 麻婆豆腐 and 回锅肉 are classic 川菜 dishes.

Notes: 穿 (to pass through) + 过 (guò, across, a directional complement). The verb of moving through and out the other side, a crowd, a forest, a tunnel. 过 marks the full traverse, in one side and out the far side.

English: to put on (and have it on)
Notes: 穿 (to thread on) + 上 (shàng, up/onto, here a result complement). The complement 上 marks the garment as now in place. 穿上 stresses the completed act of getting it on, against bare 穿 which can describe the habit of wearing.

穿 (to bore through) + 透 (tòu, thoroughly/through). Two synonyms stacked for force, used for light, sound, water, or radiation breaking all the way through a barrier. The technical word in physics and medicine for penetration.

English: to put on clothes; to dress
Notes: 穿 (to thread through) + 衣 (yī, clothing). A verb-object pair, the plainest way to say "get dressed." 衣 is the general word for what covers the upper body, so 穿衣 frames dressing as passing the body into a garment.

English: to pass through; to cut across; (popular fiction) to time-travel
Notes: Cutting through a region. Also the standard verb for popular time-travel fiction (穿越剧, 穿越小说) where a modern character is thrown into a past dynasty.

Notes: 穿 (to put on clothing) + 着 = the dressed state is in force. This is among the most natural uses of durative 着, because clothing occupies a position continuously. The same pattern applies to 戴着 (wearing a hat/glasses), 拿着 (holding), 带着 (carrying/bringing).

English: to disseminate; to spread; to broadcast; communication
Notes: 传 chuán (to transmit) + 播 bō (to sow, to broadcast). To spread information, ideas, or culture widely: 传播知识 "to disseminate knowledge," 大众传播 "mass communication." Also the academic field name, 传播学 "communication studies."

English: to convey; to pass on (a message); to communicate
Notes: 传 chuán (to convey) + 达 dá (to reach, to arrive). To deliver a message, an order, or a feeling so that it reaches its target: 传达指示 "to convey instructions," 传达上级的精神 "to pass on the leadership's intent." Stresses that the content arrives intact.

English: to pass; to relay; to convey; to transmit
Notes: 传 chuán (to pass on) + 递 dì (to hand over). To move something from one party to the next in a chain: 传递信息 "to relay information," 传递火炬 "to pass the torch." Stresses the act of handing along, often through several hands or steps.

传 zhuàn (a handed-down record) + 记 jì (to record). A written account of a person's life: 名人传记 "celebrity biographies," 人物传记 "biographies of notable figures." Note the reading shifts to zhuàn here, never chuán.

English: to infect; to be contagious; to spread (a disease)
Notes: 传 chuán (to transmit) + 染 rǎn (to dye, to be tainted). The spread of an illness from one person to another: 传染病 "infectious disease." Figuratively, an emotion or a mood that catches: 他的笑很有传染力 "his laugh is contagious."
传染 (chuánrǎn, to infect, to pass on) + 病: a disease that spreads from one person to another. It is the headline word during any epidemic and the category label on public-health notices.

English: legend; folklore; that which is passed down
Notes: 传 chuán (to transmit; to pass on) + 说 shuō (speech; to speak; theory). A legend or oral tradition , stories that have been passed down through generations without fixed written form.
传统 (traditional) + 节日 (festival, holiday). The inherited ritual calendar: 春节, 元宵节, 清明节, 端午节, 七夕节, 中元节, 中秋节, 重阳节. These are 传统节日 as opposed to 法定节假日 (statutory public holidays) like National Day.

传统 (tradition) + 文化 (culture). The received deposit of Chinese civilization: classical literature, Confucian ethics, folk festivals, traditional arts and crafts, medicine, cuisine, and everything else that is "Chinese" by inheritance rather than by innovation.

传统 (traditional) + 医学 (medicine). The formal name for the system of Chinese medicine (中医 zhōngyī) as a body of inherited knowledge: acupuncture, herbal medicine, moxibustion, massage (推拿 tuīná), and the diagnostic frameworks of qi, yin-yang, and the five phases.
船 (boat) + 票 (ticket): the fare for a passage by water, parallel to 车票 (bus/train ticket) and 机票 (plane ticket).
船 (boat) + 长 (zhǎng, chief): the head of the ship. The same 长 head-of suffix gives 校长 (principal) and 队长 (team leader).
船 (boat) + 只, here a classifier turned collective suffix. The pair names boats as a category rather than one hull, the way 车辆 names vehicles in bulk. Standard in port notices, news, and maritime law.

English: to start a business; to found a venture; to pioneer
Notes: 创 chuàng (to create; to initiate) + 业 yè (undertaking). To found something from the ground up, whether a company or a larger enterprise: 自主创业 "to start one's own business," 创业公司 "a startup." Carries the flavor of building where nothing stood before.
吹 (chuī, to blow) + 牛 (ox). From the full phrase 吹牛皮 (chuī niúpí, blow up an ox-hide), once said of herders inflating a hide skin-raft by lung power: big puff, little substance.
Borosilicate bottles are either 人工吹制 (hand-blown) or 机制 (jīzhì, machine-made). Hand-blown pieces vary more in wall thickness and weight; machine-made are more consistent and cheaper at volume.

English: Spring Equinox — balance of yin and yang
Notes: 春 chūn (spring) + 分 fēn (to divide; to share equally). The Spring Equinox: the day of perfect balance, when day and night are equal. In traditional cosmology, the moment when yin and yang are in exact equilibrium before yang takes the lead toward summer.

春 (spring) + 风 (fēng, wind). The mild wind of spring, and by extension any warm, reviving influence, a kind teacher, good news, a stroke of fortune. The phrase 春风得意 (chūnfēng déyì) describes riding high on success.

Notes: The Lunar New Year (春节 Chūnjié) is the year's most important ritual occasion. Before the family feast on New Year's Eve, offerings of food, incense, and paper money are made to the ancestors (祭祖 jìzǔ). Firecrackers (鞭炮 biānpào) are set off to drive away evil spirits and welcome the new.

Major customs of 春节: 贴春联 paste spring couplets on the door · 放鞭炮 set off firecrackers · 发红包 give red envelopes (现在多用微信红包) · 守岁 stay awake through New Year's Eve · 拜年 pay New Year visits · 吃饺子 eat dumplings (especially in North China, shaped like gold ingots 元宝).

Notes: 春 (spring) + 天 (tiān, day/season). The everyday word for the season, the one you reach for in conversation. 天 here marks a stretch of time rather than a single day, the same suffix in 夏天 (summer) and 冬天 (winter).

English: it's spring now; spring has arrived (no verb needed)
Notes: One of the most elegant features of sentence-final 了: it can attach directly to a noun phrase, without any verb, to announce that the situation has become that thing. This works because 了 marks change of state , and "it has become spring" is a state change even with no overt verb present.

English: the feel of spring; signs of spring
Notes: 春 (spring) + 意 (yì, sense/intent). The atmosphere of spring in the air, the green budding and softening light that signal the season has arrived. 春意盎然 (chūnyì àngrán) describes a scene brimming with spring.
词 cí (word; lyric; multi-character unit) + 典 diǎn (canonical reference). A dictionary organized alphabetically by pinyin or by topic that defines words and phrases rather than individual characters.

Notes: 词 cí (word) + 句 jù (phrase). Words and phrases taken together, that is, the wording of a text: 推敲词句 "to weigh one's wording carefully." It frames language at the level of phrasing rather than whole sentences.

English: Tune pattern , the named musical template to which a 词 is written. Specifies the number of lines, the syllable count of each line, the tonal contour, and the rhyme scheme. Several hundred standard tune patterns exist in the classical repertoire.

English: to hold compassion in one's heart; compassionate by nature
Notes: 慈悲 (compassion) + 为 (to be; as) + 怀 (bosom; to hold in the heart). To carry compassion as one's fundamental orientation. Used to characterize people of consistently gentle, merciful temperament , those who reliably respond to others' suffering with care rather than indifference.

Notes: 慈 (loving-kindness; tenderness) + 母 (mother). A classical compound appearing in the famous poem by Mèng Jiāo (孟郊, 751–814 CE): 慈母手中线，游子身上衣 , "In a loving mother's hands, thread; on a wandering son's body, clothing." 慈 here carries the full weight of gentle, attentive care.

Notes: 慈 (loving-kindness) + 善 (goodness; virtue). The compound that carried 慈 from the religious register into modern social discourse. 慈善事业 (císhàn shìyè, charitable work), 慈善机构 (císhàn jīgòu, charitable organization), 慈善捐款 (císhàn juānkuǎn, charitable donation) are all standard modern compounds.

English: the heart of deference and yielding — sprout of 礼 ritual propriety
Notes: 辞让 cí ràng: declining (an honor) and yielding (precedence to another). The capacity to defer , to put another's needs or claim before one's own in appropriate situations. The sprout of 礼 lǐ (ritual propriety).
此 cǐ (this) + 外 wài (outside). A formal written connector, "outside of this," used to add a further point: 此外，还有一点需要注意 "besides, there is one more point to note."

Notes: 聪 (cōng, sharp-eared; quick-witted , 耳 radical) + 明 (bright, clear-sighted , 日 sun + 月 moon). Intelligence as a compound of keen hearing and clear sight. 聪 alone originally meant "sharp of ear" in classical texts; combined with 明 (bright), it became the standard adjective for intelligence.

English: from then on; henceforth — narrative turning point
Notes: 从 cóng (from) + 此 cǐ (this; here). 从此 is a narrative marker that signals a permanent change of state after a critical event. Common in stories, histories, and personal narratives: 从此他再也没有回来 "from then on, he never returned." 从此以后 is the fuller form.

English: thereby; thus; and as a result
Notes: 从 cóng (following from) + 而 ér (and so). A written connective that draws a consequence: the second clause follows as a result of the first. Common in formal and academic prose.

English: always; never (with negation); at all times up to now
Notes: 从 cóng (from; since) + 来 lái (coming; up to now). "Coming from the past all the way here," from some starting point up to the present moment. Almost always paired with negation: 从来不 (never; has never) / 从来没有 (never; has never happened).

English: once upon a time; formerly; in the old days
Notes: 从 cóng (from; following) + 前 qián (front; before). "From the front / from the time that was in front": an even more remote and literary sense of "formerly" than 以前.

A fixed frame meaning "starting from now." 从 (from) plus 现在 plus 起 (to start). It marks a turning point or a resolution: 从现在起，我要早睡 ("from now on, I'll go to bed early"). A close variant is 从现在开始, with 开始 (to begin) in place of 起.

Texture stroke technique: the set of specialized brushwork methods used to render the surface of rocks and mountains. Different schools developed different 皴 techniques: axe-cut strokes 斧劈皴, hemp-fiber strokes 披麻皴, Mi dots 米点皴.

English: to miss (a chance, a train, a person)
Notes: 错 cuò (crosswise) + 过 guò (to pass). To pass by crosswise rather than meet: two things slip past each other and the moment is lost. Used for chances, trains, and people: 错过机会 "to miss a chance," 错过末班车 "to miss the last bus."

错 cuò (wrong) + 误 wù (to err, mistake). Both a noun, the mistake itself, and an adjective, mistaken or incorrect: 犯了一个错误 "made a mistake," 错误的决定 "a wrong decision." The standard, slightly formal word for an error of fact or judgment.

English: a wrongly written character; a typo
Notes: 错 cuò (wrong) + 字 zì (character). A character written incorrectly, whether mis-formed by hand or mistyped: 这篇作文有很多错字 "this essay has many wrong characters." A 错别字 cuòbiézì folds in 别字, the right-looking but wrong character.

Notes: 答 dá (to answer) + 题 tí (question). To work through the items on an exam or quiz: 认真答题 "answer the questions carefully." Its mirror is 出题 chūtí, to set the questions.

English: to agree; to promise; to answer (a call)
Notes: 答 dā (to answer) + 应 yìng (to respond). To answer a request with consent: to agree or promise. Also the literal "to answer" when called: 我叫了半天他都没答应 (I called for ages and he never answered). Note the neutral tone on 应 here.

English: to conquer the realm; to win power through struggle
Notes: 打 dǎ (to strike; to fight; to build through effort) + 江山 (the realm). Always implies hard-won, usually military achievement , you do not inherit 江山, you take it. The character 打 carries physical force: the same verb used for punching, striking, and waging war.

English: to break with tradition; to challenge convention
Notes: 打破 (to break, to smash) + 传统 (tradition). The act of violating inherited norms deliberately. In modern usage, 打破传统 can be positive (innovative, forward-thinking) or negative (disrespectful, reckless) depending on context.

English: to get through (a call); to open up (a passage); to clear a blockage
Notes: 打 dǎ (to make; to strike; to do) + 通 (to get through). A resultative verb: to do something until it is through.
The verb for producing samples before an order. 打样费 (dǎyàngfèi) is the sampling fee, often refunded against the first order; 打样周期 is how long sampling takes.

折 counts tenths of the price you pay, not the amount taken off. 八折 means you pay eight tenths, a 20% discount. Learners hear "eight" and think "80% off." In a negotiation 点 (diǎn, a percentage point) is more common than 折 for small moves.

Notes: 打 dǎ (to hit; to strike) + 字 zì. You are "striking" the characters into existence: the same 打 used in 打球 (play ball by striking it), 打电话 (make a phone call by striking a connection), 打鼓 (beat a drum).

English: the Great Prajñāpāramitā Sutra; the long form
Notes: The full Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, translated by Xuanzang in 600 fascicles, makes the Diamond and Heart Sutras look like fragments. The Heart Sutra is in fact a condensation of its core teaching. The long form unpacks emptiness across hundreds of contexts, dialogues, and lists.

English: great loving-kindness, great compassion — the full bodhisattva quality
Notes: 大 (great) + 慈 (loving-kindness) + 大 (great) + 悲 (compassion). The epithet most closely associated with Guanyin: 大慈大悲观世音菩萨. The reduplication of 大 before each component gives it the character of a liturgical formula.
Tags: buddhism compassion ethics virtue religion philosophy folk-religion

English: main road; grand way; the broad path
Notes: 大 dà (big; main; grand) + 道 (way; path). Physically: a wide, main thoroughfare. Philosophically: the grand way of moral order or heaven's intention.

大多数 (the great majority) and 少数 (the few) partition a set by proportion: 大多数人都同意 (most people agree), with the majority phrase taking 都 like any near-universal. 少数 appears in the fixed civic vocabulary 少数民族 (minority nationalities, China's official term for its 55 recognized non-Han groups).

大 dà + 方 fāng (square; proper; generous). Having the big-square manner: poised, natural, generous, not petty. Used for both personality (generous with money) and bearing (natural and composed, not awkward). A high compliment in Chinese social contexts.

大 dà + 夫 fū, but in this sense read dàifu with a neutral tone. A common, slightly informal word for a doctor, especially in northern speech: 看大夫 to see a doctor, 张大夫 Dr. Zhang. Read 大夫 dàfū instead and the same characters name a senior official of the old imperial court, a different word entirely.
大 dà (large, rough) + 概 gài (general outline; to level off). A rough outline: approximately, probably. One of the most natural hedges in spoken Mandarin: 大概三点 "around three o'clock."
Tags: cosmology scale daily-life grammar modal adverb communication

Notes: 大 (big) + 哥. Literally the eldest brother in the family. By extension it addresses the leader of a group, the boss of a gang, or any older man you want to flatter into helping you.
大哥 (big brother) + 大 again. First a nickname for the 1980s brick mobile phone, the status symbol of bosses; by extension the kingpin or undisputed number one in any field.
大 dà (big) + 海 hǎi (sea). The everyday word for the sea as a whole, the vast expanse of salt water. 大海捞针 "to fish a needle from the sea" is the Chinese "needle in a haystack."

Floor slang for the main order as opposed to samples. 大货生产 is bulk production, 大货样 a unit pulled from it. The word appears in nearly every merchandiser message: 大货已经上线了 means your order is on the line.

大 dà (big) + 家 jiā (family; home). Literally "the big family," used for "everyone present" or "all of us." Much warmer and more conversational than 人们. The go-to word for addressing or including a present group: 大家好！(Hello everyone!).

English: the Dajia Pilgrimage — one of the world's largest religious events
Notes: The annual Dajia Mazu Pilgrimage (大甲妈祖绕境进香) is a nine-day, eight-night procession covering approximately 340 kilometers through central and southern Taiwan, beginning from the Zhenglong Temple (镇澜宫 Zhènlán Gōng) in Dajia, Taichung.
大 (big) + 街 (street). A broad, busy thoroughfare, the high street of a town. Pairs with 小巷 (xiǎoxiàng, narrow lane) in the set phrase 大街小巷, meaning every street and alley.
大 (big) plus 姐 marks the eldest of several sisters at home. On the street it doubles as a friendly, respectful way to address a woman somewhat older than the speaker.

English: a large amount: a great quantity of
Notes: 大 dà (big) + 量 liàng (amount). Functions as a quantifier before mass and plural nouns: 大量资金 (a large amount of capital), 大量时间 (a great deal of time), 大量生产 (to mass-produce).

Notes: Big sound. Used adverbially before the verb: 大声说 (speak up), 大声朗读 (read aloud). Its opposite 小声 keeps the peace: 请小声一点，孩子睡了。Quiet please, the child is asleep.

Notes: 大使 dàshǐ (ambassador, lit. great envoy) + 馆. The ambassador's official house abroad. A smaller mission led by a consul is a 领事馆 lǐngshìguǎn, a consulate.

English: great knight-errant; heroic wanderer; the wuxia protagonist archetype
Notes: 大 dà (great) + 侠 xiá (chivalrous fighter; knight-errant). The archetypal wuxia protagonist: skilled, wandering, honorable, righting wrongs without official sanction. The 大侠 has no fixed home , the entire 江湖 is their domain.

Big-small: the size scale, the template for the whole antonym-compound family. 这双鞋大小正好 means the shoes fit exactly. Its siblings 长短 (length), 轻重 (weight), and 高矮 (height) work identically, and 轻重 doubles as "relative importance," what a tactless person 不知轻重 fails to weigh.
Tags: confucianism daily-life adjectives numbers grammar spoken vocabulary

English: university; college — and the Confucian Great Learning
Notes: 大 dà (great; large) + 学 xué (learning). The modern term for university. But 大学 is also the title of one of the Four Books of Confucianism (四书 Sìshū) , the 大学 (Great Learning), a short text that outlines the program of self-cultivation leading from individual virtue to social order to universal peace…
Tags: cosmology scale daily-life confucianism education culture philosophy

English: Great Learning · Doctrine of the Mean
Notes: Originally chapters of the 礼记, elevated to independent classic status by Zhu Xi. 大学 Dàxué outlines the nested self-cultivation program (修身齐家治国平天下).

English: the greater cause; moral principle; overriding righteousness
Notes: 大 dà (great; large) + 义 yì (righteousness; moral duty). The righteousness that supersedes personal ties, individual interest, or clan loyalty. 大义灭亲 dàyì mièqīn = to put righteousness above family (a set phrase for reporting or condemning a family member for the sake of the greater moral order).

English: to be greater than; larger than
Notes: 大 dà (big) + 于 yú (than). The comparison frame "greater than," standard in maths and formal description: 收入大于支出 "income exceeds expenditure." Its mirror is 小于 xiǎoyú (less than).

English: Greater Seal Script , the broad category encompassing the varied script forms of the Zhou dynasty bronze inscriptions, Stone Drum text, and oracle bone script.
Notes: Greater Seal Script , the broad category encompassing the varied script forms of the Zhou dynasty bronze inscriptions, Stone Drum text, and oracle bone script.

English: to handle on behalf of; to do for another
Notes: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 办 bàn (to handle; to manage). To take care of a task or piece of business in someone else's stead: 代办手续 "to handle the formalities for someone," 代办签证 "to arrange a visa on another's behalf." The errand done in your name.

English: to represent; a representative; to stand for
Notes: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 表 biǎo (to express; outward). As a verb, to represent or stand for: 红色代表喜庆 "red stands for celebration." As a noun, the person who represents others: 班代表 "class representative," 人民代表 "people's deputy."
Tags: meaning perception communication characters generation history society

English: to buy on behalf of; a purchasing proxy
Notes: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 购 gòu (to purchase). To buy something for another person, often goods from abroad: 海外代购 "overseas purchasing proxy." A familiar modern word from the rise of cross-border shopping, where one traveler buys for many at home.

English: price paid, cost (in effort or loss)
Notes: 代 (to stand in for, substitute) + 价 (price). The cost something exacts, not in money but in effort, sacrifice, or loss. You pay a 代价 for a mistake, a victory, or a hard choice.

English: to act as agent; acting (in a post); agency
Notes: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 理 lǐ (to manage). To handle affairs in an official capacity for someone else: 代理人 "an agent," 代理商 "a distributor," 代理校长 "acting principal." As a modifier it marks a temporary or proxy holder of a post.

English: to replace; to substitute for; in place of
Notes: 代 dài (to stand in for) + 替 tì (to replace). The general verb for one thing or person taking another's place: 用机器代替人工 "to replace manual labor with machines." Often follows the pattern A 代替 B, "A in place of B."

English: to neglect; to slight a guest through inattention
Notes: 怠 dài (lazy, inattentive, slack) + 慢 màn (slow). To fail to attend to someone with the care and promptness they deserve. The standard word for hosting someone poorly or neglecting a guest's needs. Often appears in apologies: 怠慢了您, please forgive my poor hospitality.

English: the elixir field — the body's energy center
Notes: 丹 dān (cinnabar; red; elixir) + 田 tián (field). The "elixir field," the body's primary energy reservoir. Three locations: 下丹田 xià dāntián (lower, 3 inches below the navel, the primary center and focus of most practice) · 中丹田 zhōng dāntián (middle, the chest) · 上丹田 shàng dāntián (upper, the head).
Tags: daoism religion immortality tcm body meditation philosophy

English: a single word; a vocabulary word
Notes: 单 dān (single) + 词 cí (word). One word taken on its own, the unit you memorize when studying a language. Common in 背单词 bèi dāncí, to memorize vocabulary.
The price per piece; 总价 (zǒngjià) is the total, 金额 (jīn'é) the amount on a line. The usual follow-up is what the unit price includes: 包括 (bāokuò) and 不包括 are the words to listen for.
单身 dānshēn (single, unmarried) + 汉 hàn (man). An unmarried man living on his own. The 汉 here is purely the colloquial "man," with none of the heroic ring of 好汉.

English: to take on; to shoulder (responsibility); accountability
Notes: 担 dān (to carry) + 当 dāng (to take up a role). To take responsibility upon oneself; as a noun, the quality of being willing to do so. 有担当 yǒu dāndāng describes a person who steps up rather than dodging.

English: to worry; to be concerned about
Notes: 担 dān (to carry on a shoulder pole; to bear a load) + 心 xīn (heart). Lit. "to carry the weight of the heart." Worry as a physical burden: the heart becomes heavy, something you haul around all day. One of the most common emotional verbs in everyday Mandarin.

Notes: May people live long; across a thousand li, may we share this moon's beauty together. Written in 1076, when Su Shi had not seen his brother Su Zhe for seven years. 婵娟 (chánjuān) was a classical term for the beautiful full moon.

Notes: 弹 tán (to spring, to bounce) + 性 xìng (property). The quality of stretching and springing back, literal in materials and figurative in arrangements: 弹性材料 "an elastic material," 弹性工作时间 "flexible working hours." Names a built-in capacity to flex without breaking.
蛋 (egg) + 白 (bái, white): literally the white of the egg. In science it extends to protein in general, and 蛋白质 (dànbáizhì) is the standard word for dietary protein.
蛋 (egg) + 糕 (gāo, a steamed or baked flour cake): a cake gets its name from the eggs whipped into the batter. The word covers birthday cakes, sponge cakes, and the slice you buy at a café.
蛋 (egg) + 黄 (huáng, yellow): the yolk. It pairs neatly with 蛋白, the two halves of every egg named by their color. Salted yolk, 咸蛋黄 (xián dànhuáng), is a prized flavor in mooncakes and pastries.

English: local; of the place in question
Notes: 当 dāng (right at) + 地 dì (place). "Of the very place" you are speaking about: 当地人 dāngdì rén (locals), 当地政府 dāngdì zhèngfǔ (the local government). The spatial twin of 当时.

English: face to face; to one's face; in person
Notes: 当 dāng (right at) + 面 miàn (face). To do something in someone's presence rather than behind their back: 当面说清楚 (sort it out face to face). Carries a note of directness and accountability.
当 dāng (ought, fitting) + 然 rán (so). "As it should be," and so "of course." Stands alone as a full answer (当然！"of course!") or leads a clause: 当然可以 "certainly you may."

English: at that time; then; at the time in question
Notes: 当 dāng (right at) + 时 shí (time). Points back to a specific past moment and the state of things in it: "at the time." Often paired with a later contrast, as in "back then I did not understand, but now I do."

English: at this moment; right now; the present
Notes: 当 dāng (at; facing; this very) + 下 xià (this point in the downward flow of time). The present moment , the point where time has currently descended to. 当下 has a slightly elevated, philosophical register compared to 现在 (now), and appears frequently in Buddhist and reflective contexts.

English: to take seriously; to take literally
Notes: 当 dāng/dàng (to treat as; regard as) + 真. To treat as real. Often used in the negative: 别当真 bié dàngzhēn "don't take it seriously," "I was just kidding."
Tags: knowing daoism philosophy virtue ethics daily-life

English: In public; in front of everyone (lit
Notes: In public; in front of everyone (lit. "at the mass"). The adverb that transforms many face-related situations. 当众批评 (dāngzhòng pīpíng, to criticize publicly) and 当众表扬 (dāngzhòng biǎoyáng, to praise publicly) are qualitatively different from the same acts done privately.

English: to treat as; to regard as; to take for
Notes: 当 dàng (to equate) + 作 zuò (to make, to do). To regard X as Y: 把困难当作机会 (treat difficulty as opportunity). A near-synonym is 当成 dàngchéng. Note the falling tone, which marks it apart from level-tone dāng.
Tags: meaning timing society characters production writing

English: to make trouble, to be naughty
everywhere; all over; in every place
Notes: 到 dào (arrive at) + 处 chù (place; location). Arriving at every place: ubiquity, pervasiveness. 到处都是 (there are ... everywhere) is one of the most common constructions. 到处找 (to look everywhere) = searching that has spread to every location.

到 dào (arrive) + 达 dá (reach; attain). Both components mean roughly the same thing, making 到达 more emphatic and formal than 到 alone. Standard in written Chinese for scheduled arrivals: planes, trains, deliveries, expeditions. Spoken Chinese usually just says 到.

English: after all; in the end; (interrogative intensifier)
Notes: 到 dào (arrive at) + 底 dǐ (bottom; base). Arriving at the bottom: getting to the root of the matter, reaching the real answer. In interrogative sentences, 到底 intensifies the question and demands a genuine response , it presses the interlocutor to stop evading and give a straight answer.
Tags: motion grammar daily-life vocabulary adverb timing communication

Notes: 到 dào (arrive) + 来 lái (come). A literary and slightly elevated compound used for the arrival of things rather than people in motion: the advent of spring, the arrival of a new era, the coming of opportunity. Found in formal prose and news writing more than casual speech.

Up to the present, used to measure a stretch reaching the present moment, often with 还 (still) or 都 to stress that something has or has not happened by now: 到现在他还没来 ("he still hasn't come, even now"). The fuller form 到现在为止 ("up to now") adds 为止 ("as the limit").

English: it would actually be better to (colloquial)
moral outlook; values framework; one's view of what is right and wrong
Notes: 道德 (morality) + 观 guān (view; perspective; lens through which one sees things , the same 观 in 世界观 worldview, 价值观 value system, 人生观 life philosophy).

English: the truth of the path — the Noble Eightfold Path
Notes: 道 dào = way, path. Sanskrit magga. The prescription: the 八正道 bā zhèng dào (Noble Eightfold Path): right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.

English: the Way models nature; the Way follows its own spontaneous pattern
Notes: 道 (the Way) + 法 (to model; to follow as a pattern) + 自然 (self-thus; spontaneous; natural). The culminating principle of Daodejing chapter 25. The Way does not follow anything outside itself , its law is its own spontaneous nature.
Tags: philosophy confucianism taoism cosmology nature heaven humanity classical

English: a Daoist temple; a Daoist monastery
Notes: 道 dào (the Way; Daoism) + 观 guàn (temple). The temple of a Daoist community, where 观 takes its fourth-tone reading. Set against the Buddhist 寺 sì (monastery) and the general 庙 miào (shrine).

English: Daoism — the way of naturalness and non-action
Notes: The Daodejing 道德经 (attributed to Laozi, c. 4th–3rd century BCE) and Zhuangzi 庄子. Central concept: 无为 wú wéi, effortless action aligned with the natural order. The sage ruler governs so lightly that the people believe they govern themselves.

English: reason; logic; principle; the way things work
Notes: 道 dào (way; path) + 理 lǐ (principle; pattern; grain of wood, the inherent structure of things). "The logic of the path." The way things make sense: the reason behind an argument, the principle underlying a situation, the basic logic that should govern behavior.

Notes: 道 dào (way; path) + 路 lù (road; route). The most standard, neutral word for a road or path. Used freely in both spatial and metaphorical senses. 人生道路 (the road of life) is one of the most common metaphorical applications, at home in political speeches and personal memoirs alike.
Tags: daoism philosophy path settlement daily-life society characters directions movement

English: moral duty; principle of right conduct; the Way and righteousness
Notes: 道 dào (the Way; the correct path; principle) + 义 yì (righteousness; moral duty). The pairing of the Way as principle and righteousness as conduct , what a person owes to the moral order. 道义上的责任 dàoyì shàng de zérèn = moral responsibility (as opposed to legal obligation).
稻 dào (rice plant) + 草 cǎo (straw). The dried stalks left after rice is harvested, used for thatch, rope, and scarecrows. 最后一根稻草 "the last straw," the final small thing that breaks a back.

English: Arrival of qi, the sensation confirming correct needling
Notes: Arrival of qi, the sensation confirming correct needling: heaviness, distension, or a spreading warmth at the needled point. Classical and modern acupuncturists both treat déqì as the essential marker of effective treatment.

To acquire guilt before someone: the verb of social danger. The folk warning 宁得罪君子，不得罪小人 advises that a crossed gentleman forgives and a crossed petty man files it away, which is the whole word-field in one proverb.
德 (phonetic transcription of "Deutsch") + 国 guó (country). 德 is the standard phonetic carrier for "Deutsch" in country and language names: 德国 Germany, 德语 German language, 德文 German script.

English: virtuous conduct; moral behavior; virtue as it shows in action
Notes: 德 dé (virtue; inner moral power) + 行 xíng (conduct; to walk; action). How virtue manifests in behavior , not the inner quality alone but the visible expression of it in how a person moves through the world. 德行 presupposes that genuine virtue is always legible: it shows.

English: Kṣitigarbha — guardian of hell and savior of the dead
Notes: Sanskrit Kṣitigarbha ("Earth Womb/Treasury"). The bodhisattva who specifically vowed to save beings in hell realms and not enter nirvāṇa until all hells are empty. Associated with Mount Jiuhua 九华山 in Anhui. His vow: 地狱不空，誓不成佛 (If the hells are not empty, I vow not to become a Buddha).
地 dì (ground) + 点 diǎn (point). A specific point on the ground, the precise spot where something happens: a meeting place, an event venue, the scene of an incident. More exact than 地方 dìfang.
When the focused element is a place, the construction answers "where?" — again, about a past event both speakers know happened. The place phrase typically includes 在 and appears immediately after 是.

地 dì (earth; ground) + 方 fang. The all-purpose word for "place," from a physical spot to an abstract point in an argument (这个地方我不同意 "on this point I disagree"). With full tone, 地方 dìfāng means "local" as opposed to "central": 地方政府 local government.

English: the underworld; the realm of the dead
Notes: 地 (earth; ground) + 府 (government office; official residence). The underground realm of the dead, governed by 阎王 Yánwáng (Yama, the king of the underworld) and his bureaucracy.
Tags: philosophy buddhism folk-religion classical poetry cosmology literary

Notes: 地 dì (earth; ground) + 雷 léi (thunder). Landmine , an explosive buried in the ground that detonates on contact. The compound is viscerally accurate: a mine hidden in the earth that erupts like thunder when triggered.

地 dì (earth) + 球 qiú (ball; sphere). Lit. "earth ball." The modern scientific term for the planet , a coinage that dates to the late 19th century, when Chinese translators had to name the heliocentric model.

地 dì (earth; ground) + 图 tú (diagram; picture; plan). Lit. "earth diagram." A transparent compound , the earth drawn out as a picture. 地图 is the standard word for any kind of map, from a hand-drawn sketch to a satellite navigation app.

English: underground; beneath the earth; covert; subterranean
Notes: 地 dì (earth; ground) + 下 xià (below; under). Literally: beneath the earth. Extended to mean "covert" or "underground" in the political sense , 地下组织 (underground organization), 地下工作 (underground/clandestine work). 地铁 dìtiě (subway; underground railway , lit. "underground iron") uses the same 地.

English: terrain; topography; the shape of the land
Notes: 地 dì (ground; land) + 形 xíng. The shape of the land: terrain, topography, the rise and fall of the ground. 地形复杂 = the terrain is complex; 地形图 = a topographic map. The most literal of the situation-words, where the shape being read is the physical landscape itself.

English: the hell realm; the path of extreme suffering
Notes: The lowest of the six realms: extreme suffering as the karmic consequence of severe negative actions , violence, cruelty, deliberate harm.

Notes: 灯 (lamp) + 光 (guāng, light, glow): the light a lamp throws, the lighting of a room or stage. Where 灯 is the object, 灯光 is the glow itself.
灯 (lamp) + 火 (huǒ, fire): the massed lights of a town or harbor seen at night, often in the literary phrase 灯火通明 (dēnghuǒ tōngmíng), brilliantly lit.
灯 (lamp) + 笼 (lóng, cage, basket): a flame or bulb held inside a frame of paper or silk. The red 灯笼 hung at the New Year and the Lantern Festival is its most familiar form.

English: to climb to high ground; to ascend
Notes: 登 dēng (to climb; to ascend; to mount) + 高 gāo (high; tall; elevated). The defining physical act of the festival. As a compound, 登高 appears broadly in Chinese outside the festival context , it can describe any ascent, or metaphorically, advancing in rank or achievement.

Notes: 等 děng (to wait) + 候 hòu (to await). A more formal, written-leaning word for waiting than plain 等. Common on signs and announcements: 请耐心等候 "please wait patiently."

English: to equal; to be equivalent to; to amount to
Notes: 等 děng (equal) + 于 yú. States equality, literal or figurative: 二加二等于四 "two plus two equals four," 不说话等于同意 "saying nothing amounts to agreeing."

English: low and short; squat; close to the ground
Notes: 低 (low) + 矮 (short, of stature or height). Used for structures rather than people: low-ceilinged rooms, squat walls, single-story buildings hugging the ground. 低矮的平房 (low-slung single-story houses) is a recurring image in descriptions of older hutong neighborhoods or rural architecture.

English: low and deep (of sound); somber; heavy; low-spirited
Notes: 低 (low) + 沉 (to sink, heavy, deep). The compound sits at the intersection of acoustic and emotional: a 低沉的声音 is a deep, resonant voice that seems to come from somewhere down in the chest; a 低沉的心情 is a mood that has sunk below normal , subdued, heavy, not quite depressed but nowhere near cheerful.

English: low place; lower ground; a lower spot
Notes: 低 (low) + 处 (place, location). A low-lying spot or lower area. Practical and descriptive in geography, architecture, and flood-risk contexts: 低处积水 (water pooling in low-lying areas) is a standard phrase in weather reports.

English: low-key; understated; keeping a low profile
Notes: 低 (low) + 调 (key, register, tone , musical or social). Originally the low musical key; now the social posture of deliberate understatement. 低调做人 (carry yourself with a low profile) and 低调行事 (act without fanfare) are standard phrases in professional and political discourse.
Tags: adjectives daily-life scale degree confucianism virtue social ethics

Notes: 低 (low) + 级 (grade, level, rank). At the lower end of a scale , which in practice means either genuinely entry-level (低级职员, junior staff; 低级别, low rank) or, more pejoratively, crude or vulgar in taste and behavior: 低级趣味 (vulgar tastes), 低级错误 (dī jí cuòwù, a basic mistake , the kind you shouldn't mak…

English: low; down; dispirited; fallen in spirit
Notes: 低 (low) + 落 (to fall, to drop, to settle down). Mood or morale that has fallen and settled at a low point. 情绪低落 (qíngxù dīluò, spirits low) is the standard phrase for feeling deflated, discouraged, or quietly unhappy without necessarily being in crisis.

English: one rank below others; to consider oneself inferior
Notes: 低 (lower) + 人 (person, others) + 一等 (one grade, one rank). To be placed one step below others in status , or to place oneself there through shame or social conditioning.

English: in a low voice; softly; in a whisper
Notes: 低 (low) + 声 (sound, voice). Speaking quietly, in a lowered voice. Appears as an adverb (低声说 , to say in a low voice) or a verb complement.

English: to lower one's head; to bow; to yield
Notes: 低 (low, lower) + 头 (head). The single most loaded compound on this page. Physically, it is simply to look down , at a phone, at work, at the ground while walking.

Notes: 低 (low) + 音 (sound, musical tone). The low end of the pitch spectrum , the bass register in music, the bottom frequencies in acoustics. 低音炮 (dīyīn pào, "bass cannon") is the colloquial term for a subwoofer. 低音提琴 (dīyīn tíqín) is the double bass. In vocal music, 低音歌手 is a bass singer.

Notes: 弟 dì (younger brother) + 子 zǐ. The pupil who studies under a teacher and carries the lineage forward, used of philosophical, martial, and religious schools alike.
第 dì (ordinal) + 二 èr (two). The ordinal "second." The same pattern extends without limit: 第三 third, 第四 fourth, 第十 tenth. The number after 第 is just the ordinary cardinal, unchanged.

English: which (in order); what number in a series
Notes: 第 dì (ordinal) + 几 jǐ (how many; which). The question form that asks for a position rather than a quantity. The expected answer is always another 第 form: 第三 (the third), 第七 (the seventh).

第 dì (ordinal) + 一 yī (one). The ordinal "first." Note the live tone-sandhi: 一 yī shifts to second tone before a fourth-tone syllable, so it is read dì-yí in 第一个 but stays dì-yī before a pause or another tone.
