Notes: 故 (cause; here, an underlying fault) + 障 (zhàng, obstruction, barrier). A malfunction in a machine or system: something with a cause behind it that obstructs normal operation.

English: to consider face; to save face for someone; to protect dignity
Notes: 顾 gù (to consider; to look after; to take into account). 顾面子 means to take face into consideration when making decisions or acting , whether one's own face or someone else's. More deliberate and conscious than simply 给面子. Suggests a thoughtful navigation of face dynamics.
顾 gù (to look after; to consider) + 问 wèn (to ask). The person one turns to and asks for counsel: 法律顾问 "legal adviser," 技术顾问 "technical consultant." Literally the one whom you regard and question.

English: hexagram; trigram; the unit of the system

English: hanging her mat to calm the storm
Notes: A convoy of ships was caught in a typhoon. Crew members and merchants, terrified, invoked Mazu. Her red skirt (or in some versions a red lantern) was seen at the masthead: she was present. The storm subsided.

English: correlation; connection; to be associated with

A common fixed expression used to characterize something as having major consequences or importance. 重大 zhòngdà = major, significant. Used in formal registers to signal that a decision, situation, or event carries real weight and should be treated with corresponding seriousness.

关 (to concern; to be connected to) + 心 (heart). The heart connected to something , caring. One of the most important relational verbs in Chinese. Both the action of caring and the expression of concern. High frequency in family, friendship, and professional contexts.
关 guān (to connect) + 于 yú (to). Marks the subject matter of a book, talk, or document: 关于历史的书 "a book about history." Where 对于 frames an attitude, 关于 frames a topic.

English: Gazing at the Vast Sea — an early landscape poem

Notes: 观 guān (view) + 点 diǎn (point). The particular angle from which you regard an issue: 我同意你的观点 "I agree with your view." The opinion you argue from, lighter and more debatable than a fixed 观念.

观 guān (view) + 念 niàn (thought). A deeper, more settled idea than a 观点: the concepts and assumptions one lives by, often slow to change. 传统观念 "traditional notions," 时间观念 "a sense of time / punctuality."

English: coffin — the most important object in traditional death culture
Notes: The coffin (棺材 guāncai) was traditionally a major family investment: solid wood, red lacquered, with auspicious carvings. The quality of the coffin reflected both the family's means and its filial devotion.

管 guǎn (to govern; to be in charge of) + 理 lǐ (to put in order). To run and oversee an organization, system, or resource: 管理公司 "to manage a company," 时间管理 "time management."

English: the bare verb: habits, facts, general truths
Notes: The unmarked verb is the default for habitual actions and standing facts, usually anchored by a frequency word: 我每天喝咖啡 (I drink coffee every day), 他住在北京 (he lives in Beijing), 地球绕太阳转 (the earth orbits the sun). No particle needed; adding 了 here would wrongly signal a completed event.

光 guāng (light; beam) + 明 míng (bright). More elevated and abstract than 明亮. Used in spiritual and political registers: 光明大道 "the road of light" (a righteous path), 走向光明 "moving toward the light." The opposite is 黑暗 hēi'àn darkness.

English: time; the passing days (literally "light and shadow")
Notes: 光 guāng (light) + 阴 yīn (shadow). The most poetic word for time in Chinese, naming the days by the very thing that measures them: the alternation of sunlight and shade, day and night, sweeping across the ground like the shadow on a sundial.
广 (guǎng, broad, expansive) + 东 (east). "The broad eastern region": the province that was the easternmost of the early southern territories brought under Tang-Song dynasty control.

Notes: 逛 (to stroll, wander) + 街 (street). A verb-object pair: to roam the streets with no fixed errand, window-shopping as much as buying. The default leisure activity in any Chinese city.

English: to stipulate; a rule; a regulation
Notes: 规 guī (rule; compass) + 定 dìng (to fix). To lay down a rule in advance, and the rule so laid down. 按照规定 ànzhào guīdìng "according to the regulations." The formal, institutional cousin of 决定.

Notes: 鬼 guǐ + 话 huà (speech; talk). Literally "ghost speech" , nonsense, lies, deceptive talk. The logic: ghosts mislead and confuse; speech that misleads and confuses is ghost-speech. 说鬼话 (to speak ghost talk) = to talk rubbish, to lie.

滚 (gǔn, to roll) + 蛋: a blunt order to get out. The image is of telling someone to roll away like a dropped egg. It is rude and forceful, used only in anger.

国 (nation) plus 歌 (song). The official song of a country, sung standing at ceremonies and medal podiums.

国 guó (nation) + 画 huà (painting). The native tradition of brush-and-ink painting on silk or paper, kin to calligraphy. Short for 中国画 Zhōngguóhuà, and set against 油画 yóuhuà, the imported oil-painting tradition.
国 guó + 际 jì (boundary; border; between). "Between countries." The standard word for anything international: 国际机场 international airport · 国际关系 international relations · 国际化 internationalization.

English: national conditions; the state of the nation
Notes: 国 (country) + 情 (conditions, circumstances, feelings). The specific circumstances of a given country , its history, population, resources, culture, and current state.

Notes: 果 guǒ (fruit) + 仁. The general category term: any kernel or "nutmeat." Wang Yangming and other Neo-Confucians explicitly used this image as the metaphor for moral 仁: a 果仁 is what gives the fruit its capacity to generate the next tree, just as 仁 is what gives a person the capacity to relate fully to…
果 (guǒ, fruit) + 肉 (flesh). The soft edible part between the skin and the pit, the meat of the fruit.
果 guǒ (fruit) + 实 shí (the ripened, full thing). The fruit a plant bears, and by extension the rewards of effort: 劳动的果实 "the fruits of labor." This is the seed-and-fruit sense of 实 made explicit.

Notes: 过 (guò, to cross) + 河 (river). A verb-object pair, to get to the far bank. It anchors several proverbs, since crossing water is the classic image of a one-way commitment.

English: you've overpraised me — a deflection of excessive praise
Notes: 过 guò (to exceed; to go too far) + 奖 jiǎng (to praise; to commend; an award) + 了 le (completion/change-of-state particle). A slightly more sophisticated deflection than 哪里哪里 , conceding that some praise may be warranted but asserting that the speaker has gone beyond what is accurate.

English: the past; to pass; to go over to
Notes: 过 guò (to pass; to cross; to go beyond) + 去 qù (away). As a noun: the past , what has passed away from the present. As a verb: to go over to (move across and away to a location). Both meanings share the same root image: time or a person crossing and moving beyond the current point.

English: after a while; in a little while
Notes: After a spell passes, used to push something a short way into the future: 过一会儿再打给你 ("I'll call you back in a little while"). 过 (to pass) marks the elapsing of the short time. A close, even softer relative is 等会儿 / 待会儿 ("in a bit, later"), the ready phrase for "hold on / later."

English: still far from good enough — modest self-assessment; "I have a long way to go"
Notes: 还 hái (still; yet) + 差 chà (to fall short; to be lacking) + 得 de (degree complement marker) + 远 yuǎn (far). A self-deprecating phrase that positions the speaker as still well short of a standard , pointing forward to future growth rather than backward at achievement.

The most versatile of the three hedges. As a standalone response to "how was it?" or "how are you?", 还好 reads as "fine, okay, not bad." As an opener to a clause, it shifts to "fortunately, luckily" , the speaker is noting that things didn't go as badly as they might have.

Used in questions that offer the listener a choice between two (or more) options: A 还是 B？It signals "which one?" and asks for a pick. A choice question with 还是 does not also take 吗, since 还是 already makes it a question. The options can be nouns, verbs, or whole clauses.

孩 paired with 童 (child, youngster). A bookish, slightly elevated word for children, common in writing and formal speech rather than casual talk.

孩 (child) plus the neutral-tone suffix 子, which turns many one-syllable nouns into stable everyday words. 孩子 is the default word for a child and also the word a parent uses for a son or daughter of any age.

海 (hǎi, sea) plus 报: a public announcement spread far and wide. The word for a poster or playbill, the kind pasted on a wall to advertise a film or a show.
海 hǎi (sea) + 边 biān (edge; side). The edge where land meets sea, the place you go to be beside the water: 去海边度假 "to vacation at the seaside."
海 hǎi (sea) + 岛 dǎo (island). A piece of land surrounded by sea. Where 岛 alone is any island, 海岛 stresses the open-sea setting, far from the mainland.
海 hǎi (sea) + 关 guān (pass; barrier). The customs authority that inspects goods crossing a border, named for the sea-passage through which trade once arrived: 过海关 "to clear customs."

Notes: 海 hǎi (sea) + 军 jūn (army; armed force). The naval branch of the military, the "sea army." Its siblings are 陆军 lùjūn (the army, "land force") and 空军 kōngjūn (the air force).

English: to fall ill, to be sick
Notes: 害 (to be afflicted by) + 病 (illness). The causative branch: to be struck down by sickness. Colloquial and slightly regional; 生病 (shēngbìng) is the neutral standard.
害 (harmful) + 虫 (insect). An insect that damages crops or carries disease. Its counterpart is 益虫 (yìchóng), a beneficial insect.
害 (dread) reinforced by 怕 (to fear). The default spoken verb for fear of a concrete thing or outcome. Takes an object directly or stands alone.
害 (to suffer a feeling) + 羞 (shame). To be visited by shyness, the blush of being seen. Describes a person's manner, not a one-off act.

Notes: 好 hǎo (good) + 处 chù (place; aspect; point). The good points of something: its advantages. Contrast: 坏处 huàichù (bad points; disadvantages).

English: a brave fellow; a stout-hearted hero
Notes: 好 hǎo (good) + 汉 hàn (fellow). A bold, admirable man, the heroic outlaw or stalwart of old novels. The saying 好汉不吃眼前亏 "a wise fellow does not take a loss he can avoid" shows its everyday use.
好 (good) + 喝 (drink): pleasant to drink. Mandarin splits "tasty" by mouth-action, so liquids are 好喝 while solid food is 好吃 (hǎo chī), good to eat.

Tags: virtue social daily-life aesthetics culture philosophy

English: done; ready; okay; alright (change of state)
Notes: 好 + 了 (change-of-state marker) = has become ready/done/okay. One of the most frequent two-syllable expressions in spoken Mandarin. Announces completion, signals readiness, and in reduplicated form (好了好了) means "alright, enough, okay."

A close friend, the most common way to mark closeness. 好 hǎo (good) stacks directly in front. For an even closer bond there is 知己 zhījǐ, "one who knows me," a soulmate-friend who truly understands you, a notion with deep roots in classical Chinese friendship.
好 hào (fond of) + 奇 qí (the strange, the unusual). Fond of the unusual , curious. 好奇心 hàoqíxīn = curiosity (the heart of fondness for strangeness).

Good things come in pairs: the principle that favors even numbers and pairing in gifts, decorations, and arrangements. Matched pairs of objects (candles, vases, figurines) are standard for weddings and auspicious occasions.
好 hǎo (good; well) + 听 (to listen). The auditory parallel of 好看 hǎokàn (nice-looking). Applied to music, voices, songs, and speech.

English: good brothers — polite euphemism for wandering hungry ghosts
Notes: 好 hǎo (good) + 兄弟 xiōngdì (brothers). The Taiwanese term of respect used in place of 鬼 during Ghost Month. Addressing spirits as "good brothers" acknowledges their presence without the provocation of calling them ghosts; it is also an appeal to fraternal feeling.

Notes: 喝 (drink) + 茶 (tea). 喝茶 also names the social ritual of sitting down together; "请喝茶" is both an offer of tea and an invitation to talk.
喝 (drink) + 酒 (liquor). The default verb for drinking alcohol of any kind, from beer to baijiu. Central to banquet culture, where 喝酒 carries social obligation.
喝 (drink) + 咖啡 (coffee). Like 喝茶, the phrase doubles as a soft social invitation: "改天一起喝咖啡" means let's meet up sometime.
喝 (drink) + 水 (water). The first sentence most learners build with this character, and the everyday reminder a Chinese host or parent will repeat constantly.
喝 (drink) + 完 (finished), another resultative: drink to completion, drain the glass. 完 marks the liquid as gone.
喝 (drink) + 醉 (drunk), a resultative compound: the 醉 is the result of the 喝. Often expanded to 喝醉了 (hē zuì le) for the completed state, "got drunk".

English: to merge; to combine; to amalgamate
Notes: 合 hé (to join) + 并 bìng (to combine side by side). To merge separate units into one: 两个部门合并了 "the two departments merged." Common in business, administration, and biology.

合 hé (to join, to combine) + 唱 chàng (to sing). Voices joined into one: a chorus, or the act of singing together. 合唱团 héchàngtuán is a choir. Contrast with 独唱 dúchàng, a solo, where one voice stands alone.

English: to merge into one; to unite into a single whole
Notes: 合 hé (to combine; to close) + 而 ér (and then; thereby) + 为 wéi (become) + 一. A classical four-character phrase describing the merging of separate things into wholeness. Used in philosophy, business mergers, artistic synthesis, and descriptions of cultural fusion.
合 hé (to fit; to accord with) + 法 fǎ (law). In accordance with the law, on the right side of the line: 合法权利 "lawful rights." Its opposite is 非法 fēifǎ (illegal) or 违法 wéifǎ (to break the law).

Notes: 合 hé (to accord with) + 理 lǐ (reason; principle). Something that accords with reason or fairness: 合理的价格 "a reasonable price," 合理安排 "a sensible arrangement." Its opposite is 不合理.

English: to close (a book, lid, door); to shut
Notes: 合 hé (to close) + 上 shàng (a result complement: shut to). To bring two edges together so a thing is closed: 合上书 "close the book," 合上盖子 "put the lid on."
合 hé (to fit) + 适 shì (to be apt). An adjective describing something that fits the situation well: 合适的工作 "a suitable job," 大小合适 "the right size." Its opposite is 不合适.
Contract. 签合同 (qiān hétong) is to sign one. The parties inside it, 甲方 and 乙方 (Party A and Party B), have become everyday slang for client and vendor.

Notes: 合 hé (to join) + 作 zuò (to do; to work). To join efforts and work as one. The everyday word for partnership of every scale, from two classmates to two nations: 合作伙伴 "a cooperation partner."

English: why must; there is no need to; why go so far?
Notes: 何 hé (why; what; how , the classical interrogative) + 必 bì (must; certainly). A rhetorical question that questions the necessity of an action, usually suggesting that the action is excessive, unnecessary, or misguided.

Notes: 河 (river) + 边 (biān, edge / side). The strip of ground along a river, where people walk, fish, and wash. One of the first place-words a beginner builds with 河.

Notes: 河 (river) + 流 (liú, to flow / a current). The generic technical term for a river as a flowing body of water, the word a geography textbook or a news report reaches for.
河 (river) + 水 (shuǐ, water). The water of a river as a substance, distinct from sea water 海水 (hǎishuǐ) or rain. Common in the proverb about minding your own affairs.

The Great Bend: the large northern loop of the Yellow River into Inner Mongolia. The fertile irrigated land within the bend has been farmed since antiquity and was historically a zone of contest between Han Chinese settlers and nomadic peoples of the steppe.

核 hé (nucleus; kernel; seed, as in 核武器 nuclear weapons) + 心 xīn (heart). The innermost, hardest, most essential center. Where 中心 is the geometric center, 核心 is the conceptual kernel, what everything else wraps around. Heavily used in political discourse, business strategy, and academic writing.

黑 hēi (black) + 暗 àn (dim; dark; unlit). Physical darkness, and by easy extension moral or social darkness: an age, a society, or a regime described as 黑暗 is corrupt and oppressive, a world where justice cannot be seen. 旧社会很黑暗 (the old society was full of darkness) is a stock phrase.

Notes: 黑 hēi (black) + 板 bǎn (board; plank). The classroom blackboard, a high-frequency HSK word and a useful anchor for the plain color sense.

English: dark tea & pu-erh — the other tea category prized for aging

Notes: 黑 hēi (black; illicit) + 客 kè (guest; visitor). The standard Chinese word for a hacker. It works on two levels at once: phonetically 黑客 echoes the English "hacker," and semantically it reads as "black guest," the uninvited intruder who enters a system in the dark.

黑 hēi (black; dark) + 马 mǎ (horse). A direct calque of the English "dark horse," now fully naturalized: a competitor nobody expected who surges from obscurity to win. Used constantly in sports, elections, business, and entertainment competitions.

黑 hēi + 色 sè (color). The neutral word for black as a color. Unlike its English counterpart, black in classical Chinese cosmology was not purely negative: in the 五行 (Five Phases) system, black is the color of Water, of the North, of winter, and of the kidneys, a respectable and necessary part of the…

English: the criminal underworld; organized crime; the mob
Notes: 黑 hēi (illicit) + 社会 shèhuì (society). Organized crime and the world it inhabits, the "black society" running parallel to and beneath the legitimate one.
黑 hēi (illicit; off the books) + 市 shì (market). A market operating outside legal channels, where goods or currency change hands at unofficial prices.

Tags: adjectives scale grammar measure-words classifiers nouns

English: many, a lot: plain and understated
Notes: 很多 is the everyday "many, a lot": 很多人 (many people), 很多问题 (many questions). 不少, literally "not few", says the same thing through understatement, and often carries a note of mild surprise: 他认识不少人 (he knows quite a few people).

English: to span across; to stretch across
Notes: 横 (héng, horizontal) + 跨. The verb of choice for bridges, viaducts, and any long structure that reaches from one side to the other. Also figurative for periods or regions: 横跨三个朝代 "spanning three dynasties," 横跨三大洲 "stretching across three continents."

Tags: color clarity symbolism daily-life culture life ritual

English: red envelope; a cash gift; a digital money packet
Notes: 红 hóng + 包 bāo (packet; bundle). The red paper envelope filled with money, given to children at New Year, to a couple at their wedding, and to employees as a bonus. The red is the point: the envelope blesses the money inside.

Notes: 红 hóng (red) + 茶 chá (tea). Fully oxidized tea, the category English calls black tea. The Chinese name describes the amber-red color of the infusion in the cup; the English name describes the near-black color of the oxidized leaf.

Notes: 红 (hóng, red) + 灯 (light): the red traffic signal that means stop. Here 灯 has shed every trace of flame and means pure colored signal. Its partner is 绿灯 (lǜdēng), the green light to go.

红 hóng (red; auspicious) + 火 huǒ (fire). A business, a celebration, or a neighborhood that is 红火 is booming, bustling, full of warmth and prosperity. The image fuses the lucky red with the energy of fire: a scene so lively it glows.

English: the Red Army; the early Chinese Communist military force
Notes: 红 hóng (red; revolutionary) + 军 jūn (army). The Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army, the Communist fighting force from 1927 until it was renamed in the late 1930s.

English: to blush; to flush red (with anger or embarrassment)
Notes: 红 (red) + 脸 (face). The cheeks going red, whether from shyness or from a flare of temper. 脸红 (liǎnhóng) reverses the order for the same blush; 红脸 also names the stern, blunt role someone plays in a good-cop bad-cop pairing.

红 hóng (red) + 绿 lǜ (green) + 灯 dēng (light; lamp). The everyday word for a traffic signal, built from its two decisive colors with red named first. 闯红灯 (chuǎng hóngdēng) is to run a red light, a common phrase that has also become a metaphor for breaking a rule that everyone agrees on.

English: a favored person; someone in favor with the powerful; a star
Notes: 红 hóng (popular; in favor) + 人 rén (person). Someone basking in favor, whether a boss's trusted lieutenant, a court favorite, or a rising celebrity. The metaphor runs straight from the color: to be 红 is to be celebrated, so a 红人 is a person bathed in that good fortune.

红 hóng + 色 sè (color). The neutral term for red as a color, but watch the second sense: 红色 also means "revolutionary" or "Communist" in political contexts. 红色旅游 (red tourism) is travel to revolutionary historical sites; 红色经典 (red classics) are the canonical works of revolutionary culture.

红 hóng (red) + 十字 shízì (cross). The International Committee of the Red Cross, established 1863. The Chinese translation renders the emblem directly: the red 十-shaped cross. The full institutional name is 红十字国际委员会 Hóng Shízì Guójì Wěiyuánhuì.

English: red thread of fate; also: a line that must not be crossed
Notes: 红 hóng (red , the color of luck, celebration, and vital force in Chinese culture) + 线 xiàn (thread; line). The red thread of fate in romantic mythology.

后 hòu (after; later) + 代 dài (generation). The generations that come after: 子孙后代 "children and grandchildren, all later generations." Used both for one's own line of descendants and, more broadly, for posterity as a whole.
Tags: generation history society characters ancestors ritual family

English: the rear; behind the front line
Notes: 后 (rear) + 方 (direction; side; region). The military and formal register word for the rear area behind a front line or forward position. Contrasted with 前方 qiánfāng (the front, the forward area). Also used metaphorically for the support structure behind any endeavor: family, logistics, home base.

English: the imperial harem; the rear palace
Notes: 后 (rear; and the empress sense) + 宫 (palace). The residential complex at the back of the imperial enclosure housing the emperor's wives and concubines. The term plays on both senses of 后: the rear palace (spatially, at the back) and the palace of the 后 (the empress and her female hierarchy).

后 (after) + 来 (to come; to arrive). "What came after" , subsequent events in a narrative or sequence. 后来 always refers to the past relative to a reference point already established: you set the scene, then 后来 picks up the story.
Tags: direction time royalty grammar logic cohesion meaning characters vocabulary conjunction timing communication

Notes: 后 (rear) + 门 (door; gate). Literally the door at the back of a building. Figuratively: an unofficial, informal, or improper channel for getting something done.

English: behind; at the back; in the rear
Notes: 后 (behind) + 面 (face; side; direction). The most common spatial word for "behind" in everyday Mandarin. Used for physical position relative to a reference point. Interchangeable with 后边 hòubian in many contexts; 后面 is slightly more formal.

后 hòu (after; later) + 世 shì (generation). The generations who come after us: 流芳后世 "to leave a good name to posterity," 后世子孙 "descendants of later generations." Looks forward to those who will inherit and remember.

后 hòu (after; behind; later) + 天 tiān (day). Chinese has dedicated words for two days in either direction of today: 前天 qiántiān / 昨天 zuótiān / 今天 jīntiān / 明天 míngtiān / 后天 hòutiān. Beyond that, you count: 三天后 sān tiān hòu (three days later).

English: to wait for a bus or train
Notes: 候 hòu (to wait) + 车 chē (vehicle). To wait for transport. Seen everywhere on station signage: 候车室 hòuchēshì "waiting room," 候车厅 "waiting hall."
候 hòu (season) + 鸟 niǎo (bird). The bird that moves with the season, contrasted with 留鸟 liúniǎo, the resident bird that stays year-round.

English: to wait to see a doctor
Notes: 候 hòu (to wait) + 诊 zhěn (to examine medically). To wait for a medical consultation. The room where patients sit is the 候诊室 hòuzhěnshì.
忽 hū (sudden, to neglect) + 然 rán (-ly). Marks an event arriving without warning: 忽然下雨 "it suddenly began to rain." Usually placed before the verb. Near-synonym of 突然.

English: Huzhou brush , brushes made in Huzhou, Zhejiang province, regarded as the finest in China. The term is used as a quality designation, much as "Huizhou ink" signals quality in the ink category. Huzhou brush-making has been a continuous craft tradition for over a thousand years.

Notes: 湖 (lake) plus 面 (surface): the open face of the water, the plane that mirrors sky and mountain.
湖 (lake) plus 南 (south): the province south of Dongting Lake, known for spicy cuisine and as Mao Zedong's birthplace.
湖 (lake) plus 畔 (pàn, bank, edge): the land at the water's rim, a literary word for a lakeshore walk or dwelling.
湖 (lake) plus 泊 (pō, a still pool). The pairing is the standard geographic term for lakes taken as a class, the word a textbook or atlas uses.
湖 (lake) plus 水 (water): the water of a lake itself, often invoked for its stillness and color.
互 hù (mutual) + 相 xiāng (each other). Placed before a verb, it says the action runs in both directions between two or more parties: 互相帮助 "to help each other," 互相理解 "to understand one another."
户 hù (door; household) + 外 wài (outside). Literally "outside the door," the open air beyond a building. Common in 户外运动 "outdoor sports" and 户外活动 "outdoor activities."

护 (protect, the 护 of 保护) + 士 (officer, the scholar-gentleman suffix of 战士 soldier and 博士 PhD). Coined when modern nursing arrived in the late Qing; the profession's day, 护士节, falls on Florence Nightingale's birthday, May 12.
花 huā (mixed-color) + 白 bái (white). Of hair or a beard, mixed black and white, grizzled: 花白的头发 "grizzled hair." The "many-colored" sense of 花 applied to the heads of the middle-aged.

Notes: 花 huā (flower) + 朵 duǒ (the measure word for blooms). A flower viewed as an individual blossom, slightly more literary than bare 花. Children are often called 祖国的花朵, "the flowers of the motherland."
花 huā (to spend) + 费 fèi (fee, to expend). A more formal word for spending, and also a noun meaning the expense itself: 生活花费 "living expenses." Heavier and more written than bare 花.

Sichuan pepper , the dried husk of the prickly ash berry, not related to black pepper or chili pepper. Contains hydroxy-alpha sanshool, which activates the same receptor as light touch and low-frequency vibration, producing the characteristic tingling numbness on the tongue and lips.

English: The decorated red sedan chair in which the bride was traditionally carried to the wedding. The chair was ornately painted and curtained, surrounded by musicians and attendants. The tradition has been revived in some contemporary weddings as a heritage element.

Notes: 花 huā (to spend) + 钱 qián (money). The basic verb-object phrase for spending money. Often split by an amount: 花了不少钱 "spent quite a lot of money," 花很多钱 "spend a lot."

English: to spend time; to take time
Notes: 花 huā (to spend) + 时间 shíjiān (time). To spend or take time on something. The same verb 花 covers time as well as money, where English needs a different word for each.
花 huā (patterned) + 样 yàng (shape, kind). A decorative pattern or a fancy variation, and by extension a trick or gimmick: 玩花样 "to play tricks," 花样滑冰 "figure skating."
花 huā (flower) + 园 yuán (garden, plot). A garden, a cultivated plot of flowers and plants. 植物园 zhíwùyuán is a botanical garden; 动物园 dòngwùyuán, a zoo, keeps the same 园.

Tags: language writing hanzi characters meta vocabulary daily-life colloquial

English: Huayan — the jewel-net philosophy of total interpenetration
Notes: Based on the 华严经 Huáyán Jīng (Avatamsaka Sutra), Huayan developed the most philosophically ambitious vision in Chinese Buddhism: the mutual interpenetration and non-obstruction of all phenomena.
滑 huá (to slide; slippery) + 雪 xuě (snow). To ski, literally "to slide on snow." The word covers downhill skiing and snowboarding alike in casual use.

English: To resolve a contradiction, a common phrase in management, diplomacy, and mediation contexts. 化解 (huàjiě) means to dissolve or resolve; 化 alone means to transform or change.
Notes: To resolve a contradiction, a common phrase in management, diplomacy, and mediation contexts. 化解 (huàjiě) means to dissolve or resolve; 化 alone means to transform or change.

English: to turn into; to become; to be reduced to
Notes: 化 huà (to transform) + 为 wéi (to be; to become), a literary verb of becoming. 化为 marks a complete turning of one thing into another, often dramatic and frequently with a sense of dissolution or loss.

English: transforming inborn nature and establishing the deliberately cultivated
Notes: 化 huà (transform) + 性 xìng (inborn nature) + 起 qǐ (establish, raise up) + 伪 wèi (deliberate cultivation). The Xunzian formula for what moral education accomplishes: it transforms what is innate and establishes in its place the cultivated.
Chemistry: transformation-study. 化学反应 is a chemical reaction; 化学式 (huàxuéshì) is a chemical formula, read left to right like grammar.
Tags: change culture science characters chemistry technology vocabulary translation biology nature life physics energy

Notes: Literally "to mark off an era," used as an adjective for something so significant it divides history into before and after: 划时代的发明 ("an epoch-making invention"). 划 (to mark, to divide) plus 时代. The strongest everyday word for a development that changes the age itself.
画 huà (to draw) + 画 huà (a picture). A verb-object pair, literally "to draw a drawing," the everyday way to say one is drawing or painting. The first 画 is the action, the second is what it produces.

画 huà (to paint; to draw; a painting) + 家 jiā. One who has made painting their home. The 家 suffix elevates the painter from a craftsperson to a master, implying sustained creative commitment and a body of work rather than mere technical skill.
Tags: arts calligraphy culture characters family society home

English: a scene; an image (on a screen or in a picture); a frame
Notes: 画 huà (picture) + 面 miàn (surface; face). The visible surface of a picture or screen: the framed image you see in a film, a photo, or a painting. 画面很美 "the image is beautiful."

English: Coming back to what we were saying or "on the other hand
Notes: Coming back to what we were saying or "on the other hand." Marks a return to a previous thread, often with a contrasting take. Useful for acknowledging a counterpoint to your own argument: "but coming back to it, you do have a point that…"
话 huà (speech; talk) + 题 tí (topic). What a conversation is about: 换个话题 "change the subject," 热门话题 "a hot topic." It frames the heading of talk rather than writing.
Tags: language communication spoken characters education meaning

English: nostalgia; to reminisce; longing for the past
Notes: 怀 (huái, to hold in the heart; to cherish , heart 忄+ 衣 clothing, the sense of something held close) + 旧 (old). Nostalgia as an emotional posture: the conscious holding of the past with affection.

Notes: Huaiyang cuisine: the specific tradition of the Yangzhou-Huai'an axis, considered the most technically refined of Chinese culinary traditions and the foundation of state banquet cooking.

Notes: 坏 (bad) + 处 (point, aspect). The disadvantage or harm of something, the standard counterpart to 好处 (hǎochu, benefit). Weighed up when deciding whether something is worth doing.
坏 (bad) + 蛋 (egg). A literal rotten egg, used figuratively for a scoundrel. Colloquial and elastic: a genuine insult when angry, a flirtatious tease between a couple when said with a smile.
坏 (to break down) + 了 (change-of-state particle). The everyday way to say a device or appliance has stopped working, or that food has gone off. Also a spoken exclamation: 坏了！ "Uh-oh, this is bad!"
坏 (bad) + 人 (person). The default word a child learns for the villain in a story or the stranger to avoid. Broad and moral, covering everyone from the cartoon antagonist to a genuine criminal.

English: to cheer; to hail with joy
Notes: 欢 huān (joy) + 呼 hū (to shout; to call). To shout for joy, the sound a crowd makes in celebration: 欢呼声 "cheers," 人们欢呼雀跃 "people cheered and jumped for joy."
欢 huān (joy) + 快 kuài (fast; quick). Joy with a quick, light tempo: a brisk and cheerful mood. Often said of music, rhythm, and movement: 欢快的旋律 "a lively melody," 欢快的舞步 "brisk, cheerful dance steps."
欢 huān (joy) + 乐 lè (happy; glad). Joy of the shared, festive kind: a celebration, a holiday, a crowd in good spirits. 欢乐的气氛 "a joyful atmosphere." More outward and communal than the quiet 高兴.
欢 (joyful) plus 送 (see off). To send someone off with celebration: a farewell party for a retiring colleague or a graduating class. The opposite number of 欢迎 (huānyíng), to welcome.
Tags: emotion culture characters feeling motion social daily-life

English: to be jubilant; to seethe with joy
Notes: 欢 huān (joy) + 腾 téng (to leap; to surge). A crowd boiling over with joy, leaping and shouting. Said of stadiums, squares, and whole towns at a great moment: 全场欢腾 "the whole place erupted in jubilation."
欢 huān (merry) + 喜 xǐ (glad). A warm, somewhat colloquial word for being happy and pleased, common in the south and in the phrase 欢欢喜喜 "all merry and glad," and in 皆大欢喜 "everyone happy."

欢 huān (joy) + 迎 yíng (to greet; to meet). To receive someone gladly. Also the set greeting 欢迎 "welcome!" and the shop sign 欢迎光临 "welcome, please come in." 受欢迎 shòu huānyíng means "popular; well-liked."

幻 huàn (illusion; phantom; to change; to vanish) + 想 xiǎng (thought; imagination). Thinking directed at what is illusory or impossible: fantasy, wishful thinking, daydreaming. Carries a mildly critical register , implies the thought has decoupled from reality.
换 (swap) + 班 (shift). To trade work shifts with a coworker, or for one shift to hand over to the next. The swap is of time slots rather than objects.
换 (swap) + 车 (vehicle). To get off one bus, train, or subway line and board another. The word every commuter says at an interchange station; 换乘 (huànchéng) is the signboard version.

English: Let's change the subject	Let's change the subject." Direct topic-change marker, used when the current thread has run its course or when you want to move on from something uncomfortable. Slightly more deliberate than 对了; signals an intentional shift rather than a stumble onto something new.

Literally swap a sentence and say it: 换 (swap) + 句话 (a sentence) + 说 (say). A fixed connective that restates a point another way, exactly like English "to put it differently."

Notes: 换 (swap) + 钱 (money). A verb-object pair for converting currency or breaking a large note into small ones. The default phrase at any bank counter or exchange window.
换 (swap) + 衣服 (clothes). The everyday house phrase: take off what you are wearing and put on something else. The same frame builds 换鞋 (change shoes) and 换床单 (change the sheets).

皇 huáng (august; emperor) + 后 (the commanding consort). The principal wife of a reigning emperor in the Chinese imperial system. A formal title with specific ritual privileges and a defined role in the imperial hierarchy.

The almanac: literally "yellow calendar," named for the imperial yellow of the official calendar. An annual publication (now also a mobile app feature) that gives day-by-day auspiciousness ratings based on the traditional calendrical system.

Notes: 黄 (huáng, yellow) + 牛, literally the yellow ox of the fields. In cities it became slang for a ticket scalper, from the way scalpers swarm and jostle like a milling herd.

The Loess Plateau: the wind-deposited silt plateau of northwestern China that gives the Yellow River its color and its sediment load. Covering approximately 640,000 km², it is one of the largest loess deposits on earth and the cradle of earliest Chinese agriculture.

English: Huizhou ink , ink sticks produced in the Huizhou region of Anhui province, regarded as the finest in China. Huizhou is also home to the She inkstone 歙砚 and Xuan paper, making Anhui province the geographic center of the Four Treasures tradition.

Notes: Huizhou merchants: the merchant class from the southern Anhui mountain region who dominated certain sectors of Chinese commerce (especially salt, timber, and pawnbroking) from the Song through the Qing dynasty.

Notes: 回 (huí, to return) plus 报 (to requite): to give back in kind. Used for repaying kindness and, in finance, for the return on an investment.

English: to answer; to reply; an answer
Notes: 回 huí (back) + 答 dá (to respond). To send a response back to a question: 回答问题 "to answer a question." As a noun, the answer itself: 一个满意的回答 "a satisfactory answer."

English: Coming back to what we were talking about	Coming back to what we were talking about." Returns to an earlier thread after a digression. Particularly useful in longer conversations where you want to close out a tangent and pick up the original point.
Notes: daily spoken language etiquette

English: to go home; to return home
Notes: 回 huí (to return) + 家 jiā (home). One of the most common V+location phrases in the language. The directional verb 回 indicates movement back toward an origin point: home as the natural destination of return, not merely a place you happen to go.

Notes: 回 huí (to return; to turn back) + 来 lái (toward here). To turn and come back toward the speaker's reference point, usually home, a shared location, or where you were before leaving. The counterpart is 回去 huíqù (to go back, returning away from the speaker).

English: To return a gift , to reciprocate with a gift of one's own
Notes: To return a gift , to reciprocate with a gift of one's own. 回礼 is expected and its absence is noticed. The return gift should be roughly equivalent in value to the original but need not be identical in kind. Returning a gift of equal or slightly higher value is considered courteous.

English: to turn one's head; later; to repent
Notes: 回 huí (turn back) + 头 tóu (head). To turn the head around, and by extension "in a little while" (回头见 "see you later") or to turn back from a wrong path (回头是岸 "to repent is to reach the shore").

English: to recall; to look back on; a memory
Notes: 回 huí (turn back) + 忆 yì (to remember). To turn the mind back to the past. As a noun, a remembered scene: 美好的回忆 "fond memories." The eddy here loops through time rather than space.

A factory that quotes in dollars but pays its costs in RMB carries the exchange risk and may ask to reprice when the rate moves. 汇率波动 (huìlǜ bōdòng) is fluctuation. Agree a reference rate, or a band within which the price stays fixed.

English: can speak Chinese — learned through study and practice
Notes: 会 indicates that a skill was acquired through learning, training, or practice. The speaker once did not have this ability and now does , through effort. This is the fundamental meaning: know how to.

Notes: 绘 huì (to depict) + 画 huà (to paint). A more formal word than 画画, naming painting as a discipline or art form: 绘画艺术 "the art of painting." Used in writing and in talk about fine art rather than casual sketching.

English: Huike — second patriarch; the arm in the snow
Notes: Huike (487–593 CE) is remembered for two things: the snow-and-arm story of his fierce aspiration, and the exchange above about the unfindable mind , which is itself a kōan on the non-existence of a substantial, locatable self.

English: Huineng — sixth patriarch; the Platform Sutra; Southern Chan
Notes: Huineng (638–713 CE) is the most historically consequential figure in Chinese Chan. An illiterate woodcutter from Guangdong, he achieved sudden recognition of his original nature upon hearing a line from the Diamond Sutra.

English: Huiyuan (334–416 CE) — Eastern Jin dynasty founder
Notes: Huiyuan is revered as the first patriarch of Chinese Pure Land Buddhism, though he did not use that term himself.

婚 hūn (marriage) + 礼 lǐ (rite; ceremony). Wedding as ritual. The 礼 suffix creates ceremony words for life's great transitions: 婚礼 wedding · 葬礼 zànglǐ funeral · 成人礼 chéngrénlǐ coming-of-age ceremony · 开幕礼 kāimùlǐ opening ceremony.

Notes: 婚 hūn (marriage, 女 woman + 昏 dusk, from the tradition of evening weddings) + 姻 yīn (marriage-alliance; matrimony, 女 woman + 因 cause/connection). The formal compound for marriage. 婚礼 hūnlǐ = wedding ceremony. 结婚 jiéhūn = to get married. 离婚 líhūn = to divorce.

English: activity; event; to move about; to exercise
Notes: 活 huó (lively) + 动 dòng (to move). As a noun, an organized activity or event; as a verb, to move one's body, to stretch and stir after sitting still. The lively-and-moving pair names anything that gets people up and going.

English: work; a job; a task; a piece of work
Notes: 活 huó (work) + the retroflex 儿 (ér) ending, typical of northern colloquial speech. The concrete job itself: the work to be done, often skilled handwork. A fine piece of craftsmanship is 好活儿 (good work).

Living Buddha , the Chinese term for a recognized reincarnation (tulku in Tibetan). Not precisely "Buddha" in the doctrinal sense but a lama whose successive rebirths are identified and confirmed by the tradition. The Dalai Lama and Panchen Lama are the most senior examples.

Notes: 活 huó (lively) + 泼 pō (to splash, itself a water word). A doubled water image, the splash of a living current, describing a bright, spirited, outgoing temperament. Most natural for children and young people: 活泼可爱 (lively and adorable).
活 huó = living, alive. Used in folk speech to describe a person of extraordinary virtue or generosity , a doctor who heals the poor without payment, a neighbor who gives without being asked.

活 huó (to live) + 着 zhe (the durative marker, an ongoing state). To be in the state of being alive, as opposed to 死了 (dead). Yú Huá's famous novel 《活着》 takes the word as its whole subject: simply going on living through everything.

火 huǒ + 车 chē (vehicle; cart). Named when steam locomotives first arrived in China , "fire-powered cart." The word has outlasted the steam era. 高铁 gāotiě (high-speed rail) is now preferred for bullet trains, but 火车 remains in universal use.

火 huǒ + 锅 guō (pot; wok). A simmering communal pot at the table , the quintessential Chinese social meal. 吃火锅 = to eat hotpot, one of the most common social dining activities. Regional varieties: 四川火锅 Sichuan hotpot (numbing-spicy 麻辣), 北京涮羊肉 Beijing lamb hotpot (clear broth).

English: the right heat and timing; (by extension) the right moment or level of skill
Notes: 火 huǒ (fire) + 候 hou (the timing of). In cooking, the exact control of heat and duration that makes or ruins a dish. Figuratively, the ripeness of a moment or the maturity of a skill: 火候到了 "the moment is ripe."

Notes: 火 huǒ (fire) + 山 shān (mountain). A fire-mountain. Strikingly direct. Related: 火山爆发 volcanic eruption · 活火山 active volcano · 死火山 extinct volcano · 休眠火山 dormant volcano.

The fire star twice over: the red planet of the five-phase planet names, and the everyday spark from a fire or a grinder's wheel. Internet slang added a third life: a 火星人 (Martian) is someone hopelessly behind on the news.
火 huǒ + 焰 yàn (flame , itself contains the fire radical 火). Used for actual flames and for intensity: 熊熊火焰 "roaring flames." Also in compound idioms: 火焰般的热情 "flame-like passion."

或 (perhaps; one possibility) + 者 (the said one; that case). Originally meaning "one possibility or the other," 或者 grammaticalized into a straightforward conjunction meaning "or." Notes: 货 huò (goods; commodity) + 物 wù (thing). Goods as freight or stock in trade, the things that move through commerce: 运送货物 "to transport goods," 货物清单 "a manifest of cargo."

Notes: A 乩童 (also written 乩手 jīshǒu or 乩身 jīshēn) is a human medium through whom a deity speaks and acts. During trance, the medium is said to be ridden by the god (神明附身 shénmíng fùshēn).

English: sharp spontaneous exchange — the master tests the student
Notes: 机 jī (opportunity; trigger) + 锋 fēng (blade; sharpness). The live Chan exchange: master and student meet in the present moment, and the master uses any available means , a question, a non-sequitur, a shout, a gesture , to test whether the student is genuinely awake or merely performing understanding…

English: quick-witted; resourceful; clever in the moment
Notes: 机 jī (opportunity; mechanism; key moment , originally a trigger mechanism on a crossbow, the precisely timed release point) + 智 zhì (intelligence; discernment). Wisdom that activates at the right moment: the quick intelligence that reads a situation instantly and responds with precision.
肌 (jī, muscle tissue) + 肉 (flesh). The fibrous flesh that moves the body; both characters carry the 月 flesh-radical.
鸡 (jī, chicken) + 蛋 (egg): the default egg in Chinese kitchens. When a recipe or menu just says egg, it means a hen's egg, so 鸡蛋 is one of the first nouns most learners cook with.
鸡 (chicken) + 肉 (ròu, meat). The flesh on the menu, as opposed to the live bird. Pair it with 牛肉 (niúròu, beef) and 猪肉 (zhūròu, pork) to name the everyday meats.

English: to accumulate virtue · good karma; meritorious deeds
Notes: 积善 jī shàn: 积 jī (to accumulate; to pile up over time) + 善 shàn. The idea that individual good acts deposit something durable in a person's character or fate , virtue as a slow savings account rather than a single decision.

English: basic; fundamental; (基本上) basically, on the whole
Notes: 基 jī (foundation) + 本 běn (root). The base layer of something: 基本功 jīběngōng (basic skills), 基本工资 (base salary). The adverb 基本上 jīběnshàng means "basically, by and large."

基本 jīběn (basic; fundamental) + 功 gōng (skill). The foundational skills of any discipline, the drills a beginner must master before anything else: scales for a musician, stances for a martial artist, strokes for a calligrapher.

Notes: Gene: sounds like the English, means "basic cause." 转基因 (zhuǎnjīyīn, transgenic/GMO) is the charged supermarket word built on it.

English: excited; agitated; stirred up; worked up
Notes: 激 jī (to rouse; to surge) + 动 dòng (to stir). A fast, strong emotional stirring, joy, anger, or agitation that one can barely sit still through: 太激动了 "so excited," 别激动 "calm down."

The usual way to join liner and shell at the mouth; 氩弧焊 (yàhúhàn, TIG welding) is the older method. 焊缝 (hànfèng) is the weld seam. A weld that is not fully sealed (焊不牢 or 虚焊 xūhàn, a false weld) lets air back in and the bottle loses its insulation weeks later.

English: to pass the imperial examination; to place in the rankings
Notes: 及 jí (to reach; to attain) + 第 dì (rank). To succeed in the civil-service exam and be placed in the official order. A historical and literary term; the modern equivalent is 考上 kǎoshàng (to test into).
及 (reach) + 格 (the standard grid): to reach the mark, customarily 60 out of 100. 不及格 is failing, and the near-miss score of 59 is proverbial for agony: 59分 is one point short of relief.

Auspicious, lucky, propitious , the standard term for something considered to bring good fortune. A number, date, phrase, or object that is 吉利 is sought after and displayed. Its opposite: 不吉利 (bù jílì), inauspicious.

English: extremely; utterly; in the highest degree
Notes: 极 jí (extreme; pole; utmost) + 其 qí (its; that). "Its extreme" , intensifier placing something at the outer limit of its property. More formal and emphatic than 非常 fēicháng or 很 hěn. Common in written evaluations, literary description, and critical prose.
急 (urgent) + 救 (jiù, to save). Saving in haste. The set term for first aid and emergency rescue: 急救箱 (jíjiùxiāng) is a first-aid kit, 急救车 (jíjiùchē) an ambulance.

Notes: 急 (urgent) + 忙 (máng, busy). An adverb of manner: doing something fast because time is short. It sits right before the verb to color the action with haste.
急 (impatient) + 性子 (xìngzi, temperament). Someone whose nature is to rush, who cannot stand waiting. The opposite is 慢性子 (mànxìngzi), an unhurried, easygoing type.

急 (urgent) + 诊 (zhěn, to diagnose). Emergency consultation. 急诊 is the hospital department you go to when something cannot wait, the Chinese counterpart of the emergency room. 看急诊 (kàn jízhěn) means to go to the ER.

Notes: 疾 (jí) and 病 are near-synonyms paired into one formal noun. In classical usage 疾 was the slight ailment and 病 the serious one; fused together, 疾病 is the neutral cover term for disease in medical and official language.

English: the truth of the origin of suffering — craving and clinging
Notes: 集 jí = accumulation, gathering. Sanskrit samudaya: arising. The cause of suffering is 贪爱 tān'ài (craving/clinging, also translated 渴爱 kě'ài, thirst): the driven, compulsive wanting and clinging to pleasant experiences, the desperate aversion to unpleasant ones, and the delusion of a fixed self that…
集 jí (to gather) + 体 tǐ (body). A gathered body of people acting as one: 集体活动 "a group activity," 集体主义 "collectivism." Set against the individual, 个人 gèrén.

English: collective wisdom; the shared intelligence of a group
Notes: 集体 jítǐ (collective; group; the body of people together) + 智慧. The wisdom that emerges from a group deliberating, pooling experience, and correcting one another , greater than any individual's 智慧 alone.

Asks about a small, countable number, typically under ten, and must be followed by a measure word: 几个 ("how many"), 几本 ("how many volumes"), 几位 ("how many people," polite). It assumes the answer is small, so it is the word for guests, family members, hours, or days.

Notes: Outside questions, 几 + measure word means "a few": 几个朋友 (a few friends), 几本书 (a few books), 前几天 (a few days ago). The same word asks "how many?" when the expected answer is small; the statement and question readings are told apart by context and intonation.
几 jǐ (how many; a few) + 个 ge. Either a question ("how many?") or a vague small number ("a few"), depending on context: 几个人 "how many people?" or "a few people."
Geometry. Classical Chinese for "how much?", repurposed by Xu Guangqi and Matteo Ricci in their 1607 translation of Euclid. Both senses live on: one in the classroom, one in Cao Cao's poetry.

己 jǐ (one's own) + 见 jiàn (view). The opinion that is distinctly one's own, valued for independence but cautioned against when it hardens into obstinacy. Lives in 固执己见, "to cling stubbornly to one's own view."

Notes: Cancellations, postponements, rejections, and suspensions are natural territory for 被. The subject (plan) is acted upon by an impersonal or unspecified authority. The adversative flavor is clear: the plan was ended by something outside its (or its creator's) control.
To calculate, to compute. The formal verb behind 计算机 (jìsuànjī, computer, "calculating machine") and 计算器 (jìsuànqì, calculator). Colloquial speech often just says 算 (suàn).
记 jì (to record) + 笔记 bǐjì (notes). The standard phrase for taking notes: in class, in a meeting, during a lecture. The verb-object construction: 上课要记笔记 (take notes in class).
记 jì (to keep in mind) + 得 de (a resultative marker). To have something still held in memory, the everyday word for remembering: 我记得他 "I remember him." Its opposite is 忘记 wàngjì (to forget).

English: a mark; a sign (made to remember by)
Notes: 记 jì (to mark) + 号 hào (sign, number). A mark made deliberately so you can find or recall a spot: 做记号 "to make a mark." Often a tick beside a line or a fold in a page.
记 jì (to write down) + 录 lù (to copy, to register). To set something down in writing, and the written result itself. Also the "record" that is broken in sport: 世界记录 "world record."

Notes: 记 jì (to remember) + 忆 yì (to recall, recollect). The faculty of memory and its contents, more formal and abstract than 记得: 童年的记忆 "childhood memories," 记忆力 jìyìlì "the power of memory."

Notes: 记 jì (to record) + 者 zhě (one who). Literally "one who records," the reporter whose work is to set down and report events: 新闻记者 "a news reporter."

English: to remember firmly; to commit to memory
Notes: 记 jì (to keep in mind) + 住 zhù (a resultative meaning "to stay fast"). To make something stick so it will not slip away: 记住这个号码 "memorize this number." The 住 stresses that the memory has caught and held.

Notes: 祭祖 (lit. "offering to ancestors") is the ritual presentation of food, incense, and goods to deceased family members. The offering table holds cooked dishes (often the ancestor's favorite foods in life), rice, fruit, and wine. Incense is lit and prostrations (拜 bài) are made.

English: Jixia Academy — the Warring States research university
Notes: Established by the state of Qi near its capital Linzi (临淄 Líncí) in the early 4th century BCE, operating for about a century. Scholars from all schools received state stipends and official titles without bureaucratic duties.

Notes: 加 jiā (to add; to increase) + 快 kuài (fast). Adding more speed to something already in motion. Common in official and news language for policy goals, construction schedules, and economic development; equally at home in everyday speech.
加 (jiā, to add) plus 热 (heat): to add heat, to warm something up. The verb on the microwave button and the recipe step.

English: in addition; plus; adding to this

Notes: 扫一扫 (sǎo yi sǎo) is "scan"; one person shows their QR code (二维码 èrwéimǎ), the other scans. 我扫你 means "I'll scan yours." 拉群 (lā qún) is to create a group chat, the norm for an order with several people on each side.
加油 (jiāyóu, to add fuel) + 站 (station): the place a car stops to refuel. Note that 加油 doubles as the cheer "let's go! keep it up!", literally "add oil," but here it is strictly the fuel sense.
To pick up with chopsticks: the specific verb for the gripping action of chopsticks. 夹菜 (jiā cài) is to pick up food from a shared dish.

English: To pick food for someone else , placing food from a shared dish into another person's bowl as a gesture of care and hospitality. The action is performed with chopsticks and directed toward honored guests, elders, or someone whose preferences you are attending to.

English: auspicious festival; festive holiday — literary register
Notes: 佳 jiā (excellent; fine; auspicious) + 节 jié (festival; season; node). A slightly elevated term for a holiday or festival occasion, preferred in literary and formal contexts over the more neutral 节日 (jiérì).

Notes: 佳 jiā (fine; good) + 音 yīn (word; news). The good news one hopes for, slightly formal in tone: 静候佳音 "to await good news quietly," a polite way to say you are hoping for a favorable reply.

家 jiā (home) + 常 cháng (ordinary; often; constant). The routine of domestic life: meals, small talk, everyday rhythms. A warmly neutral word that positions the homely and ordinary as valuable rather than inferior.

English: family tradition; values passed through generations
Notes: 家 jiā (family) + 风 fēng (wind; custom; style; ethos). The invisible ethos that blows through a family across generations: the unspoken values, behavioral norms, and character traits transmitted from parents to children.

家 jiā (family) + 规 guī (rules; regulations; norms). The explicit code of conduct of a household, the spoken version of what 家风 transmits implicitly. Distinguished families in imperial China often had written 家规 codifying expectations for children's conduct, study, and marriage.

English: family-country sentiment; patriotic feeling rooted in personal bonds
Notes: 家 (family) + 国 (country) + 情怀 qínghuái (feeling, sentiment, cherished aspiration). The emotional bond that flows from family love outward to love of country: the Confucian ladder enacted as feeling.

家 jiā + 人 rén (person/people). The people of the home. More intimate and emotionally warm than the formal compound 家庭成员 (family members, bureaucratic). 家人 feels like "my people": those who share your roof and your life.

Notes: Family; household. The nuclear unit of parents and children who share a home. 家庭作业 (jiātíng zuòyè, homework , lit. "family work") and 家庭医生 (jiātíng yīshēng, family doctor) show the compound in everyday use. The term carries a warmth and domesticity that the more formal 家族 lacks.

Notes: 家 jiā + 乡 xiāng (countryside; native place, the rural origin point). The place where 家 was first made. A place of origin rather than merely an address: family roots, ancestral connections, formative landscape. Central to Chinese identity, deeply tied to belonging and longing.

English: Clan; extended family network; lineage group sharing a surname. 家族企业 (jiāzú qǐyè) is a family business , often meaning a business controlled across generations by a single clan. The word implies shared ancestry, shared surname, and historically shared clan property and ancestral hall (祠堂 cítáng).

English: oracle bone script — the earliest Chinese writing
Notes: 甲 jiǎ (shell / armor) + 骨 gǔ (bone) + 文 wén (writing). Writing incised on turtle plastrons (腹甲 fùjiǎ) and ox scapulae (肩胛骨 jiānjiǎgǔ) used for royal divination during the Late Shang period. Over 4,000 distinct graphs have been identified; roughly 2,000 are deciphered.

Notes: 假 jiǎ (false; supposed) + 如 rú (suppose). A slightly more formal "if," at home with imagined or hypothetical cases: 假如我是你 "supposing I were you." Interchangeable with 如果 in most sentences.

Notes: 价 (price) + 格 (a fixed standard, a slot). The settled, stated price of a good, the figure printed on the tag or quoted by the seller. The everyday word for what something costs.
Tags: society social daily-life characters economy culture business commerce numbers vocabulary

Notes: 价 (price) + 值 (to be worth). The abstract worth of a thing, an act, or an idea, far beyond any market figure. Carries the moral and intellectual sense, as in 价值观 (jiàzhíguān), a set of values.

English: Dowry , the goods the bride's family sends with her to the new home. Traditionally included furniture, bedding, household items, and valuable objects. The dowry and betrothal gifts are understood as a two-way transfer that balances the exchange between families.

Notes: 兼 jiān (jointly; all together; simultaneously) + 爱 ài (love; care). The central Mohist doctrine: love that makes no distinction by relationship, proximity, or social standing. Contrasted directly with the Confucian 爱有差等 ài yǒu chā děng (love is graded by degree of relationship).

English: to reduce; to decrease; to diminish
Notes: 减 jiǎn (to subtract, to reduce) + 少 (few, less). To make less: to reduce a quantity, frequency, or intensity. 减少污染 (reduce pollution); 减少开支 (cut expenditure); 人数减少了 (the number of people decreased). The standard verb for any reduction in quantity.

English: abbreviated-character tablature — the guqin's notational system
Notes: 减 jiǎn (reduce; abbreviate) + 字 zì (character) + 谱 pǔ (notation; score). Developed in the Tang dynasty, used continuously since. Each composite character encodes string number, finger, position, and technique in a single glyph. Over 3,000 pieces survive in this notation.

From a lab, often for a named standard: LFGB, FDA, and the like are said as letters. 认证 (rènzhèng) is certification, 证书 (zhèngshū) the certificate. Check the report's date and which material it covers.
简 (pared down) + 便 (convenient). A method or procedure that is both simple and easy to use, with no fuss in the steps.
简 (brief) + 称 (to call, a name). The shortened form of a long name: 北大 for 北京大学, 联合国 from its full title. As a verb, to abbreviate something as.
简 (slip, hence pared down) + 单 (single, plain). The everyday word for simple, whether a task, an idea, or a person who is uncomplicated. Negated as 不简单 it flips to mean impressive, no small feat.

English: To put it simply or "in short
Notes: To put it simply or "in short." Introduces a condensed version of a longer explanation. Useful when you have been speaking at length and want to summarize the core point.
简 (pared down) + 短 (short). Brief in the sense of few words: a brief speech, a brief reply, a brief note. The narrow slip rendered literal as length.

简 (simple) + 化 (the -ize / -ify suffix, to turn into). To make a process, a procedure, or a script simpler. The very term 简体字 (jiǎntǐzì), simplified characters, is the product of this verb applied to writing itself.
简 (brief) + 介 (to introduce). The short blurb that sums up a book, a company, a film, or a person. The about-line under a profile is a 简介.
简 (brief) + 历 (one's history, experience). A condensed record of your schooling and work, the document you send with a job application. Literally a brief life-history.

简 jiǎn (simple; brief; bamboo slip, an early writing surface) + 体 tǐ (form; style) + 字 zì. Introduced in mainland China in the 1950s–1960s under the People's Republic, with the goal of increasing literacy rates.

Notes: 简 (plainly) + 直 (straight, directly). An adverb of emphasis: put plainly and directly, it amounts to. Used to push a statement to its extreme, often with a touch of exasperation or wonder.
Tags: writing communication characters intensifier even emphasis

English: see a ghost! — absurd! ridiculous! what the hell!
Notes: 见 jiàn (to see; to encounter) + 鬼 guǐ (ghost). Literally "see a ghost!" — used as an exclamation of disbelief, exasperation, or dismissal of something absurd. Equivalent to "what the hell!" or "that makes no sense!" Does not carry strong profanity weight.
Tags: folk-religion religion culture classical symbolism ancestors

English: to meet; to see one another (in person)
Notes: 见 jiàn (to see) + 面 miàn (face). Literally "to see faces," the everyday verb for meeting someone in person. It is a separable verb: 见了一面 "met once," 见过面 "have met before."
Tags: perception knowing daily-life society space food grammar syntax spoken

Notes: 建 jiàn (to build, to establish) + 国 (country, state). The founding of a state. 建国以来 (since the founding of the country) is a common phrase that, depending on speaker, refers to 1912 (Republic) or 1949 (People's Republic). 国庆节 (National Day, October 1) marks the 1949 建国.
Architecture, building. 建筑师 (jiànzhùshī) is an architect, distinct from the 工程师 who makes the building stand up. As a verb, 建 alone means to build: 建一座桥, build a bridge.

健 (robust) + 康 (well, at ease). The formal health word: 健康码 was the pandemic-era health code, 健康证 the food-worker's health certificate, and 亚健康 ("sub-health") the popular term for run-down-but-not-sick, a category Chinese wellness culture takes seriously.
Tags: health body tcm characters meaning daily-life vocabulary

Notes: 健 (strengthen) + 身 (body). The gym era's verb: 健身房 is the gym, 健身教练 the personal trainer. The park's older exercise culture keeps its own verb, 锻炼, so the generations can be told apart by which word they use.

Originally specifically the Yangtze River (长江 Chángjiāng , the Long River), which is so dominant in Chinese geography that 江 alone referred to it. Over time 江 generalized to any large river, while smaller rivers typically use 河 hé.

Notes: North of the Yangtze. In local usage, particularly in Nanjing and Shanghai, this refers to the area immediately north of the river, considered rougher and less cosmopolitan than Jiangnan. A mild regional insult in some contexts.

English: the debts and vendettas of the martial world; the cycle of obligation and revenge
Notes: 江湖 + 恩 ēn (grace; debt of kindness) + 怨 yuàn (grievance; resentment). The engine of wuxia narratives: every favor creates an obligation, every wrong creates a grievance. The 江湖 keeps score across generations , a debt unpaid by the father falls to the son.

English: a person of the rivers-and-lakes world; someone who lives by the code
Notes: The person defined by their membership in the 江湖 , not just someone who passes through it, but someone whose identity is constituted by it. 江湖人 abide by a parallel moral code: loyalty to sworn brothers (义气 yìqi), repayment of debts and favors, the obligation to right wrongs.

English: south of the Yangtze; the culturally and economically rich lower Yangtze region
Notes: 江 jiāng (the Yangtze) + 南 nán (south). The region south of the Yangtze , centred on present-day Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Shanghai , is the most romanticized landscape in classical Chinese poetry. 江南 means silk, canals, spring rain, white walls, and scholar gardens.

English: Jiang Qing, Mao's wife, Gang of Four leader
every generation of rivers and mountains produces its talented people; each era brings forth its own greatness
Notes: From Zhao Yi's (赵翼) 18th-century poem 论诗 (On Poetry): 江山代有才人出，各领风骚数百年 (every generation of rivers and mountains produces its talented people; each holds sway for hundreds of years).

English: the future; in the future; what is coming
Notes: 将 jiāng (about to; will; the near future) + 来 lái (coming; arriving). What is about to arrive, the future approaching. 将来 refers to the general future (not an immediate event). Slightly more formal than 以后 yǐhòu. Contrast: 未来 wèilái (the future, lit.
Tags: direction motion grammar time modern perception characters tense aspect

English: to speak; to explain; to lecture
to mind one's manners; to be attentive to politeness
Notes: 讲 jiǎng (to attend to; to value; to make a point of) + 礼貌. The active form: not just having manners but consciously practicing them. Common in parental instruction and educational contexts. 讲礼貌 is what 有礼貌 looks like as a discipline rather than a state.

English: to be civilized; to behave with proper manners
Notes: The everyday descendant of the classical sense, deployed across public-conduct campaigns. Bus stops, parks, and tourist sites carry signs urging citizens to 讲文明 (be civilized) and 讲礼貌 (be polite).

English: to descend; to lower; to fall
to reduce; to lower; to bring down
Notes: 降 jiàng (to descend, to lower , as in altitude, rank, or intensity) + 低 (low). The standard transitive verb for reducing a measurable value: 降低价格 (lower the price); 降低风险 (reduce the risk); 降低标准 (lower the standard).

English: to cut the price, mark down
Notes: 降 (to lower) + 价 (price). To bring a price down, to discount. Its opposite is 涨价 (zhǎngjià), to raise the price. Both are verb-object compounds, so an amount can split them: 降了价.

English: to land; to descend (aircraft); to come down
Notes: 降 jiàng (to descend, to lower) + 落 luò (to land). The standard word for an aircraft landing. Also used for anything descending to earth: 降落伞 jiànglùosǎn = parachute.
Tags: nature motion characters movement space settlement

Notes: 交 jiāo (to cross) + 错 cuò (crosswise). The original "crossing" sense, with no fault implied: lines, paths, or branches weaving across one another. 纵横交错 describes a network running every which way.
交 (mutual) + 换 (swap). A two-way exchange where both sides hand something over: gifts, contact details, opinions, prisoners. More formal and reciprocal than a plain 换.

English: cross-collar wrapping right-over-left — the defining feature of hànfú

Notes: A verb-object phrase: 交 jiāo (to associate with, to form bonds) + 朋友. To make a single friend is 交个朋友 (with 个 splitting the phrase). The same 交 appears in 交流 (to exchange, communicate) and 社交 (social interaction), all built on the sense of mutual exchange.

Notes: Also 货期 (huòqī). Ask when the clock starts: from deposit received, from sample approval, or from materials arriving. 延期 (yánqī) is a delay; 赶货 (gǎnhuò) is rushing an order.

Notes: 交 jiāo (to cross; to exchange; mutual) + 通 (to go through; to connect). The crossing-and-passing of people and vehicles: the whole system of movement through a place. 交通 covers traffic in the everyday sense (交通堵塞, a traffic jam) and transport as a category (交通工具, means of transport).
交通 (jiāotōng, traffic) + 灯 (light): the three-color signal at an intersection. Also called 红绿灯 (hónglǜdēng), literally the red-green light.

English: noodle topping; the garnish that makes the bowl
arrogant; proud (positive or negative depending on context)
Notes: 骄 jiāo (arrogant; a rearing horse , the original pictograph showed an unruly horse rearing up on its hind legs) + 傲 ào (proud; disdainful; lofty). The primary antonym of 谦虚. In moral discourse, always negative , 骄傲是谦虚的对立面 (arrogance is the opposite of humility).

角 jiǎo (corner) + 落 luò (to settle, to land). The place where things come to rest in the corner, a nook. Both literally (a room's corner) and figuratively (a quiet, tucked-away place in the world). The name of this site: 角落書屋.

Tags: space geometry music culture arts history

English: dumplings — the northern New Year food
Notes: The quintessential northern Chinese New Year food, eaten at midnight on New Year's Eve in many northern households. The shape resembles the 元宝 yuánbǎo (ancient sycee gold ingots), making them symbols of wealth.
Tags: food culture geography history confucianism daily-life family tcm cosmology

Notes: Dumpling wrapper, literally "dumpling skin." Sold pre-made in supermarkets, but making them by hand is considered superior.

脚 jiǎo + 本 běn (root; book; basis). The script for a play, film, or shoot , and, in the modern technical vocabulary, a programming script (a JavaScript file is a JS 脚本). The 脚 here gestures at the foundational text that the performance or program is built on.

脚 jiǎo + 步 bù (step). Both the literal sound of footsteps and the figurative pace of progress. 听见脚步声 "to hear footsteps"; 加快脚步 "to quicken one's pace"; 跟上时代的脚步 "to keep up with the pace of the times."

English: underfoot; right beneath one; (also) at the present moment
Notes: 脚 jiǎo + 下 xià (below). Literally under the foot , the immediate ground one is standing on. By extension, "right here, right now," especially in the older expression 脚下 used for the immediate present.

English: footprint; the mark of a foot
Notes: 脚 jiǎo + 印 yìn (mark; seal; print). Both the literal print of a foot in mud or snow, and the figurative traces someone has left behind: 留下脚印 "to leave footprints" can describe an explorer's path or a person's life-marks.

脚 jiǎo + 趾 zhǐ (toe; finger of the foot). The standard word for toe. Note the partner term: 手指 shǒuzhǐ "finger" (literally "hand-finger") , Chinese carefully distinguishes hand-fingers from foot-fingers.

Tags: syntax object disposal passive agent grammar spoken

English: to be a stickler; to take something too seriously
Notes: 较 jiào (to compare; to dispute) + 真. To insist on getting the real, exact, literal version of something , usually said with mild disapproval. The cousin of 认真 with the dial turned past serviceable into pedantic.
Tags: knowing daoism philosophy virtue ethics daily-life

Notes: 教 (to teach) + 练 (to drill). The one who teaches by drilling: a sports coach, a driving instructor, a fitness trainer.
教 jiào (to teach) + 师 shī (master; expert). The formal word for a teacher as a profession, common in writing and titles. In direct address the warmer 老师 lǎoshī is used instead.
教 jiào (to teach) + 室 shì (room). The room where teaching happens. Watch the tone of 室 (shì), and do not confuse it with 教师 jiàoshī (teacher); the two words differ only in the second syllable.

English: to teach (as a profession); to be a teacher
Notes: 教 jiāo (to teach) + 书 shū (books). Literally "to teach books," the standard way to say one teaches for a living. Note the first-tone jiāo here, the colloquial verb reading.
教 jiào (religion) + 堂 táng (hall). The hall of worship, a church building. The community of believers, by contrast, is 教会 jiàohuì.

English: a lesson (learned the hard way); to reprimand
Notes: 教 jiào (to teach) + 训 xùn (to admonish). As a noun, the lesson drawn from a mistake or setback: 吸取教训 "to learn the lesson." As a verb, to scold or take someone to task.

教 jiào (to teach) + 育 yù (to raise; to nurture). The whole enterprise of teaching and bringing up, as both a noun and a verb: 高等教育 "higher education," 教育孩子 "to bring up a child." This is the formal jiào reading.

The fermentation pit: the earthen or stone pit in which the fermented grain mash (酒醅 jiǔpēi) undergoes anaerobic fermentation. Old pits with established microbial ecosystems are considered the most valuable assets of a distillery.

Staircase price: the unit price falls as quantity rises. Asking for a tier table is the cleanest way to learn the factory's real cost curve, and it moves the conversation from "lower the price" to "at what quantity."

English: to come into contact, to engage with
Notes: 接 (to touch) + 触 (chù, to make contact). Two surfaces meet, or two people start dealing with each other. Used for physical contact and for first encounters with ideas, fields, or strangers.
接 (receive) + 电话 (diànhuà, phone call). To take up a ringing call and connect the line. The hand that closes the gap now closes a circuit.

English: to approach; to be close to; to approximate
Notes: 接 jiē (to connect; to receive; to meet) + 近 (near). To connect by closing the gap , a more formal and abstract verb than 靠近.

English: one after another; in succession; repeatedly
Notes: 接 jiē (to join; to connect) + 连 lián (in a series). An adverb meaning that events occur in close, repeated succession, each new one arriving before the last has finished registering. Often reinforced as 接连不断 (continuously, without a break).

English: to pick someone up, to meet someone
Notes: 接 (to meet) + 人 (rén, person). To go to a station, airport, or door and collect a person who is arriving. The everyday counterpart to ceremonial 迎接.
接 (receive) + 受 (shòu, to be given). The hand takes what is offered and keeps it. Used for offers, opinions, criticism, conditions, anything you take in and agree to.
A clear, polite refusal. Stronger than 有点难, softer than 不行. Pair it with the reason and what you could accept.
接 (join) + 着 (zhe, continuing aspect). One action takes the baton from the one before it. Use it to mean "and then, right after that," or "go on (doing something)."

Notes: The opening of the closing mantra. Even taken out of liturgical context, these lines carry a strong recognizable rhythm in Chinese Buddhist culture; readers and listeners hear the rest of the mantra by implication when these first phrases sound.
