Notes: 街 (street) + 道 (road, way). The everyday word for a city street. In administrative use it also names the smallest urban division, the 街道办事处 (jiēdào bànshìchù), a neighborhood subdistrict office.
街 (street) + 坊 (a city ward). The people who share your street, your neighbors in the old close-knit sense. 街坊邻居 (jiēfang línjū) is the warm collective phrase for the whole neighborhood.
街 jiē (street) + 角 jiǎo (corner). The physical corner where two streets meet. In narrative, the street corner is a classic site of waiting, meeting, and chance encounter.
街 (street) + 区 (district, zone). A block or built-up quarter bounded by streets. Common in urban planning and real-estate talk: 商业街区 (shāngyè jiēqū) a commercial district.
街 (street) + 头 (head, end). The mouth of a street or the streetside in general. It frames public, open-air activity: 街头艺人 (jiētóu yìrén) a street performer, 街头篮球 (jiētóu lánqiú) streetball.
Tags: settlement daily-life society characters body space meaning

English: critical juncture; the pivot point of a situation
Notes: 节 jié (joint) + 骨 gǔ (bone) + 眼. The eye at the joint of the bone , the precise small spot at which a thing turns. Colloquial; almost always paired with 上 in 节骨眼上 "at the critical juncture."

节 (jié, section; festival; segment) + 目 (item). A listed performance item or broadcast segment. 电视节目 (TV program); 春节联欢晚会节目 (Spring Festival Gala items). The word traveled from variety show programs into streaming, where 综艺节目 means a variety program and 节目单 is a program schedule.

节 jié (node; joint; festival) + 日 rì (day). The standard word for a festival or public holiday. 传统节日 chuántǒng jiérì = traditional holiday (Spring Festival, Mid-Autumn, Dragon Boat). 法定节假日 fǎdìng jiàjià rì = statutory public holiday. 情人节 Qíngrén Jié = Valentine's Day (lit. "lover's day").
Tags: festival calendar daily-life characters culture history cosmology food

Notes: A short greeting at Chinese New Year and the Mid-Autumn Festival maintains the relationship between orders. 新年快乐 or 中秋快乐 with a line of thanks is enough.

English: to save; to cut down on; to use sparingly
Notes: 节 jié (restrain) + 省 shěng (to economize; to spare). To save money, time, or effort by using less of it: 节省时间 "save time," 节省开支 "cut expenses." The hands-on, daily-budget cousin of 节约.

Mozi condemned extravagant funerals, elaborate music, and luxury consumption on utilitarian grounds: if a practice does not benefit the people, enrich the state, and increase the population, it is harmful. His critique of Confucian ritual was direct and sustained.
Tags: mohism universal-love philosophy history classical ethics virtue confucianism statecraft ancient

Notes: 节 jié (restrain) + 约 yuē (to bind; to limit). To hold consumption within bounds, especially of shared or large-scale resources: 节约用水 "conserve water," 节约能源 "conserve energy." The word of public campaigns and stated principle.

English: simple burial; against elaborate funerary practice
Notes: Three inches of wood for the coffin; three garments for the body; no grave mound. 节葬 is the direct application of 节用 to death. It was a pointed attack on the bronze-vessel burial culture of Mozi's era , the practice of entombing rulers with vast quantities of ritual bronzes, servants, and goods.
Tags: mohism universal-love philosophy history classical ethics virtue confucianism statecraft ancient

English: to restrain; to be moderate; temperance
Notes: 节 jié (restrain) + 制 zhì (to control). To hold one's appetites or conduct within limits: 饮食节制 "moderation in eating and drinking." The inward, moral side of 节, keeping a thing from running past its proper bound.
结 jié (to conclude) + 果 guǒ (fruit; result). The outcome a process ties off into. Also a connective: "as it turned out." Read this way it is jiéguǒ; the verb "to bear fruit" reads jiē guǒ instead.
Tags: connections meaning society characters logic cohesion

English: to combine; to integrate; to unite
Notes: 结 jié (to tie) + 合 hé (to join). To bring two things together so they work as one: 理论与实践结合 "to combine theory with practice." Abstract and constructive, used of ideas, methods, and elements, not of physical knots.

结 jié (to tie) + 婚 hūn (marriage). To tie the marriage bond, the standard word for getting married. A separable verb: 结过婚 "have been married," 结了婚 "got married." Its opposite is 离婚 líhūn (to divorce).
Tags: connections meaning society characters grammar syntax spoken

Notes: 结 jié (to tie, to knot, to conclude) + 论. The conclusion that an argument or investigation arrives at: the point where reasoning is tied off. 下结论 xià jiélùn "to draw a conclusion," 得出结论 déchū jiélùn "to reach a conclusion."
Tags: connections meaning society characters communication rhetoric language

English: to settle in full: to pay off
sturdy; durable; (of a body) strong and solid
Notes: 结 jiē (to bear fruit; to form) + 实 shi (solid). Built to last, not flimsy: 这张桌子很结实 "this table is very sturdy." Of a person it means strongly built: 身体结实 "physically robust." Note the toneless reading jiēshi here, distinct from 结 jié elsewhere.
Tags: connections meaning society characters evaluation quality

English: to end; to finish; to conclude
Notes: 结 jié (to tie off) + 束 shù (to bind; a bundle). To bring an event or period to its close: 会议结束了 "the meeting is over." Its opposite is 开始 kāishǐ (to begin).
Tags: connections meaning society characters change motion daily-life grammar language

English: to form a karmic bond; to connect; to begin a meaningful relationship
Notes: 结 jié (to tie; to form; to knot) + 缘. To tie a karmic thread , to form a connection that carries the weight of 缘分.
姐 (elder sister) plus 夫 (husband) names the man married to one's older sister. Chinese kinship marks the relation precisely, distinct from 妹夫 (mèifu), a younger sister's husband.
The doubled character is the everyday word for one's older sister. The second 姐 takes a neutral tone, giving the warm, soft cadence Chinese kinship terms favor.
姐 (elder sister) plus 妹 (younger sister) yokes the two into a single word for "sisters" as a pair or group, and by extension a tight circle of close female friends.

English: to remove; to lift; to terminate (a state or obligation)
Notes: 解 jiě + 除 chú (to remove; to do away with). To untie and clear away. Used for lifting a binding state or formal tie: 解除警报 = lift an alert; 解除合同 = terminate a contract; 解除武装 = disarm; 解除疲劳 = relieve fatigue. More formal than 解开, it dissolves an arrangement or condition rather than a physical knot.

English: to answer; to solve and explain; a solution
Notes: 解 jiě + 答 dá (to answer; to reply). To unravel and answer. Used for working out and explaining the answer to a question or problem, especially in study: 解答疑问 = answer a question; 标准解答 = the standard solution.

English: to interpret; to construe; to make sense of
Notes: 解 jiě (to untie; to dissolve; to explain) + 读. The standard verb for interpretive reading , of a text, a result, a signal, a person's behaviour. Where 阅读 is comprehending what is plainly there, 解读 is going after what is implicit.

解 jiě + 放 fàng (to release; to set free). To untie and let go. The standard word for liberating people from bondage, oppression, or restraint: 解放思想 = free up one's thinking; 解放双手 = free one's hands (from drudgery).

English: to unseal; to lift a lockdown

Notes: 解 jiě + 雇 gù (to hire; to employ). To undo the hiring. The formal word for dismissing someone from a job, the legal counterpart to the colloquial 炒鱿鱼 chǎo yóuyú (lit. stir-fry the squid). 解雇 separates the worker from the employment tie, the same "undoing a bind" logic applied to a contract of work.

English: to solve; to resolve; to settle
Notes: 解 jiě + 决 jué (to decide; to settle). To undo and settle. The all-purpose verb for solving a problem or settling a matter: 解决问题 = solve a problem; 解决困难 = overcome a difficulty; 想办法解决 = find a way to settle it.
Tags: knowing meaning communication characters vocabulary daily-life evaluation

English: to untie; to undo; to unfasten
Notes: 解 jiě + 开 kāi (to open). The most literal 解-word: to untie a knot, undo a button, unfasten a rope. By extension it covers loosening any bind, even a metaphorical one: 解开心结 = untie the knot in one's heart, resolve an inner tension. The picture of separating the bound thing is right on the surface.
解 jiě + 渴 kě (thirst; thirsty). To undo thirst. The everyday verb-object phrase for slaking thirst: 喝水解渴 = drink water to quench thirst; 西瓜很解渴 = watermelon is very thirst-quenching.

English: to explain; to interpret; an explanation
Notes: 解 jiě + 释 shì (to release; to elucidate). To open a thing up and let its sense out. The everyday word for explaining: 解释原因 = explain the reason; 做出解释 = give an explanation. It also covers defending oneself: 解释误会 = clear up a misunderstanding. Where 解决 settles a problem, 解释 makes a meaning plain.
Tags: knowing meaning communication characters language rhetoric

English: liberation; release; to be freed from bondage or constraint
Notes: 解 jiě (to untie; to release; to dissolve) + 脱 tuō (to escape; to shed; to free oneself from). In Buddhist context: liberation from 轮回, the shedding of karmic bondage and conditioned existence.
Tags: buddhism religion philosophy cosmology classical fate life

English: interface; the surface between two systems
Notes: 界 (boundary; boundary marker) + 面 (surface; face). The surface at the boundary between two things. In technology and computing: the user interface (用户界面 yònghù jièmiàn), screen interface. In science: the interface between two phases or systems.
借 (lend) + 给 (give to). Pinning 给 after 借 fixes the direction outward: the subject is the one handing the object over.

English: to learn from, draw on as a model
Notes: 借 (to borrow) + 鉴 (mirror, to reflect on). To borrow another's experience as a mirror for your own, taking what is useful from a model or precedent.
借 (to borrow) + 口 (mouth). A "borrowed mouth," words you reach for that are not the true reason. As a noun it is the excuse itself; as a verb, "to use as a pretext."
借 (borrow/lend) + 钱 (money). A verb-object pair whose direction depends on the prepositions around it: 向他借钱 is borrowing from him, 借钱给他 is lending to him.

English: to draw on, with the help of
Notes: 借 (to make use of) + 助 (aid). To accomplish something by leaning on an external tool, force, or person. Formal register, common in writing.

English: this life; the present life; this age
Notes: 今 jīn (present; now) + 世 shì (life; age). The life one is living now, set against 前世 (a former life) and 来世 (the next): 今生今世 "this very life." Can also mean the present age in a more general sense.

今 jīn (now; the present moment) + 天 tiān (day). The word for "today" encodes "the now-day." Chinese time words are nouns that typically occupy the topic position at the start of a sentence, before the verb; they work differently from English adverbs like "today."

English: today I mainly want to discuss
Notes: Sets the agenda. Saying it early, with numbered points, is the strongest move a visitor has: it decides what gets talked about and in what order. Follow with 第一 (dì-yī), 第二, 第三, and close each topic with 这个先到这里 ("let's leave this one here for now").
The market half-kilo. 一斤多少钱 ("how much per jin?") is the essential market question. Originally a pictograph of an axe, which is still its job as a radical.
Tags: language grammar daily-life scale trade history numbers

English: weight; one's true worth or standing
Notes: 斤 jīn (catty) + 两 liǎng (tael), the two traditional units of weight, hence "weight" in general, and figuratively a person's substance or worth. 掂量掂量自己的斤两 (to weigh up one's own worth) means to take an honest measure of what one can really do.

English: the Diamond Sutra; the foundational text of Chan Buddhism
Notes: The full title is 金刚般若波罗蜜经 (Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng), the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sutra. The diamond image is the cutting power of 般若 that severs every clinging.

Notes: 金 jīn (gold) + 钱 qián (coin; money). A slightly elevated or literary term for money. Used in formal writing and in philosophical contexts: 金钱不是万能的 "Money is not omnipotent." Compare: 钱 (everyday "money"), 金钱 (money as an abstraction or moral question), 财富 cáifù (wealth/riches).

Epigraphy: the study of inscriptions on bronze and stone. The scholarly discipline that underlies serious seal carving: to carve seal script well, one must have studied the ancient bronzes and stone inscriptions from which the script derives.

English: to do one's utmost; to try one's best
Notes: 尽 jìn (to exhaust; to the limit) + 力 lì (effort). To use up all the effort one has, to spare nothing: 我会尽力 "I will do my best," 尽力而为 "do all one can."

English: the end; the very end; the limit
Notes: 尽 jìn (to exhaust, to use up) + 头 tóu (end). The point where a thing runs out: the far end of a road, the limit of a stretch. 路的尽头 "the end of the road."
紧 (close, tight) + 跟 (gēn, to follow). To follow with no gap. Physical (stay right behind) or figurative (紧跟时代, keep pace with the times).

紧 (pressing) + 急 (jí, hurried, anxious). Two words for urgency stacked together, intensifying each other. The register of sirens, evacuations, and red-banner notices: 紧急出口 (emergency exit), 紧急情况 (emergency situation).
The doubled form intensifies the grip. 紧紧 describes an action done with full, unrelenting tightness, often a hold or an embrace that won't let go.
紧 (taut) + 张 (zhāng, to stretch open). A surface pulled tight from both ends. Used for nerves before an exam, the tension in a thriller, and resources stretched thin (时间紧张, time is short).

Notes: 近 jìn (near; close; recent) + 来 lái (coming; approaching the present). "What has come near," the recent past approaching the present. A slightly more formal or literary synonym of 最近 zuìjìn. Common in formal speech, writing, and news contexts.

English: in recent years; over recent years
Notes: 近 (recent) + 年 (year) + 来 (coming from , a directional particle marking elapsed duration). Time that has been coming toward the present moment across recent years. A standard phrase in news, academic writing, and formal speech: 近年来，中国的城市化速度加快 (in recent years, China's urbanization has accelerated).

English: in the near future; recently; in the near term
Notes: 近 (near) + 期 qī (a period of time; a term; a scheduled point). A time period that is near , used for both the recent past and the near future depending on context. 近期内 (within the near term); 近期计划 (near-term plans). The period implied is typically weeks to a few months, not years.
近 (near) + 视 shì (to see; vision). Seeing only what is near , the clinical and colloquial term for myopia. 近视眼镜 (myopia glasses , corrective lenses); 高度近视 (high myopia, severe nearsightedness).
进 jìn (to advance) + 步 bù (a step). To move forward step by step, hence to improve. Works as a verb (你进步了 "you've improved") and as a noun (很大的进步 "great progress").

English: to go into town; to go to the city
Notes: 进 jìn (to enter) + 城 chéng (city; town). A verb-object phrase: to go into the city. The expression preserves the old sense of the city as a bounded place one literally enters, crossing from outside to inside.
跟进 (gēnjìn) is to follow up, 催 (cuī) to chase. Ask for photos as well as words; a picture of goods on the line settles more than 快了 (kuài le, "nearly there").
Evolution: advance-transformation. 进化论 is Darwin's theory; gamers use 进化 for level-ups, which Darwin might have minded. The neutral scholarly variant is 演化.

English: to import; imports; entrance (of a place)
Notes: 进 jìn (to take in) + 口 kǒu (mouth; opening). To bring goods in across a border, the opposite of 出口 chūkǒu (to export). The same word also names a physical "entrance," the opening you go in through.
进 jìn (to enter) + 来 lái (to come). To enter moving toward where the speaker is. 请进来 "please come in" is what you say from inside a room to someone at the door.

English: to go in (away from the speaker)
Notes: 进 jìn (to enter) + 去 qù (to go). To enter moving away from where the speaker stands. From outside a building you tell someone 你先进去 "you go in first."

English: to enter; to go into (a place or stage)
Notes: 进 jìn (to enter) + 入 rù (to go in). A more formal "to enter," used of physical spaces and of abstract stages alike: 进入房间 "enter the room," 进入新阶段 "enter a new phase."

English: palace graduate — the highest examination degree
Notes: The degree conferred on all who passed the palace examination (殿试). Literally "advanced to scholar" or "presented scholar." Receiving the 进士 degree placed a candidate in the imperial bureaucracy; specific posting and rank depended on one's place in the final ranking.

Notes: 进 jìn (to advance) + 展 zhǎn (to unfold). The headway a task, plan, or situation makes over time: 工作有了进展 "the work has made progress." More about an undertaking than a person.
经 jīng (to pass through; constant) + 常 cháng (constant). The standard adverb for an action that recurs as a regular habit: 我经常去那家店 "I go to that shop often." Stresses regularity, not just repetition.

Notes: 经 jīng (canon) + 典 diǎn (standard text; canon). A proven, enduring work, or the quality of being a touchstone: 经典电影 "a classic film," 文学经典 "literary classics."

English: to pass through; to go by; (after) the course of
Notes: 经 jīng (pass through) + 过 guò (cross over). To travel through a place, or to go through a process. As a noun it names the whole course of events: 事情的经过 "how the matter unfolded."

Notes: 经 jīng (manage; order) + 济 jì (aid; relieve). A shortening of 经世济民, "to order the age and aid the people." Now the standard word for the economy, and as an adjective "economical, thrifty": 经济实惠 "good value for money."

English: Special Economic Zone — the instrument of the opening
Notes: 经济 (economy, economic) + 特区 (special zone, from 特 special/exceptional + 区 zone/district). The bounded territories where market rules applied before they were extended nationally: 改革开放's experimental method made spatial.
经 jīng (manage) + 理 lǐ (to put in order). The one who runs the day-to-day affairs of a business: 总经理 zǒngjīnglǐ "general manager," 部门经理 "department manager."

English: to experience; experience; what one has been through
Notes: 经 jīng (to pass through; warp threads; to undergo) + 历 lì (to go through). The most common everyday word for living through something and for the sum of what one has lived through. As a verb it takes events as objects: you 经历 a war, a hardship, a change.

Notes: 经 jīng (warp thread; main channel) + 络 luò (network thread; connecting channel). Together they describe the body's energy network: 12 primary 经 channels + 8 extraordinary 奇经八脉 vessels + an extensive network of 络 branch channels. The basis of acupuncture, acupressure, and qigong.

English: mosque school education — traditional Islamic learning
Notes: 经堂教育 (mosque school education, lit. "sutra hall education," using the Buddhist term 经堂 for a building devoted to sacred texts) is the traditional system by which Hui Muslim boys study Arabic, Persian, and Islamic jurisprudence under an imam (阿訇 āhōng, from Persian ākhund).

经 jīng (pass through) + 验 yàn (to test; verify). The practical know-how gathered by having passed through and tested much: 工作经验 "work experience." Distinct from 经历, which is the events themselves rather than the lessons drawn from them.

English: a pleasant surprise; to be pleasantly surprised
Notes: 惊 jīng (startled) + 喜 xǐ (joy). The happy jolt of an unexpected good thing: 一个惊喜 "a surprise (gift or event)," 又惊又喜 "both startled and delighted."
精 (refined, essential) + 简 (pared down). To trim away the excess and keep only what is needed, used of staff, budgets, text, and organizations. Sharper and more deliberate than plain 简化.

Notes: A signature term of post-1978 reform-era political vocabulary, paired with 物质文明 (wùzhì wénmíng, material civilization).

English: to be proficient in; to master; to have a thorough command of
Notes: 精 jīng (refined; essence; finely worked) + 通 (to be all the way through). To have passed thoroughly through a field down to its fine grain: full mastery, not mere acquaintance. 精通 is reserved for genuine expertise: 精通三门外语 (fluent in three foreign languages), 精通法律 (thoroughly versed in law).

Notes: To toast , to offer a drink as a gesture of respect. 敬 means "to respect" or "to offer respectfully"; 酒 means "alcoholic drink." The act of toasting at a Chinese meal is a structured social protocol, not a casual gesture.

English: still-form qigong; seated or standing meditation
Notes: 静 jìng (still; quiet) + 功 gōng (practice). Qigong performed without external movement: seated meditation, standing post (站桩 zhàn zhuāng), or lying-down practices. The body is still while breath and attention cultivate interior movement of qi.

Notes: Nine Songs: the series of eleven shamanic hymns attributed to Qu Yuan, addressing the gods of the Chu pantheon. Among the most directly religious texts in the 楚辞, they preserve the ritual language of Chu shamanism within a literary frame.

English: double nine — colloquial shorthand; homophonic longevity wish
Notes: 九 jiǔ (nine) + 九 jiǔ (nine). The colloquial compressed name for the festival, and a sound-based wish: 九九 is homophonous with 久久 (jiǔ jiǔ, for a long time; lasting), turning the calendar date into an expression of the wish for long life.

Notes: The multiplication table: memorized in China as a chant of 45 compressed phrases from 一一得一 (1×1=1) to 九九八十一 (9×9=81). The chant begins with the smaller number, which is why it runs from 1×1 up rather than 9×9 down as in some other traditions.

English: the supreme position; the imperial throne
Notes: 九五 (the Nine-Five, the fifth yang line of the Qian hexagram, the "flying dragon in the heavens") + 之尊 (the honored, the exalted). The throne itself, the supreme position of the emperor. To 登上九五之尊 is to ascend the throne.

English: the highest heavens; the ninth sky
Notes: 九 jiǔ + 霄 xiāo (the upper sky; the clouds). The ninefold heaven, the very top of the sky, as high as the cosmos reaches.

九 jiǔ + 月 yuè (month). September in the solar calendar. The ninth day of the ninth lunar month is the Double Ninth Festival (重阳节 Chóngyáng Jié), when the doubled nine (the highest yang) is celebrated by climbing heights and honoring the elderly, the day's name 重阳 meaning "double yang." English: the Nine Provinces; all of China
Notes: 九 jiǔ + 州 zhōu (province; region). The nine ancient provinces into which the legendary sage-king Yu was said to have divided the land after taming the floods. 九州 became a poetic name for the whole of China, the entire civilized realm: 九州大地 (the great land of the nine provinces).

English: long ago; from the distant past; far back in time
Notes: 久 jiǔ (long; for a long time) + 远 yuǎn (far). Temporal distance mapped onto the same word as spatial distance. 久远 specifically emphasizes the antiquity of something , a tradition, a custom, a wound, a memory. Literary and slightly formal.

Notes: 酒 jiǔ (alcohol; wine; liquor) + 鬼 guǐ (ghost). A drunkard , someone possessed by alcohol to the point of losing themselves. The pattern is productive: 赌鬼 (dǔguǐ) is a compulsive gambler, 烟鬼 (yānguǐ) is a heavy smoker, 色鬼 (sèguǐ) is a lecher.

English: drinking capacity: how much alcohol one can hold
Notes: 酒 jiǔ (alcohol) + 量 liàng (capacity). A person's tolerance for drink, the amount they can take before they are affected. A culturally loaded word at the banquet table, where 酒量好 (a good capacity) is treated as a social asset: 他酒量很大 (he can really hold his drink).

English: the old calendar; the lunar calendar
Notes: 旧 (old) + 历 (lì, calendar; to pass through). The traditional lunisolar calendar, officially called 农历 (nónglì, agricultural calendar) or 阴历 (yīnlì, lunar calendar).

English: the old era; the old order
Notes: 旧 (old) + 时代 (shídài, era, age , time + generation). A period that has ended and been superseded. The phrase carries strong evaluative loading: in Communist-era writing, 旧时代 nearly always means the pre-1949 Republican or imperial period, and the connotation is negative.

旧 (former) + 址 (zhǐ, site, address , earth 土 + stop 止, the place where one stops/settles). The location of something that has moved or no longer exists. Appears on historical markers, museum labels, and administrative documents.
救 (rescue) + 护 (hù, protect) + 车 (chē, vehicle). The "rescue-and-protect vehicle." Hear a siren in a Chinese city and this is the word.

English: to save someone's life; to revive (the dying)
Notes: 救 jiù (to rescue) + 活 huó (alive) as a resultative ending. To rescue with the result of being alive: 活 here marks the outcome, that the rescue succeeded and the person lives. The same pattern builds 养活 yǎnghuó (to support, to keep alive by feeding).

救 (rescue) + 火 (huǒ, fire). Counterintuitively this means "to put out a fire," not to save the fire; here 救 keeps its Shuōwén sense of 止, halting the disaster. The same logic gives 救灾 (jiùzāi, disaster relief).
救 (rescue) + 济 (jì, to aid, to cross over). Material relief for the poor or disaster-struck: food, money, shelter. This is 救 in its social-welfare register.

救 (rescue) + 命 (mìng, life). Literally "save a life." As a shout it is the standard Chinese cry of distress, the equivalent of "Help!" As a verb-object phrase it describes the act of saving someone from death.

Notes: 救 (rescue) + 人 (rén, person). The general act of pulling a person out of danger, whether from water, fire, illness, or ruin.
救 (rescue) + 援 (yuán, to aid, to reach a hand). A coordinated, often large-scale rescue effort: teams, equipment, logistics. The default word for earthquake and mountain rescue.

English: nearby; at a convenient location close by
Notes: 就 jiù (then; right there; to conform to; to make use of what is present) + 近 (near). Making use of what is nearby , going to the closest available option rather than traveling farther.

English: precisely; exactly; even if; it's just that
Notes: 就 jiù (then; precisely; at once) + 是. Multiple functions make 就是 one of the most versatile particles in spoken Mandarin.

English: it's just that simple; merely this easy
Notes: 就 in this usage minimizes or dismisses: it is merely, just, only this , simpler or smaller than one might have expected. 就这样 "just like this, that's all" and 就这么 "it's simply this" are extremely common in casual speech for dismissing complexity or closing a matter.

居 jū (to dwell, to reside) + 民. A person defined by where they live rather than by their nationality: the residents of a building, a neighbourhood, a city, a region. The everyday administrative word, as in 居民区 jūmínqū (a residential district) and 城市居民 (urban residents).

English: chrysanthemum — the flower of the ninth month
Notes: 菊 jú (chrysanthemum) + 花 huā (flower; blossom). The chrysanthemum blooms in the ninth and tenth lunar months, when most flowering plants have finished. This timing made it a literary symbol of resilience, late-life achievement, and the refusal to conform to expected seasonal rhythms.

English: Grand Master — the head of the Mohist organization
Notes: 巨 jù (great; chief) + 子 zǐ (master). The elected or designated leader of the Mohist order, holding authority over all members. The 巨子 could direct members to travel, take on defense contracts for states, and enforce the school's internal law.

Notes: 句 jù (sentence) + 号 hào (mark; sign). The punctuation mark that closes a sentence, written in Chinese as a small hollow circle 。 rather than a dot. Idiomatically 画上句号 "to draw the full stop" means to bring something to a close.

句 jù (sentence) + 子 zi (noun-suffix). The everyday word for a complete sentence as a grammatical unit: 一个句子 "one sentence," 简单的句子 "a simple sentence." The building block every grammar lesson works with.

具 jù (to possess, to furnish) + 体 tǐ (body, form). Having a definite body, hence concrete and specific as against vague or abstract. Its opposite is 抽象 chōuxiàng (abstract): 具体的例子 "a concrete example."

English: to possess (a quality, characteristic, or abstract attribute)
Notes: 具 jù (to possess; equipped with; concrete tool) + 有. Formal written register. Used specifically to assert that a subject possesses an abstract quality, characteristic, feature, or capacity , not physical objects. 具有能力 (to possess ability), 具有价值 (to have value), 具有代表性 (to be representative).

English: As far as I know	As far as I know." A hedge that acknowledges your information may be incomplete. Useful when stating something you believe to be true but do not want to assert with full confidence. Carries a slightly bookish, considered tone.

距 (jù, to be apart) plus 离 (to be apart). A noun for the measured space between two points, and also a verb for being that far apart. Used for physical and emotional distance alike.

Notes: 决 jué (to resolve; to break through) + 定 dìng (to settle). To bring a choice to rest, and also the decision itself. 做决定 zuò juédìng "to make a decision." The most common everyday word for deciding.

English: Quatrain , four lines of five or seven characters
Notes: Quatrain , four lines of five or seven characters. The most concentrated Tang form.
军 (military) + 队 (formed unit). The standing army as an institution, the original martial home of 队 made explicit.

Notes: The political relationship. The ruler (君 jūn) is obligated to govern benevolently and justly; the subject (臣 chén) is obligated to serve loyally and to remonstrate when the ruler errs. 忠 zhōng (loyalty) is the core virtue for the subject; 仁政 rénzhèng (benevolent governance) for the ruler.

English: to see a doctor; to seek medical treatment
Notes: 看 (to look at, to examine) + 病 (illness). The verb covers both sides of the clinical encounter: the patient "looks at" the illness by going to be treated, and the doctor "looks at" the illness to diagnose it. Context distinguishes who is doing the looking. 我去看病 (I'm going to see a doctor).

English: to look down on; to disdain; to have contempt for
Notes: 看 (to look) + 不起 (cannot rise up to). The potential complement 不起 indicates inability to raise the gaze high enough , to look up to. Contempt as a failure of elevation. Its opposite is 看得起 kàndéqǐ (to respect, to think well of, to regard highly). 他看不起任何人 , He has contempt for everyone.

English: to see through; to figure out
Notes: 看 (kàn, to look) + 穿 (to pierce, as a result complement). The gaze bores all the way through the surface, you see through a lie, a disguise, a scheme. 穿 here is the original drilling sense turned to the mind: the look penetrates and reaches the truth behind.

English: to see; to catch sight of
Notes: 看 kàn (to look) + 到 dào (arrive). Looking that arrived at its object: perception confirmed. 看到 asserts that the visual information reached awareness. Without 到, 看 is merely the act of looking, which may or may not result in seeing.

看 (to watch) + 电视 (television). 看 is the default verb for watching screens: 看电影 (to watch a film), 看视频 (to watch a video), 看直播 (to watch a live stream), 看比赛 (to watch a match). The verb doesn't change regardless of the medium , 看 covers any directed visual consumption of moving images.
看 (kàn, to look) plus 懂. The visual counterpart to 听懂: to read a text, watch a film, or view a chart and grasp it.

看 (to look) + 法 (method, way). A held view as a particular way of looking at something. 你对这件事有什么看法？ (What's your view on this matter?). More formal and substantive than 意见 yìjiàn (opinion, suggestion). 世界观 shìjièguān (worldview) extends the same logic: how the world appears from your vantage.

English: to favor; to back; to be bullish on
Notes: 看 (to see, to judge) + 好 (as good/positive). To evaluate something as likely to succeed or worth supporting. Widely used in investment contexts (看好这只股票 , bullish on this stock), sports prediction (我看好他们赢 , I favor them to win), and interpersonal support (我很看好你 , I have high hopes for you).

#fields:Hanzi: 看见 · 看完 · 看懂
Notes: 看 combines with resultative complements to specify the outcome of the looking. 看见 kànjiàn (to catch sight of , result: visual contact made). 看完 kànwán (to finish reading or watching , result: completion). 看懂 kàndǒng (to read and understand , result: comprehension).

English: watched twice; read it through twice
Notes: 了 with a frequency complement (遍 biàn = complete passes through, 次 cì = times, 回 huí = times in colloquial speech). Marks the action as having been performed a counted number of complete cycles. The quantification of repetition implies completion of each cycle.
看门 (kānmén, to watch the gate) + 狗. A dog that guards the door. Figuratively it names anything that stands watch, including the software process that restarts a crashed system.

English: to visit a friend; to go see someone
Notes: 看 extends naturally from visual attention to social attention: going to see someone implies caring, checking in, tending to the relationship. 看朋友 (visit a friend), 看望 kànwàng (to visit and care for, especially an elder or patient), 探望 tànwàng (to pay a visit, more formal).

Notes: 看 (to look at) + 书 (book). The standard way to say "to read" in Mandarin , specifically reading for comprehension or leisure. 读书 dúshū overlaps but emphasizes reading aloud or formal study; 看书 is the unmarked everyday verb for sitting with a book.

可 kě (can; worthy of) + 爱 ài (love). Worthy of being loved: cute, adorable. One of the most-used adjectives in everyday Mandarin. Used for children, animals, cartoon characters, and endearing people.

Notes: 可 (worth) + 靠 (to lean on; to rely on). Worth leaning on. Used for people, sources of information, systems, and promises.

Notes: A very common stack: 可能 ("possibly") plus the modal 会 ("will / be likely to"), giving "might, may well." 明天可能会变冷 ("it might turn cold tomorrow"). The 会 adds the sense of a future tendency, so 可能会 feels a touch more about what is likely to happen, while bare 可能 just flags that something is possible.

可能 kěnéng (possible) + 性 xìng (-ness). The abstract noun "possibility," built by attaching the -ity suffix to the adjective 可能: 有可能性 "there is a possibility," 很大的可能性 "a strong likelihood." A model case of how 性 turns a quality into a countable, discussable thing.
可 (worth) + 怕 (to fear). Worth fearing. Used for things that inspire genuine dread , horror films, dangerous situations, extreme weather, powerful people.

English: unfortunately; what a pity; it is a shame that
Notes: 可 (worth) + 惜 (to pity; to regret the loss of something). Worth regretting. Functions as an adjective (这很可惜 , this is a pity) and as a sentential adverb opening a clause (可惜他没来 , unfortunately he did not come).
Tags: grammar modal ability permission classical syntax

Notes: 可 kě (worthy of; -able) + 笑 xiào (laugh). Worthy of being laughed at: ridiculous, absurd. Built on the same 可 + verb pattern as 可爱 (worthy of love → cute) and 可怕 (worthy of fear → frightening). Often carries a sting.

English: can; may; it is permissible to; acceptable; not bad
Notes: The most versatile 可-compound. 可 (permitted/possible) + 以 (by means of; using). As a modal verb it covers both capability and permission. As a colloquial adjective it means "acceptable" or "not bad." It is the go-to answer when someone asks if something is okay.

English: May I come in? — requesting permission
Notes: 可以 is the canonical permission modal. It asks or grants social authorization , whether rules, norms, context, or a person in authority allows an action. The asker knows they have the physical ability; the question is whether they have the social right.

Notes: 克 kè (to overcome) + 己 jǐ (self). To conquer one's own impulses, the Confucian ideal of self-mastery. The root of 克己复礼, "subdue the self and return to ritual," and of 克己奉公, "curb oneself and serve the public good."

刻 (kè), to carve or engrave, joins 苦 (kǔ) to describe effort that bites in: study or training pursued through self-denial. A 刻苦 student drills past comfort, the way a blade is sharpened against stone.

Notes: Guest star: a star that appears briefly and then fades, i.e., a nova or supernova. Chinese court astronomers maintained careful records of guest stars for astrological-political interpretation: a guest star in a particular mansion was a portent for specific ministers, regions, or dynasties.
课 kè (lesson) + 本 běn (volume). The book for a course of study. A close synonym is 教科书 jiàokēshū, slightly more formal.
课堂 kètáng (classroom) + 笔记 bǐjì. Notes taken during class. 借笔记 jiè bǐjì = to borrow someone's notes. 整理笔记 zhěnglǐ bǐjì = to organize/clean up one's notes.
肯 kěn (to be willing; to assent) + 定 dìng (to settle). To settle a thing as yes: as an adverb, "certainly," and as a verb, "to affirm, to confirm." Its opposite is 否定 fǒudìng (to negate; negative).

Notes: 空 kōng (empty) + 间 jiān (space). Empty space, both physical and figurative: 没有空间 "no room," 发展空间 "room to grow." Paired with 时间, the two name space and time together.

Notes: 空 (sky, air) plus 姐 is the colloquial word for a female flight attendant, literally a "sky sister." It is a clipped, affectionate everyday term beside the formal 空中小姐 (kōngzhōng xiǎojiě).

空 kōng (empty; void; sky) + 气 qì. The physical substance of the atmosphere, what you breathe. Also used metaphorically for social atmosphere: 房间里的空气很紧张 "the air in the room was tense." The same word covers oxygen and social mood.

Notes: 口 kǒu (mouth) + 才 cái (talent). Literally "mouth-talent," the ability to speak well and persuasively: 他很有口才 "he is very eloquent." One of a family of 才 compounds naming a specific gift, alongside 文才 wéncái (literary talent).

English: manner of speaking; breath smell; implied attitude
Notes: 口 kǒu (mouth) + 气 qì. Operates on two levels: (1) the qi from the mouth, literally breath smell (口气重 "bad breath"); (2) the implied attitude and tone in what someone says, what their words reveal about how they feel. 你这个口气 "That tone of yours…" carries reproach.

Mouth-Chan: enlightenment talked rather than lived, generalized into anyone's verbal habit. 他的口头禅是"没问题" means "no problem" is his catchphrase. One of the most useful conversation words about conversation.

口 kǒu (mouth) + 味 wèi (flavor; taste). Both the objective flavor of food and the subjective preference of a taster. 这不合我的口味 "This doesn't suit my taste." 口味重 kǒuwèi zhòng = "strong-flavored preferences" , liking bold, heavy flavors.

口 kǒu (mouth) + 吻 wěn (lips; to kiss, the form of the mouth). The shape of what comes from the mouth, the distinctive way a person speaks, implying their perspective and attitude. More literary than 口气, used in written analysis, narration, and formal commentary.
口 kǒu (mouth) + 音 yīn (sound). The sound a particular mouth gives a language, marking where the speaker is from: 南方口音 "a southern accent," 带口音 "to have an accent."

苦 kǔ = suffering, bitterness, difficulty. Sanskrit dukkha: a wheel whose axle is off-center, generating grinding rather than smooth motion. The Buddha's first noble truth: life as ordinarily lived is characterized by dukkha.

苦 (bitter, hard) plus 力 (lì, strength) names grueling physical labor and, historically, the laborer himself. The English word "coolie" carries this same syllable. In modern speech 干苦力 means to do back-breaking work.

English: to train hard, to drill relentlessly
Notes: Here 苦 works as an adverb on 练 (liàn, to train): to practice bitterly, to grind. The word frames mastery as something earned through painful repetition rather than talent.

苦 (bitter) joins 难 (nàn, calamity, disaster) to name suffering on a large, often historical scale: famine, war, oppression. Weightier than everyday hardship, 苦难 belongs to the language of nations and generations.
苦 (bitter) plus 心 (xīn, heart, mind) names the trouble one's heart goes through for someone else's sake. 一片苦心 (yí piàn kǔxīn) is a heartful of well-meant pains, often unrecognized.

苦 (bitter) plus 衷 (zhōng, inner feelings) names the private difficulty behind a person's puzzling choice, the bitterness they cannot say aloud. To have a 苦衷 is to act badly for a reason you keep hidden.
Containment covers goods not yet shipped. Ask the factory to check 库存 and the work in progress (在制品 zàizhìpǐn) before anything else leaves.

English: to boast; to praise (phonetic of 跨)
to take a stride; a step
Notes: 跨 + 步 (bù, step). The base physical sense , a single deliberate stride, often a long one. Used in athletics, dance, military drill, and figuratively for any decisive move forward.

English: span (of a bridge, an era, a project)
Notes: 跨 + 度 (dù, degree; measure). The measurable distance from one support to another , originally an architectural and engineering term (the 跨度 of an arch or bridge), now extended to time spans, salary ranges, age gaps, and the scope of a project or career.
跨 + 国 (guó, country). 跨国公司 (kuàguó gōngsī, multinational corporation) is the canonical compound. Also 跨国婚姻 (cross-national marriage), 跨国合作 (cross-national cooperation), 跨国犯罪 (transnational crime).

English: to step over; to get past
Notes: 跨 + 过 (guò, to pass). The everyday verb of stepping over a low obstacle: a threshold, a puddle, a fallen branch. By extension, getting past a difficulty in a single move. Common with 门槛 ménkǎn (threshold) , both literal and metaphorical.

跨 + 界 (jiè, field; domain). A buzzword in entertainment, design, and business since the 2000s: an actor turning singer, a fashion brand collaborating with a tech company, a novelist directing a film. 跨界合作 (kuàjiè hézuò) "crossover collaboration" appears constantly in marketing copy.

跨 + 境 (jìng, border; territory). The standard term in trade and law. 跨境电商 (kuàjìng diànshāng, cross-border e-commerce) is one of the most-used compounds in contemporary business writing. 跨境 carries a more administrative tone than 跨国; 国 invokes the country, 境 the legal frontier.

English: to cross over into the new year
Notes: 跨 + 年 (nián, year). The standard verb for what one does on New Year's Eve , celebrating through midnight from the old year into the new. 跨年晚会 (kuànián wǎnhuì) "New Year's Eve gala" is the genre name for the live-broadcast countdown shows.

English: to mount; to step up onto (astride)
Notes: 跨 + 上 (shàng, up; onto). To swing one leg over and mount: a horse, a bicycle, a motorcycle, a stage. The verb preserves the original image of legs spread on either side. The poetic phrase 跨上战马 kuà shàng zhànmǎ "to mount the war-horse" recurs throughout classical narrative and modern wuxia.

跨 kuà (to straddle, to cross over) + 文化 (culture). Cross-cultural: spanning or bridging different cultural contexts. 跨文化交际 kuà wénhuà jiāojì (intercultural communication) is an academic field. 跨文化婚姻 (cross-cultural marriage) appears in demographic and social discussions.

Notes: 跨 + 学科 (xuékē, academic discipline). The standard rendering of "interdisciplinary" in Chinese academic writing. 跨学科研究 (kuà xuékē yánjiū) "interdisciplinary research" is now a frequent funding category.

The modifier form, suffixing 式 (shì, type/style) to make an adjective. Most common in 跨越式发展 (kuàyuè shì fāzhǎn, "leap-forward development"), the standard term in Chinese policy and journalism for skipping intermediate stages of economic or technological growth.

Spoken prices use 块 for the main unit, 毛 for tenths, 分 for hundredths; written prices use 元, 角, 分. The trailing unit is often dropped: 四块一 is 4.10, 三块八五 is 3.85. Factories apply the same words to dollars, so add 美金 (měijīn) or 人民币 (rénmínbì) when it could be either.

English: be quick; a bit faster; hurry
Notes: 快 kuài (fast) + 点 diǎn (a little; somewhat , the softening particle). The most colloquial way to tell someone to speed up. Tonal in its delivery: said gently it is a nudge, said sharply it is impatient.

English: carefree; cheerful; lively and at ease
Notes: 快 kuài (unobstructed) + 活 huó (alive; living; moving freely). The image is life flowing without constraint. Carries a slightly old-fashioned or literary flavor in modern Mandarin, but remains warm and vivid in fiction and colloquial northern speech. Describes people who seem naturally unburdened.

Notes: 快 kuài (released; unobstructed) + 乐 lè (music; joy; ease). The standard word for happiness in modern Mandarin: it is an adjective predicate, a pre-noun modifier, and a noun. Appears in greetings and fixed phrases far more than the simple 快 alone.

Notes: 快 kuài (fast) + 速 sù (speed; velocity). The compound reinforces both components, producing the most neutral, all-purpose word for fast in formal or written Chinese. Works as an adjective before nouns or as an adverb before verbs.

Notes: Chopstick rest: a small ceramic or metal rest placed beside the bowl to lay chopsticks on between bites. Used in formal settings; absent in casual ones.

宽 kuān (wide; broad) + 容 róng (to hold). To hold broadly: a generous, forgiving disposition that leaves wide room for others' faults. Where 容忍 is a grudging act, 宽容 is an admired character trait. The 宽 (wide) intensifies the holding image directly: a broad vessel spills less.
狂 kuáng (wild; unrestrained) + 欢 huān (joy). Joy turned up to its loudest: unrestrained revelry. 狂欢节 kuánghuānjié is the standard word for Carnival, and 狂欢 names any wild, all-out celebration.

Notes: 困 (trapped) + 境 (situation, circumstance). A predicament you are stuck inside, with no obvious exit. Stronger and more structural than 困难: a 困境 is the whole walled situation, not a single problem.
困 (sleepy) + 倦 (weary, jaded). The settled, heavy tiredness that pulls a person toward sleep. More literary than 犯困, fitting written description of a long day's fatigue.

困 (hemmed in) + 难 (hard). The everyday word for a problem that resists you, or for the strained circumstances a person lives through. Works as both a noun (a difficulty) and an adjective (difficult, hard-up).

Notes: 困 (sleepy) + 意 (feeling, inclination). The sensation of sleepiness itself, the rising pull you can either fight off or give in to.

English: there's not enough time; too late to do something
Notes: 来 lái (to come; to reach) + 不 bù (not) + 及 jí (to reach; to catch up to). The time has not come far enough to reach this action, so there is not enough time. Opposite: 来得及 lái de jí (there is still time; still possible).

English: (he/she/it) has come; has arrived; here it is
Notes: 来 lái (to come) + 了 le (completion/change-of-state particle). The arrival has been completed: the thing or person is now here. One of the most basic and high-frequency phrases in Mandarin.

English: the next life; the afterlife; the life to come
Notes: 来 lái (coming) + 世 shì (life). The life that follows this one in the Buddhist cycle of rebirth: 来世再相见 "to meet again in the next life." Paired with 前世 (a former life) and 今世 (this life) to span the chain of rebirths.

English: source; origin; where something comes from
Notes: 来 lái (to come) + 源 yuán (source; origin; spring, where water comes from). "The place from which it comes." Used for the source of funding (资金来源), information (信息来源), authority (权力来源), and anything whose origin needs to be named.

English: to come from; to originate from; hailing from
Notes: 来 lái (to come; to arrive) + 自 zì (from; self; origin). The standard formal expression for geographic or conceptual origin. Used for people (来自北京), ideas (这个想法来自实验), data (数据来自2023年), and institutions (来自联合国的报告).

English: a musical composition; a piece of music
Notes: 乐 yuè (music) + 曲 qǔ (tune; melody). A composed piece of music: 一首乐曲 "a piece of music." The 曲 names the melody, the 乐 the musical art it belongs to.

English: delight; pleasure; the fun of a thing
Notes: 乐 lè (joy) + 趣 qù (interest; fun). The pleasure or enjoyment found in an activity: 读书的乐趣 "the pleasure of reading."

English: to take joy in mountains and water; to be a person of refined nature
Notes: A condensed echo of the Analects line. Note the alternative reading: in this fixed phrase 乐 is sometimes read yào in the classical pronunciation (the same character as 乐 lè / yuè, with multiple historical readings , yào here marks affective preference).
乐 lè (glad) + 意 yì (intention; will). To be happy to do something, with the nuance of genuine willingness: 我很乐意帮忙 "I'd be glad to help."

了 liǎo (to conclude; to surpass) + 不 + 起 (unable to rise above; potential complement marker). Literally "cannot be surpassed or concluded" , what cannot be surpassed is extraordinary. A high-praise adjective in everyday speech.

English: to conclude; to settle; to bring to a definitive end
Notes: 了 liǎo (to conclude) + 结 jié (knot; tied up; settled). To tie off and close a matter definitively. Used for settling disputes, concluding legal cases, or resolving something that has dragged on without resolution. Has a formal or literary flavor , matters of weight are 了结d.

English: to understand thoroughly; to have rounded knowledge of
Notes: 了 liǎo (clear-sighted; complete) + 解 jiě (to unravel; to untie). Common across casual speech and formal registers.

Notes: Phonetic transliteration of the English "radar" (Radio Detection And Ranging). 雷 léi (thunder) + 达 dá (to reach; to arrive). A felicitous loanword: the chosen characters evoke the technology's function , a signal (like thunder, striking out from a source) that reaches and returns.

English: Duke of Thunder — the thunder deity
Notes: 雷 léi (thunder) + 公 gōng (duke; honorific for male deities and elder men). The personified god of thunder, depicted with a bird beak, wings, and ring of drums. Works alongside 电母 (Diàn Mǔ, Mother of Lightning).

English: the sound of thunder; a thunderclap
Notes: 雷 léi (thunder) + 声 shēng (sound). The rumble or crack of thunder. Often used in the phrase 雷声大，雨点小 (léishēng dà, yǔdiǎn xiǎo) , "thunder loud, raindrops small" , meaning all bluster and announcement with little actual follow-through.

雷 léi (thunder) + 雨 yǔ (rain). A thunderstorm , rain accompanied by thunder and lightning. Also the title of one of the most important plays in modern Chinese literature: 雷雨 (Léiyǔ, 1934) by Cao Yu (曹禺), a family tragedy of suppressed desire and social constraint.
Cold. 天冷了，多穿点 ("it's gotten cold, wear more") is the all-purpose expression of care from mothers, landladies, and group chats.

#fields:Hanzi: 离 + 时间点 + 还有
Notes: 离 measures distance in time as well as space. Naming a future point, then 还有 ("there still is") plus a span, counts down to it: 离新年还有两个星期 ("there are still two weeks until New Year"), 离上课还有五分钟 ("five minutes until class"). It is the natural way to say "how long until" something.

Leave-shore price. Most export quotes are FOB, always with a port: FOB宁波, FOB深圳. In speech people simply say the letters, F-O-B. The port matters, since inland trucking to a distant port is part of the factory's cost.

English: to part, to take leave (of people)
Notes: 离 (to part) plus 别 (bié, to part, to bid farewell). A literary word for the parting of people, weighted with feeling. It carries the ache of long goodbyes.
离 (to part) plus 婚 (hūn, marriage). A separable verb: the two halves can split apart, mirroring the meaning. 离了婚 (líle hūn) means got divorced.

Notes: 离 (to part) plus 开 (kāi, to open, to move away). The most common verb for leaving a place or a person. It takes a direct object: you leave something.

Notes: 离 lí (to separate from; to leave; distance) + 去 qù (to go away). To separate and go , departure with a sense of severance. More emphatic and often more final than 走 alone. Used for leaving a job, a relationship, a city, or a life. 她悄悄地离去了 (She quietly departed) , the 去 carries the irreversibility.

English: to resign, to leave a post
Notes: 离 (to leave) plus 职 (zhí, post, office). The formal verb for quitting a job or stepping down from a position.

Ritual morality eats people: the compressed formula, derived from "A Madman's Diary," for Lu Xun central argument that the Confucian system of ritual and ethical teaching functions as a mechanism of social domination and destruction rather than genuine moral cultivation.

English: ritual and music — the twin pillars of Zhou social order
Notes: 礼 lǐ (ritual; propriety; ceremony) + 乐 yuè (music; joy). The cultural program systematized by the Duke of Zhou: ritual prescribed the correct form for all significant social acts; music calibrated the relationship between human society and the cosmic order.

Notes: 礼貌 + 用语 yòngyǔ (set expressions; phrases used in a particular register). Names the inventory of fixed polite phrases: 您好 nín hǎo, 谢谢 xièxiè, 不客气 bú kèqi, 对不起 duìbuqǐ, 请 qǐng, 麻烦您 máfan nín, 辛苦了 xīnkǔ le. Mastering 礼貌用语 is the visible threshold of being 有礼貌.

礼 lǐ (ritual offering) + 物 wù (thing; object; matter). Lit. "a ritual-offering made material." A gift in Chinese culture is always, at some level, a ritual object that carries social meaning exceeding its material value.

Notes: 礼 lǐ + 仪 yí (appearance; manner; instrument of measurement). The formal standards of conduct for official occasions. 礼仪小姐 = ceremonial hostess. 外交礼仪 diplomatic protocol. More formal and institutional than 礼貌.

Notes: 理 lǐ (principle, pattern, reason) + 论. A theory: an organised set of principles, as opposed to practice (实践 shíjiàn). 理论上 lǐlùn shàng "in theory" pairs with 实际上 shíjì shàng "in practice" in the standard contrast.

Notes: 力 lì (force, strength) + 量 liàng (measure, amount). The measurable quantity of force, whether physical, social, or moral: 体力的力量 (bodily strength), 团结的力量 (the power of unity), 知识就是力量 (knowledge is power).

Notes: 力 lì (force) + 气 qì (breath; vital energy). The bodily strength you can feel in your muscles, the kind used to lift, carry, or push: 没力气 "have no strength," 花力气 "to spend effort." Concrete and physical, never abstract.

历 lì (successive; passing through) + 代 dài (generation; dynasty; era). Refers to the whole sequence of past dynasties or generations taken together: "every dynasty in turn," "successive ages." English: to go through; to undergo (a long or arduous process)
Notes: 历 lì (to pass through) + 经 jīng (to undergo). The same two characters as 经历 in reverse order, but the register and feel differ: 历经 is more literary and emphasizes a long, often difficult passage through many stages.

English: always; throughout history; from of old up to now
Notes: 历 lì (passing through time) + 来 lái (coming up to the present). An adverb meaning "all along throughout the past until now," used to assert that something has consistently been the case across the whole span of history.
历史 lìshǐ (history) + 故事 gùshì (story). A historical narrative , story with identifiable historical figures and events. Distinguished from 神话 (myth) and 传说 (legend) by its claimed factual basis.

历史 + 观 (view; perspective; outlook , the same 观 as in 世界观 shìjièguān, worldview, and 人生观 rénshēngguān, outlook on life). 历史观 is the framework through which one interprets history: its patterns, its forces, its meaning.

English: historiography; the academic discipline of history
Notes: 历史 + 学 (the suffix marking a field of systematic study: 哲学 philosophy, 科学 science, 心理学 psychology). 历史学 is history as an academic discipline , the methods, debates, and institutions of scholarly historical inquiry, as distinct from history as the accumulated record of events.

Notes: 厉 (severe, sharp) + 害 (harm), here neutral-toned. Literally cutting and harmful, the word swung into admiration: someone or something so strong it could hurt you. Praise and warning at once.

立 (lì, to stand/establish) + 春 (spring). The first of the twenty-four solar terms (节气 jiéqì), falling around February 4, when the year's farming cycle is reckoned to begin. 立 marks a season being set up, the same verb in 立夏, 立秋, 立冬.

English: to render meritorious service: to perform a deed
Notes: 立 lì (to establish; to set up) + 功 gōng (merit). To establish merit through a notable deed, originally military, now also civic and professional. A verb-object compound, so it splits: 立了大功 = rendered great service. Often paired with reward: 立功受奖 = to perform a deed and receive a commendation.
利 lì (benefit) + 己 jǐ (self). Acting for one's own advantage. Often paired in contrast: 利己 vs. 利人 (to benefit others), and condemned in the phrase 损人利己, "harm others to profit oneself."

English: to make use of; to leverage; to exploit
Notes: 利 lì (benefit; advantage; profit) + 用 yòng (to use). To use something for advantage, to derive profit from a resource, opportunity, or person. Context determines valence: 利用时间 (make good use of time) is positive; 利用别人 (exploit others) is negative.

English: for example; for instance; such as
Notes: 例 lì (example; case) + 如 rú (like). The standard phrase for introducing an instance: 例如这本书 "for example, this book." Its close cousin is 比如 bǐrú, which is more colloquial.

Notes: 连…都 also works in "positive" extremes , where the person chosen is the most likely to be able to do something, the highest authority on the scale. When even they fail, the implication is that certainly no one else can.

连 lián (right after; immediately) + 忙 máng (busy; to hurry). An adverb describing a reaction that follows hard on the heels of its cause, "at once, without delay." English: not even time to sleep — the most basic need is unmet
Notes: The item after 连 can be an entire noun phrase, including a relative clause. 连睡觉的时间 = "even the time for sleeping" , 睡觉 is the most basic physical requirement; not having time even for that represents the absolute extreme of busyness or exhaustion.

English: even he doesn't know — the informed one is stumped
Notes: The simplest and most frequent form: 连 + person/thing + 都 + (negated) verb. The person chosen is the one who would be most expected to know or be able to do the thing , making their failure maximal evidence for the claim.

连 lián (to join) + 同 tóng (same; together). A prepositional connector meaning "together with," used to add an item to a group as part of the same action. It bundles the second thing into the first, treating them as one joined set: send the report along with the attachments.

连 lián (in a series) + 续 xù (to continue; to extend). Without interruption, one period or event following directly on the last. Frequently paired with a counter: 连续三天 (three days running), 连续剧 (a TV serial, lit. "continuous drama"). The emphasis is on an unbroken stretch.

Pinyin: lián yī fēn qián dōu méiyǒu
English: doesn't have even a single cent — the minimum quantity = nothing
Notes: When the extreme case is a minimum quantity (one cent, one word, one minute), the construction means "not even the smallest amount." This is a highly emphatic way of expressing absolute absence. The minimum unit becomes the threshold , and even that threshold is not crossed.

English: to unite; to join together; joint; united
Notes: 联 lián (to link; to connect) + 合 hé (to join). To link separate parties into a single front: 联合国 "the United Nations," 联合声明 "a joint statement." The uniting is formal and often institutional.

English: to contact; to get in touch; to link; connection
Notes: 联 lián (to join; to unite) + 系 xì (tie). Both the act of making contact and the link itself. As a verb: 联系我 "get in touch with me." As a noun: 保持联系 "keep in contact."

Notes: A compound that fuses both face concepts. 脸面 covers the full spectrum , both the social prestige dimension of 面子 and the moral character dimension of 脸. Often used in contexts where both are at stake: 要顾脸面 (to consider one's dignity) means both social standing and personal integrity.
脸 (face) + 盆 (basin). The basin you fill to wash your face, a fixture of older Chinese households before plumbing reached every sink. A small window onto domestic life packed into two characters.

English: facial skin; (figurative) sense of shame; nerve
Notes: 脸 (face) + 皮 (skin). The skin of the face, and by extension one's capacity for shame. 脸皮厚 (liǎnpí hòu), thick-skinned, means shameless or unembarrassable; 脸皮薄 (liǎnpí báo), thin-skinned, means easily mortified.

Notes: Both shores: the standard PRC and Taiwan term for the cross-strait relationship: literally "both banks" (of the Taiwan Strait). 两岸关系 (cross-strait relations) is the neutral term used by both governments.

两 liǎng + 边 biān (side). Both sides, the two sides of something, drawing directly on 两's sense of a balanced pair: 马路两边 (both sides of the road), 两边都同意 (both sides agree). Related are 两手 (both hands), 两旁 (on either side), and 两端 (the two ends).
两 liǎng + 点 diǎn (o'clock; point). Two o'clock: 下午两点 (two in the afternoon). Because 点 functions as a measure word here, the two must be 两, not 二. The same logic gives 两点意见 (two points of opinion).

两 liǎng + 个 gè (the general measure word). The basic, high-frequency way to count two of almost anything: 两个人 (two people), 两个问题 (two questions), 两个小时 (two hours). The use of 两 rather than 二 here is obligatory, since a measure word follows.

English: a married couple; husband and wife
Notes: 两 liǎng + 口 kǒu (mouth, here a person) + 子 (suffix). A colloquial, warm word for a married couple, the two of them as a household pair: 他们两口子 (the two of them, that couple). 小两口 (xiǎo liǎngkǒu) is an affectionate term for a young couple.

English: to take a temperature: to measure body heat
Notes: 量 liáng (to measure) + 体温 tǐwēn (body temperature). A high-frequency everyday verb-object phrase: to take someone's temperature with a thermometer. The same 量 measures other body data in parallel phrases, 量血压 (liáng xuèyā, to take blood pressure), 量身高 (liáng shēngāo, to measure height).

Notes: 灵 líng (quick, clever, responsive) + 活 huó (lively, free). Able to move or change freely: nimble fingers, a flexible schedule, a supple mind. The opposite is 死板 sǐbǎn (rigid, literally dead-stiff), where the water has stopped flowing.

English: the trance-rescue — spirit-sailing to save her father
Notes: The foundational legend: Lin Mo, while weaving at home, fell into a trance. In her spirit-state, she crossed the sea, seized her father's boat with one hand and her brother's boat with the other, guiding them through a terrible storm.

English: The four major silk fabric types (gauze, thin silk, thick silk, satin) often used together as a set phrase meaning luxury silk goods in general. An elegant way to say "silk" in classical and literary contexts.

Notes: 聆 (to listen carefully , 耳 radical) + 听 (to hear). A formal compound for respectful, focused listening. Used for listening to elders, teachers, and music: 聆听老师的教诲 (listen attentively to the teacher's instruction); 聆听音乐 (to truly listen to music, not just hear it).

零 líng (fragmentary; odd; loose) + 件 jiàn (a piece). The small individual parts that make up a machine, especially replaceable ones. 零 carries the sense of scattered, loose pieces, so 零件 is the loose hardware: screws, gears, the bits kept in a parts drawer.

English: to wither and fall; scattered; declined and broken up
Notes: 零 líng (to fall in drops) + 落 luò (to fall; to drop). Closest to the character's root: things falling and scattering. Of flowers and leaves, to wither and drop; of people, families, or fortunes, to scatter and decline (家道零落, the household fallen on hard times).

零 líng (zero; scattered; odd bits) + 钱 qián. Change, small bills and coins. Increasingly rare in mainland China where mobile payment (微信支付/支付宝) dominates. 找钱 zhǎo qián = to give change. 整钱 zhěng qián = a whole bill (no change needed).

Notes: 零 líng (small, piecemeal) + 食 shí (food). The bits eaten between whole meals: snacks, nibbles, treats. 吃零食 is to snack. The word reflects 零's sense of the scattered and fractional, food taken in small odd amounts rather than as a proper sit-down meal (整餐).

零 líng (zero) + 下 xià (below). Below zero degrees, the standard way to state freezing temperatures: 零下十度 (minus ten degrees). Its counterpart 零上 (above zero) is less often said, since positive temperatures are usually given as a bare number.

Besides or "in addition." Marks a related but separate point. Useful when you want to add information that is not strictly part of the same argument: 另外, 我想问你一件事 ("also, I want to ask you something").

Liu Bei — the archetype of the benevolent ruler

English: to circulate; to spread and survive; to be handed down
Notes: 流 liú (to flow) + 传 chuán (to pass on). For a story, saying, or work to circulate widely and endure over time: 这个传说一直流传至今 "this legend has been handed down to the present day." Combines the flowing of 流 with the passing-on of 传.

English: popular; trending; to spread (of fashion, illness, songs)
Notes: 流 liú (to flow) + 行 xíng. Flowing-and-traveling. The verb for something that spreads through a population , fashion, slang, popular songs, viruses. 流行音乐 = pop music; 流行病 = an epidemic; 这种说法很流行 = "this expression is very widespread."

English: 留白 — leaving white; the empty space in composition
Notes: 留 liú (to leave; to keep) + 白 bái (white; blank). The deliberate empty space left unpainted in Chinese composition: 留白 is an active compositional element, not a failure to fill space. Empty space creates breathing room, implies what is unseen, and activates the imagination.

English: the six paramitas; the six perfections of the bodhisattva path
Notes: 波罗蜜 bōluómì from Sanskrit pāramitā: "crossing to the other shore" , from suffering to liberation, from delusion to insight.

六 (six) + 道 (path; way; realm). The six realms through which beings cycle in Buddhist cosmology: gods, asuras, humans, animals, hungry ghosts, and hell beings. The human realm (人道 rén dào or 人间道 rénjiān dào) occupies the middle tier. Beings move between realms through karma generated in each life.

English: the six-realm cycle of rebirth; the full Buddhist cosmological cycle
Notes: The full phrase naming the complete cycle: 六道 (six realms) + 轮回 (the turning cycle). Used when the complete cosmological picture is being invoked rather than just the concept of rebirth in general.

English: the six directions; the whole universe
Notes: 六 liù + 合 hé (to unite; union). The four compass directions plus up and down, hence the three-dimensional totality of space, the entire cosmos.

English: six-six, all goes smoothly — a wish for things to go well
Notes: 六六 (six-six) + 大顺 (great smoothness). A set blessing built on the homophony of 六 liù with 流 liú (to flow) and the auspicious 顺 shùn (smooth, unobstructed). Said at weddings, openings, and new beginnings to wish that everything proceed without obstacle.

nature culture virtue confucianism aesthetics royalty classical

Notes: 六 liù + 亲 qīn (relative; kin). The six categories of close relatives (variously listed: father, mother, elder and younger brothers, wife, children, in some reckonings). In practice 六亲 means one's close family as a whole.
The sixty-year cycle: the combination of twelve animals with ten Heavenly Stems, the basic unit of traditional Chinese time reckoning.

English: the six arts of the Confucian gentleman
Notes: 六 liù + 艺 yì (art; skill). Rites (礼), music (乐), archery (射), charioteering (御), writing (书), and mathematics (数). The complete curriculum of the Zhou-dynasty gentleman, balancing civil and martial accomplishments.
六 liù + 月 yuè (month). June in the Gregorian calendar. Like all Chinese month names, it is simply the number plus 月, with no separate words for the months.

Tags: buddhism classics religion philosophy chan pure-land

English: the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch · ~20,000 characters · Tang dynasty
Notes: The only Chinese-authored Buddhist text designated a sutra. The recorded teachings of Huineng (惠能, 638-713 CE), the sixth patriarch of Chan and the founder of the Southern School.
Tags: buddhism classics religion philosophy chan pure-land

Notes: The awakening Wang Yangming experienced in 1508 while exiled to Longchang in Guizhou province. In the middle of the night, he grasped that the principles he had been seeking in external objects were already present in the mind itself , the insight that became the foundation of 心学.
Tags: wang-yangming neo-confucianism confucianism philosophy ethics human-nature knowing mind history ming

English: descendants of the dragon; heirs of the dragon civilization
Notes: 龙 lóng + 的 de (possessive marker) + 传人 chuánrén (one to whom something is transmitted; inheritor). The phrase reached mass consciousness through the 1978 song 龙的传人 by Taiwanese songwriter Hou Dejian 侯德健, recorded in 1980 and covered countless times since.

English: dragon and phoenix; the imperial pair; auspicious union of opposites
Notes: 龙 lóng + 凤 fèng (phoenix; 凤凰 fènghuáng). In classical Chinese cosmology, the dragon and phoenix are complementary opposites: 龙 is yang, male, the emperor, authority, and the power of water; 凤 is yin, female, the empress, grace, and the power of fire.

From 龙坞 Dragon Hollow near Hangzhou, Zhejiang. China's most famous green tea , flat-pressed leaves, clean chestnut aroma, and a 1,200-year history. Imperial tribute tea. 西湖龙井 Xī Hú Lóngjǐng (West Lake Dragon Well) is the protected-origin premium grade.

龙 lóng + 脉 mài (vein; pulse; channel). In feng shui 风水 theory, mountains are the visible backs of buried dragons; the ridgelines and peaks are the spine of a living creature moving through the earth. The 龙脉 are the underground channels through which this vital energy flows.
Tags: culture history science cosmology geography philosophy geomancy space

English: Dragon Gate — the grottoes; the legend of transformation
Notes: 龙 lóng + 门 mén (gate; door). Two distinct referents share this name. The historical Longmen Grottoes 龙门石窟 near Luoyang (Henan province) are a UNESCO World Heritage site: over 100,000 Buddhist statues carved into cliff faces along the Yi River, primarily during the Northern Wei and Tang dynasties.
龙 lóng + 年 nián (year). The Dragon is the fifth sign of the twelve-year zodiac cycle 生肖 shēngxiào and the only mythic creature among the twelve.

English: dragon robe; the emperor's ceremonial garment
Notes: 龙 lóng + 袍 páo (long robe). The emperor's official ceremonial dress, embroidered with nine five-clawed dragons on a yellow ground (yellow being the imperial color, reserved exclusively for the Son of Heaven).

English: dragon head; leader; industry frontrunner; water faucet
Notes: 龙 lóng + 头 tóu (head). Three active meanings in modern Chinese: (1) the dragon's literal head, (2) the leader or dominant player in an industry or organization (龙头企业 is the standard term for a market-leading company), and (3) a water faucet or tap, because classical bronze spigots were cast as a dra…

English: the Dragon Throne; the imperial seat
Notes: 龙 lóng + 椅 yǐ (chair; seat). The emperor's throne, elaborately carved with five-clawed dragons, in the Hall of Supreme Harmony 太和殿 of the Forbidden City in Beijing.

龙 (dragon) + 舟 (boat, the classical word for it; 船 chuán is more common in modern speech). The ornate long boat with a dragon head at the prow. 赛龙舟 (to race dragon boats) is the verb phrase. 龙舟竞渡 (lóngzhōu jìngdù) is the literary term for the race.

楼 (lóu, a building of multiple floors) plus 房. A building with stories stacked above ground, contrasted with the single-level 平房 (píngfáng). The everyday word for the apartment blocks of a modern Chinese city.

楼 lóu (building; storied structure; floor) + 上 shàng (above; up). The floor above; upstairs. 楼下 is the natural pair. These two form one of the most common directional pairs in everyday speech, used for apartments, offices, restaurants, and any multi-story space.

Notes: 路 (lù, road) + 灯 (lamp): the tall lights lining a street. They come on at dusk and mark the shape of the road after dark.

路 lù (road) + 口 kǒu (mouth, opening). The "mouth of the road," where roads meet and a choice opens. Used both literally (the intersection up ahead) and figuratively for any decision point: 人生的路口 rénshēng de lùkǒu (a crossroads in life).

旅 lǚ (to journey; a traveler) + 行 xíng. The standard word for travel as recreation or as an extended trip. Distinguished from 出差 chūchāi (business travel) and 旅游 lǚyóu (tourism, sightseeing). 一次愉快的旅行 "a pleasant trip."

旅行 lǚxíng (to travel) + 社 shè (agency). The business that arranges trips, tours, and tickets: 跟旅行社报名 "to sign up through a travel agency," 旅行社的导游 "the agency's tour guide." A textbook example of the agency sense of 社 attached to a whole two-syllable field word.

English: regulated verse — the Tang's dominant poetic form
Notes: The eight-line regulated poem: fixed tonal pattern, mandatory parallelism in the middle two couplets (对仗 duìzhàng), and strict rhyme scheme. An eight-line poem in five-character lines (五言律诗 wǔyán lǜshī) or seven-character lines (七言律诗 qīyán lǜshī).

Notes: In a large family of four-character expressions, 八 pairs with another number (most often 七) to mean "of all sorts, every which way," not a literal count: 七嘴八舌 (everyone talking at once), 四面八方 (from all directions), 七上八下 (agitated).
轮 (wheel) + 船 (boat): the wheel is the paddle wheel of the first steamers, so the word came to mean any large engine-driven ship. Today it is the everyday term for a big passenger or cargo liner.

English: a paper; a thesis; a dissertation
Notes: 论 + 文 wén (writing, text). A formal academic argument in writing: a journal paper, a term paper, a graduate thesis. 毕业论文 bìyè lùnwén "graduation thesis," 发表论文 fābiǎo lùnwén "to publish a paper."

Notes: Geomantic compass: a multi-ring instrument centered on a magnetic needle, encoding the eight trigrams, Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches, 24 solar term directions, 28 lunar mansions, and multiple other cosmological correspondence systems in concentric rings.

Notes: Gongs and drums: the percussion ensemble that provides the rhythmic foundation of Peking Opera and cues entrances, emotional intensification, and combat sequences.

English: to be completed (of a building); inauguration
Notes: 落 luò (to settle) + 成 chéng (to complete, to become). Used specifically for the completion of a building or major construction project. 落成典礼 = inauguration ceremony.

English: to fail the examination; to be rejected from the list
Notes: Literally "to fall from the notice board": 第 refers to the ranked list of successful candidates posted publicly after each examination. To fail was to have your name absent from that list.

Notes: 落 luò + 后 hòu (behind). To lag behind others in a race, in development, or in progress. Used in sports, economics, and social commentary. Carries a normative weight , something that has fallen behind should catch up.

English: to settle in (a place); to find lodging; to come to rest
Notes: 落 luò (to fall; to land) + 脚. To set the foot down after travel , to find a place to stay, to settle in temporarily or permanently. 在北京落脚 "to settle in Beijing" (especially as a newcomer); 落脚点 luòjiǎodiǎn "a place to settle, a foothold."

English: to implement; to pin down; to make concrete
Notes: 落 luò (to land) + 实 shí (solid, real, concrete). To take something from the abstract and make it real , to land on a decision, confirm a plan, carry out a policy. One of the most important governance and management words in Chinese.

English: to fall; to drop behind; to be left behind
Notes: Two distinct pronunciations with different meanings. luò xià = to fall downward (rain falling, price falling). là·xia (neutral tone) = to fall behind, to leave something behind by accident: 把钥匙落下了 "left the keys behind."

English: Mazu — goddess of the sea, protector of sailors
Notes: A historical woman named Lin Mo (林默, 960–987 CE) from Fujian Province who died young and was venerated as a protector of fishermen. Over centuries, the imperial court awarded her progressively higher titles, and she was absorbed into the Daoist pantheon.

Notes: Numbing-spicy , the characteristic flavor combination of Sichuan cuisine, combining the numbing sensation (麻 má) of Sichuan pepper (花椒 huājiāo) with the heat (辣 là) of chili pepper. The geographic signature of the Sichuan basin's isolated, humid interior.

Notes: 马 (horse) + 车 (cart, vehicle). The literal horse-and-cart, the carriage that ran on the 马路 long before engines.
马 (horse) + 虎 (tiger). A folk tale tells of a painter who drew a creature half horse, half tiger and could not say which it was; the slapdash beast gave its name to careless, half-attentive work.

Notes: 马 (horse) + 力 (power, force). A loan-translation of "horsepower," the unit that measures an engine in horses, keeping the animal alive inside the machine that replaced it.

马 mǎ (horse) + 路 lù (road). Originally "horse road," wide and packed enough to take horse traffic, in contrast with footpaths. In modern usage 马路 is the standard word for a paved urban street, especially one with vehicle traffic. Crossing it: 过马路 guò mǎlù.

Notes: 马 mǎ (horse) + 上 shàng (on top of; mounted on). Literally "on horseback," from the military image of an order being carried out while still mounted, without dismounting. One of the most common adverbs in spoken Mandarin.

Notes: Buy + not + shoulder. Distinct from 买不到 (can't get one: sold out) , the two negatives diagnose different tragedies, wallet versus supply chain.

Transactional and decisional verbs with 了 are extremely common in everyday conversation. The completion is commercially and practically significant , the item has been acquired, the deal is done, the decision has been executed.

English: meshrep — the traditional Uyghur community gathering
Notes: 麦西热甫 màixīrèfǔ (meshrep, from Persian/Turkic mäshrip meaning "gathering place") is the traditional Uyghur social institution: a community assembly that brings people together for music, dance, storytelling, comedy, and the resolution of social disputes through a combination of festivity and collecti…
满 mǎn (full) + 意 yì (heart; wish). The heart filled to its wish, hence satisfied: 对结果很满意 "very pleased with the result." Its opposite is 不满 bùmǎn, dissatisfied.

English: the one-month celebration for a newborn
Notes: 满 mǎn (full; complete) + 月 yuè (month). When a baby has survived its first full month , historically the most dangerous period , the family celebrates with red eggs (红鸡蛋 hóng jīdàn), gifting of gold jewelry, and a feast. The custom signals that the child is likely to thrive.

满 (mǎn, full; filled to capacity) + 足 (sufficient). Completely sufficient: fulfillment, contentment, the state of having enough and knowing it. Both a verb (满足需求, to satisfy a need) and an adjective (感到很满足, to feel deeply satisfied).

Reduplication of 慢 to form an adverb of manner. 慢慢 implies an unhurried pace that unfolds naturally over time, without pressure. Warmer in register than 慢慢地 (the version with the adverbial particle 地), though both are standard.

English: walks slowly — reduplicated adverb + 地 + verb
Notes: 地 links a manner adverb or adverbial phrase to the verb it modifies. It always sits between the adverb and the verb. The adverb answers "how?" the action is performed. Reduplication of adjectives to form adverbs + 地 is extremely common and productive: 慢慢地, 快快地, 轻轻地, 安静地.

慢 màn (slow) + 性 xìng (nature, character, disposition). "Of a slow nature." The medical term for chronic conditions, contrasted with 急性 jíxìng (acute, sudden-onset). 慢性病 mànxìngbìng = chronic illness. 慢性子 mànxíngzi = a person with a slow, unhurried temperament (slightly pejorative; see note).

English: walk slowly — polite farewell to a departing guest
Notes: 慢 màn (slow) + 走 zǒu (to walk; to leave). Literally "walk slowly" , said by a host as a guest departs, equivalent to "take care" or "safe travels." The Chinese farewell phrase, so common it has become almost automatic. The literal meaning (don't rush away) has calcified into pure social courtesy.
漫 màn (free; unrestrained) + 画 huà (drawing). A free, sketchy drawing: the word for comics and cartoons. The same two characters name Japanese manga, where they are read manga.

盲 (blind) + 目 (eye). An intensified compound where both characters carry the same meaning: acting as though blind, without seeing the situation clearly. 盲目乐观 mángmù lèguān means "blindly optimistic"; 盲目跟风 means to follow trends without thinking.
毛 máo (hair; fur) + 笔 bǐ. The classic soft-tipped brush of calligraphy and ink painting, named for the animal hair of its tuft. The tool that gives Chinese writing its living, varying line.
