Notes: 文化 (culture) + 交流 jiāoliú (exchange, mutual flow). The official term for cultural diplomacy programs, art exhibitions, study exchanges, and any organized cross-cultural contact. 中美文化交流 (Sino-American cultural exchange) covers everything from touring orchestras to academic partnerships.

文化 (culture) + 遗产 yíchǎn (legacy, inheritance , 遗 left-behind + 产 property/birth). The inherited deposit of past civilization. 世界文化遗产 (World Cultural Heritage, UNESCO designation) is a major category of Chinese public pride.

文化 (culture) + 自信 (self-confidence). Belief in the value of one's own cultural tradition without need for external validation. 文 wén (writing; text) + 件 jiàn (a piece). A written document, an official paper, or a computer file. The word covers both physical paperwork and digital files: on a screen, 文件 is exactly the word for a file, and 文件夹 wénjiànjiā is a folder.

English: literati — the scholarly class who cultivated the guqin

文人 wénrén (literatus; cultivated scholar-official) + 画 huà (painting). The tradition of painting as personal cultivation and self-expression rather than as commissioned craft. Theorized by Su Shi 苏轼 and Mi Fu 米芾 in the Northern Song, dominant from the Yuan onward.

文 wén (writing; culture; pattern) + 学 xué (learning). The discipline of literature , both the creative output (novels, poetry, essays) and the scholarly study of it. 文学家 wénxuéjiā = writer, literary figure. 中国文学 = Chinese literature. 古典文学 = classical literature. 现代文学 = modern literature.

Notes: 文 wén (writing; written form) + 言 yán (speech; language) + 文 wén (text). The written form of classical spoken Chinese, crystallized in the pre-Han period and used as the literary and official written standard for approximately 2,000 years.

English: my book — possessive pronoun + 的 + noun
Notes: 的 marks possession and belonging: pronoun or noun + 的 + noun. This is structurally identical to the adjective pattern , the modifier always comes before 的 which always precedes the noun.

English: What I mean is	What I mean is." Used to clarify when you sense you have been misunderstood, or to preface a more careful restatement of your point. Roughly equivalent to English "what I'm trying to say is…"

I feel or "I think." The default opinion frame in spoken Chinese. Softer than 我认为 (wǒ rènwéi, "I hold the view that"), which is the more formal written-register equivalent. 我觉得 carries no special weight; it is the natural way to introduce any personal take.

Notes: 来 and 去 can be followed directly by a verb of purpose: "come/go in order to do [V]." This is structurally simple: 来/去 + verb phrase. The motion establishes the direction; the following verb specifies the purpose of the trip. This is one of the most frequent patterns in everyday speech.

English: I understand now; I get it (I have entered a state of understanding)
Notes: State-change verbs like 明白 (understand), 知道 (know), 懂 (grasp), 累 (tired), 饿 (hungry), 高兴 (happy) pair powerfully with sentence-final 了. The 了 marks the entry into that state , the moment the change occurs. Before: didn't understand. After: understands.

Pinyin: wǒ shì zài Běijīng chūshēng de

English: I want the red one — 的 stands alone as nominal
Notes: When the noun after 的 is already understood from context, it can be dropped , leaving 的 to function as a standalone noun phrase meaning "the one(s) that are X." This is the nominalizing function of 的, productive across all the adjective and clause patterns above.

English: I feel the same way or "I think so too

卧 (wò, to lie down) plus 房. The room for sleeping. In everyday speech 卧室 (wòshì) is now more common, but 卧房 survives and shows the same logic: the chamber where one lies down.

屋 (wū, room, building) + 里 (interior). The most domestic use of 里 , the interior of the dwelling, the warm and enclosed space against the outdoors. 屋里人 (wūlǐ rén, the person inside the room) was a classical and regional euphemism for one's wife , the person who keeps the interior.

Notes: 屋 wū + 子 zi (nominalization suffix). The colloquial word for a room or the interior of a small house. Warmer and more intimate than 房间. Used in everyday spoken Chinese for the space one actually lives in.

Notes: May Fourth Movement: the intellectual and cultural movement sparked by student protests on May 4, 1919, against the terms of the Treaty of Versailles. It catalyzed demands for science and democracy, rejection of Confucian tradition, and the development of a new vernacular literature.

English: the five flavors — sour, bitter, sweet, pungent, salty
Notes: 五 wǔ (five) + 味 wèi (flavor, taste). Sour 酸 suān (Wood/Liver), bitter 苦 kǔ (Fire/Heart), sweet 甘 gān (Earth/Spleen), pungent/spicy 辛 xīn (Metal/Lung), salty 咸 xián (Water/Kidney). Each flavor enters and supports its corresponding organ system in moderate amounts; in excess, it taxes it.

English: the Five-Starred Red Flag (flag of the PRC)
Notes: 五 wǔ + 星 xīng (star) + 红旗 hóngqí (red flag). The national flag of the People's Republic of China: one large star surrounded by four smaller ones on a red field.

English: the five phases; the five agents
Notes: 五 wǔ + 行 xíng (to move; phase; agent). Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water, understood as five phases of cyclical change rather than fixed substances. The generating cycle (相生) runs Wood feeds Fire, Fire makes Earth (ash), Earth bears Metal, Metal carries Water, Water nourishes Wood.

English: the five yin organ systems — heart, liver, spleen, lung, kidney
Notes: 五 wǔ (five) + 脏 zàng (solid, yin, storing organ). In TCM, 五脏 refers to five functional systems, not five anatomical organs in the Western sense. Heart (心 xīn) , Fire; Liver (肝 gān) , Wood; Spleen (脾 pí) , Earth; Lung (肺 fèi) , Metal; Kidney (肾 shèn) , Water.

Notes: Stage combat: the acrobatic fighting sequences of martial opera. Also used colloquially for action-movie fight choreography.

Notes: 武 wǔ (martial; military) + 功 gōng (skill). Skill in the martial arts, the trained fighting ability central to wuxia fiction and film. 武功高强 = of formidable martial skill. 一身武功 = a whole body of fighting skill. The word also has a classical sense of military accomplishment, the deeds that win wars.

Notes: 武 wǔ (martial) + 力 lì (force, power). Force exercised through arms, the option of compulsion by military means as opposed to negotiation: 使用武力 "to use force," 武力解决 "to resolve by force." A neutral, often institutional word for the state's capacity to wage war.

English: the martial forest; the community of martial artists
Notes: 武 wǔ (martial) + 林 lín (forest). The metaphor is ecological: martial arts practitioners form a dense, interconnected ecosystem , as complex and competitive as a forest, with dominant trees, understory growth, and constant struggle for light and resources.

武 wǔ (martial) + 器 qì (implement, tool). The weapon itself, from a single blade to a nation's arsenal: 核武器 "nuclear weapons," 武器装备 "weaponry and equipment." Figuratively, any decisive instrument: 知识是有力的武器 "knowledge is a powerful weapon."

One of the most famous heroes, celebrated for killing a man-eating tiger on Jingyang Ridge with his bare hands, drunk. Upright and ferocious, he later avenges his murdered brother and is driven by repeated injustice into outlawry.

Notes: 武 wǔ (martial) + 侠 xiá (a chivalrous knight-errant). The genre of stories about wandering martial heroes bound by honour and loyalty: 武侠小说 "martial-arts fiction," 武侠片 "a martial-arts film." A vast and beloved tradition in Chinese popular culture, peopled by swordsmen who right wrongs outside the rea…

Notes: 武 wǔ (martial) + 勇 yǒng (brave, courageous). Bravery of the martial kind, valour in combat: the courage of a warrior who is both skilled and fearless. A more literary word than the everyday 勇敢, weighting the bravery specifically toward fighting and the battlefield.

武 wǔ (martial) + 装 zhuāng (to equip, to fit out). As a verb, to arm or equip with weapons; as an adjective, armed; as a noun, an armed force: 武装部队 "armed forces," 武装冲突 "armed conflict." Also figurative: 用知识武装头脑 "to arm the mind with knowledge."

English: the transformation of things — all things are in constant change
Notes: 物 wù (things; beings) + 化 huà (to transform, change). The final concept named in the butterfly dream passage: "Between Zhuang Zhou and the butterfly there must necessarily be a gap, and this is called the transformation of things 物化." All distinctions, including the distinction between self and othe…
物 (goods, things) + 价 (price). The general price level of everyday goods across a market or city. The word that shows up in talk of inflation and the cost of living.

Notes: 物 wù (thing; matter) + 理 lǐ (principle). Literally "the principles of things," the modern name for physics. A clear case of 理 meaning the lawful pattern running through the physical world.

Notes: 物 wù (thing) + 品 pǐn (article; kind). The formal word for goods or articles, the kind you see on a shipping label or in a store inventory: 贵重物品 "valuable items," 日用物品 "everyday articles."

Notes: 物 wù (thing) + 体 tǐ (body). A physical object regarded as a body occupying space, the term used in physics and plain description alike: 不明飞行物 "an unidentified flying object."
物 wù (thing) + 质 zhì (substance). Matter in the scientific sense, and the material as opposed to the spiritual: 化学物质 "a chemical substance," 物质需求 "material needs."
Frames a disagreement as a communication gap rather than bad faith, which lets the other side correct course without losing face. Use it even when you suspect it was no accident.

误 wù (to err; by mistake) + 解 jiě. To take a thing apart wrongly. To read a meaning incorrectly, or the wrong reading itself: 产生误解 = a misunderstanding arises; 消除误解 = clear up a misunderstanding. The 误 marks the comprehension as faulty, the inverse of a clean 理解.

Notes: Smog: fog plus the revived haze character 霾. 今天有雾霾，戴口罩 was the 2010s urban parent's daily instruction; 蓝天 is its cheerful antonym.
夕 xī (dusk; evening) + 阳 yáng (sun). The low sun of late day. By extension 夕阳 marks anything in graceful decline: 夕阳产业 "a sunset industry," the mirror of the 朝阳 sunrise one.

English: A medial exclamatory or rhythmic particle characteristic of Chu poetry, appearing within lines to create a pause and an emotional breath. It has no precise lexical meaning but gives the 楚辞 style its distinctive incantatory rhythm. Untranslatable; sometimes rendered as "ah" or simply omitted.

Notes: 西 (western) + 餐 (meal, cuisine). As opposed to 中餐 zhōngcān (Chinese food). In Chinese urban culture, 西餐厅 (Western restaurant) typically means a European-style restaurant with table settings, bread, and fork-and-knife service.

English: the West; western direction; Pure Land (Buddhist)
Notes: 西 (west) + 方 (direction; region). The context determines which of the three senses is meant: cosmological/Buddhist (the Pure Land), historical-geographic (Western Regions), or modern geopolitical (the liberal West). When paired with 东方, it is almost always the modern cultural/civilizational sense.

Notes: 西 (west) plus 湖 (lake): the storied lake at Hangzhou, ringed by causeways and pagodas, the most painted and most quoted lake in Chinese poetry.

English: rinsing the tea — the first discard infusion

Notes: 洗 (to wash) + 脸 (face). The first ritual of the morning. A verb-object pair, so you can split it: 洗个脸 (xǐ ge liǎn), to give the face a quick wash.

English: to love; to be fond of; to favor
Notes: 喜 xǐ (to delight in) + 爱 ài (to love). A warmer, more literary cousin of 喜欢, often used of things admired or cherished: 深受喜爱 "deeply loved (by the public)," 喜爱的作家 "a favorite author."
Tags: emotion culture family characters vocabulary feeling daily-life

English: a liking; a preference; to be keen on
Notes: 喜 xǐ (to like) + 好 hào (to be fond of, 4th tone). Both a verb and a noun for a settled preference or taste: 个人喜好 "personal preferences," 喜好读书 "fond of reading." Note 好 here is hào, not hǎo.

English: a festive air; an atmosphere of joy
Notes: 喜 xǐ (joy) + 气 qì (air, mood). The bright, celebratory atmosphere of a happy occasion, the feeling in a room hung with red: 满屋喜气 "the whole house full of festive joy."

English: happy money — cash gifts at joyous occasions

Notes: Auspicious, festive: the quality of being celebratory and lucky. Red is described as 喜庆 by default; white and black are explicitly not 喜庆 in gift or festive contexts.

A "joyful funeral": the death of a person who lived to old age and left many descendants. Treated as cause for celebration alongside mourning, and marked with comparatively festive elements: the music may be more exuberant, the occasion more public.
Tags: ritual social culture etiquette daily-life family symbolism

English: a happy occasion; a joyous event; (esp.) a wedding
Notes: 喜 xǐ (joy) + 事 shì (matter, affair). Any auspicious event, and by default a wedding. Its standing opposite is 丧事 sāngshì, a funeral, the unhappy event.
喜 xǐ (joy) + 悦 yuè (pleased). A literary, slightly elevated word for inner gladness, the quiet glow of a good thing: 丰收的喜悦 "the joy of a good harvest," 内心的喜悦 "the delight within."
Opera fan, literally "theatre-obsessive." The devoted fan who can sing along from memory, knows every role's vocal style, and has opinions about every major performer.

系 xì (string together) + 列 liè (row; to arrange). A run of related items strung in a row: 系列产品 "a product series," 一系列问题 "a whole series of problems." The connecting 系 makes the separate items read as one ordered set.
系 xì (connection) + 统 tǒng (to unify). An ordered whole of interworking parts: 操作系统 "operating system," 神经系统 "nervous system." As an adjective it means systematic: 系统地学习 "to study systematically."
Cell: fine wrap. 干细胞 (gànxìbāo) is a stem cell, and 细胞分裂 is cell division, vocabulary every 生物课 student recites before exams.

English: to finish work; to get off work; end of shift
Notes: 下 xià (to descend; to leave the higher platform) + 班 bān (shift; work roster). To come down from the work platform , to leave one's post at the end of the day. The indispensable pair of 上班. 下班后 (after work) is the default framing for evening activities in Chinese urban conversation.
Tags: direction grammar motion vocabulary daily-life society communication

English: to put in the work; to make a serious effort; to buckle down
Notes: 下 xià (to place; to put down) + 功夫 (effort/work). The verb phrase for serious, sustained investment of effort. The directional 下 is crucial: you are depositing effort into something, like placing a foundation. Not a momentary burst of energy but a committed, extended investment.

English: class is over; end of class; to dismiss class
Notes: 下 xià (to end; to come down from) + 课 kè (lesson; class). Class has descended from its height, releasing students and teacher. The verb pair 上课/下课 (class begins/class ends) is the daily rhythm of Chinese school life. 下课了！is the joyful announcement that class is over.

English: come down; slow to a stop
below; underneath; the lower surface; the following
Notes: 下 xià (below; under) + 面 miàn (face; side; surface). The underside; what is below. Used for physical position (床下面 = under the bed) and for discourse organization (下面请看 = please see the following).

下 xià (to come down; to fall) + 雪 xuě (snow). The standard way to say "it is snowing," built on the same 下 used for 下雨 (to rain). Chinese treats weather that falls from the sky as something the sky "sends down," so snow, rain, and frost all take 下.

下 xià (to descend; to fall from above) + 雨 yǔ (rain). Rain descending from the sky. The 下 construction extends to all precipitation: 下雪 (to snow), 下冰雹 (to hail). Notably, 下 is the standard verb for precipitation in Mandarin , not "fall" or "pour" but "descend." The sky issues weather downward.

English: it's raining now; it has started to rain
Notes: The canonical example of sentence-final 了 announcing a new situation. There is no past tense here , the rain is starting now, and the 了 signals a change of state has occurred or is occurring. This 了 carries the meaning: "now things are different from before."
To download: carry down. Paired with 上传 (upload). 载 also reads zǎi meaning "year" in classical texts, a polyphone trap for advanced readers.

下 xià (next; the following) + 周 zhōu (week). The temporal use of 下: what descends next into the present from the future. Consistent across all time units: 下周 (next week), 下个月 (next month), 下年 / 明年 (next year).

English: to scare away; to frighten off
Notes: 吓 (xià, to frighten) + 跑. A V+跑 resultative: the action of frightening produces the result of running off. Highly productive pattern: 赶跑 gǎnpǎo (chase off), 撵跑 niǎnpǎo (drive off), 骂跑 màpǎo (scold off). The construction packages cause and escape into one verb.

English: let some get rich first — permission for inequality as a stage
Notes: 先 (first, beforehand) + 富 (wealthy, to become rich) + 起来 (resultative complement indicating a process coming into effect). The condensed form of Deng's proposition: 让一部分人先富起来 (ràng yī bùfen rén xiān fù qǐlai, let some people get rich first).

先 xiān (first; ahead; earlier) + 生 shēng (one born; person). "One born earlier" , originally a teacher or Confucian master; now the standard polite term for "Mr." and also "husband" in formal contexts (我先生 "my husband"). A word whose meaning has drifted beautifully from teacher → gentleman → Mr.

Notes: 鲜 xiān (fresh) + 花 huā (flower). Living, fresh-cut blossoms, the flowers you buy and give: 一束鲜花 "a bouquet of fresh flowers." Distinct from 假花 jiǎhuā, artificial flowers.

鲜 xiān (fresh; vivid , the "umami" character, fish + sheep 鱼+羊) + 美 měi (beautiful; delicious). The compound for food that is both fresh and deeply flavorful. Note: 鲜 also contains the sheep radical 羊, linking back to 美's own etymology. Used for broths, seafood, and fresh ingredients.
显 xiǎn (visible, to show) + 然 rán (-ly). States that something is plain to see: 显然 he was lying. Often opens a sentence as a comment on the whole: 显然，这是个错误 "clearly, this is a mistake."

Notes: 县 xiàn (county) + 城 chéng (walled town). The administrative town at the center of a county, historically walled, the seat of the local magistrate.
现 xiàn (present) + 场 chǎng (site; field). The very place where something is happening: 案发现场 "the scene of a crime," 现场直播 "a live broadcast."

English: ready-made; off the shelf; already prepared
Notes: 现 xiàn (on hand) + 成 chéng (completed). Already finished and available, needing no further making: 现成的答案 "a ready-made answer," 现成的衣服 "off-the-rack clothing."

现代 xiàndài (modern; the modern era) + 化 huà (the -ize suffix). The textbook example of the 化 suffix at work: "to make modern." 现代化 is one of the central words of twentieth-century Chinese politics, most famously in 四个现代化 (the Four Modernizations: agriculture, industry, defense, science and technolog…

Notes: 现 xiàn (present; to appear) + 金 jīn (gold; money). Cash in hand, as opposed to digital payments, credit, or promises. 付现金 "to pay in cash." In a society where 微信支付 and 支付宝 (WeChat Pay and Alipay) dominate, 现金 is increasingly rare.

English: reality; actual; (of a person) realistic, practical
Notes: 现 xiàn (present) + 实 shí (real; solid). What is actually the case here and now, set against 理想 lǐxiǎng (the ideal). As an adjective for a person it can mean clear-eyed, or pointedly materialistic.
Filling: the stuffing inside the wrapper. The -r suffix is a Beijing-dialect feature that appears frequently in food vocabulary.

English: homesickness; nostalgia for one native place
Notes: 乡 xiāng (native place; hometown; rural area) + 愁 chóu (sorrow; melancholy; anxiety). The specific emotional register of Double Ninth as a festival: not grief for the dead (清明节), not fear of wandering spirits (中元节), but the longing of those separated from home by distance.

Notes: Zodiac conflict: signs that are diametrically opposite in the twelve-year cycle and considered incompatible. The Rat-Horse conflict, the Tiger-Monkey conflict, etc.

English: to get along; to spend time together
Notes: 相 xiāng (each other) + 处 chǔ (to dwell; to be with). To live alongside or get along with others: 容易相处 "easy to get along with," 相处了很多年 "spent many years together."

相 xiāng (mutual) + 克 kè (to conquer, to regulate, to check). In the Five Phases context, 克 means disciplined control rather than destruction , the river bank that contains the flood, not the dam that annihilates the water.
Tags: wuxing five-phases cosmology philosophy tcm nature yin-yang history ancient

English: to be linked; to be connected to each other
Notes: 相 xiāng (mutually; each other) + 连 lián (to link). To be mutually joined, used when two or more things are connected to one another rather than one connecting the other. Common in describing geography, anatomy, and abstract relations: lands that border each other, ideas that are bound together.
相 xiàng (appearance) + 片 piàn (a flat slice; sheet). The printed photograph as an object. Its everyday synonym 照片 zhàopiàn is equally common; both name the picture you hold or hang.

English: to meet a prospective marriage partner; a matchmaking meeting
Notes: 相 xiàng (to examine) + 亲 qīn (marriage; relative). The arranged meeting where two people look each other over with marriage in mind, often set up by family or a matchmaker. Note: this 相 keeps a level tone for many speakers, but the sense is the inspecting one.

相 xiāng (mutual, reciprocal) + 生 shēng (to give birth, to generate, to produce). Each phase nourishes and gives rise to the next; each is simultaneously "mother" to the phase it generates and "child" to the phase that generates it.
Tags: wuxing five-phases cosmology philosophy tcm nature yin-yang history ancient

Notes: 相 xiāng (mutually; each other) + 思 sī (to miss; to long for). The classical word for romantic yearning. 相思 is not a modern word , it carries centuries of weight from classical poetry.
相 xiāng (mutually) + 同 tóng (same). Two or more things being the same as each other: 完全相同 "exactly the same." More formal and written than the everyday 一样 yīyàng.
相 xiāng (mutual) + 信 xìn (trust). To place trust in someone or to believe a thing is so: 我相信你 "I trust you," 相信科学 "to believe in science." One of the most common verbs built on the mutual reading.

Fragrant herbs and beautiful women: the conventional shorthand for the allegorical system of the 楚辞, in which fragrant plants represent virtuous ministers and women represent the king who should (but does not) receive them.

Notes: 香 (fragrant) + 水 (water). Literally fragrant water, the modern word for bottled perfume. Measured with 瓶 (píng, bottle) or 滴 (dī, drop).
香 (fragrant) + 甜 (sweet). Of food, fragrant and sweet at once. By extension, of sleep, deep and contented, the way you sleep after a good meal.
香 (fragrant) + 味 (smell, flavor). The scent something gives off, especially of food or flowers. The everyday word for a good aroma.
香 (fragrant) + 烟 (smoke). The everyday word for a cigarette, named for the scented smoke it gives off. Counted with 支 (zhī, stick) or 包 (bāo, pack).

English: the Xiang Army — Zeng Guofan's force
to respond to; to answer (a call); response
Notes: 响 xiǎng (to sound, to echo) + 应 yìng (to respond). To answer a call or appeal, often a collective one: 响应号召 (respond to a call), 积极响应 (respond actively). The image is of an echo answering a sound.

English: to think of; to occur to; to realize
Notes: 想 xiǎng (to think; to consider) + 到 dào (arrive). Thinking that arrived at an idea: the thought reached its destination. 想到 implies the idea arrived in mind, often unexpectedly or after searching.

想 xiǎng (to think) + 法 fǎ (method; approach; way). The product of thinking: what thinking produces when it runs long enough. Used freely for ideas, opinions, views, and intentions. 你有什么想法？ is one of the most common ways to ask for someone's opinion in meetings and conversations.

English: to be homesick; to miss home
Notes: 想 xiǎng (to miss) + 家 jiā (home; family; household). The heart facing home from a distance. A verb in Chinese where English uses an adjective ("homesick").

English: to miss someone; to long for; to think of fondly
Notes: 想 xiǎng (to think of; to miss) + 念 niàn (to think of; to recite; to hold in mind). Two overlapping words for mental attending-to, doubled for emphasis: 念 carries the connotation of something repeated, recurring, kept alive by repetition, the way a prayer or a name is recited.
Tags: mind memory buddhism mindfulness recitation emotion philosophy

English: to recall; to call to mind

Notes: 想 xiǎng (to think) + 象 xiàng (image; likeness; elephant , 象 was borrowed for "image" because of its visual suggestiveness: the elephant is the largest thing you picture). Think-image: to form mental images of things not present. Used as both a verb (to imagine) and a noun (imagination).

想 xiǎng (want; think) + 要 yào (want; need; will). The two wanting words stacked for explicitness or emphasis. Where 想 alone can be tentative (I'd like to; I'm thinking of), 想要 is more direct and pointed. Used when desire is clear and conscious rather than a vague inclination.

English: always (up to now); from the start; hitherto
Notes: 向 xiàng (facing back along) + 来 lái (coming up to now). A close synonym of 一向, slightly more literary: 他向来诚实 "he has always been honest." Frames a quality as having held from the beginning to the present.
向 xiàng (toward) + 前 qián (front). Directed at the space ahead: 向前走 "walk forward," 向前看 "look ahead," both literally and in the sense of looking to the future rather than dwelling on the past.
Tags: direction time philosophy grammar space motion meaning characters

English: to yearn for; to long for; to look forward to
Notes: 向 xiàng (toward) + 往 wǎng (to go toward). The heart facing a place or life it longs for: 向往自由 "to yearn for freedom," 向往美好的生活 "to long for a good life." Warmer and more aspirational than plain "to want."

English: facing the sun; sunny (of an aspect)
Notes: 向 xiàng (toward; facing) + 阳 yáng (sun). Oriented toward the sun, said of a room, window, or slope that gets good light. A 向阳的房间 is a sought-after sunny room.

向 (toward; in the direction of) + 右 (right). The standard directional command for turning right: 向右转 (turn right), 向右走 (go right). As with its mirror pair 向左, used in navigation, military drill, physical education, and any instruction involving directional movement.

向 (toward; in the direction of) + 左 (left). The standard instruction for turning or moving left: 向左转 (turn left), 向左走 (go left, walk left). Used in navigation, traffic directions, dance instruction, and any context requiring directional movement.

English: to resemble; to be like; such as
Notes: A verb meaning "to resemble, to be like." The basic frame is A 像 B ("A is like B"), asserting likeness rather than identity. It powers similes in the frame A 像 B 一样 + Adj/Verb ("A is just like B"). 像 also introduces examples, "such as / like" (像…这样的, "things like…").

English: to digest; to absorb (food, or by extension, information)
Notes: 消 xiāo (to dissolve; to dissipate; to consume) + 化 huà (to transform). The verb for digestion: food broken down and turned into something the body can absorb. 化 again names the physical turning of one substance into another.

English: Theravada — the Lesser Vehicle (pejorative Mahayana term)

Notes: Small cleverness: the shortcut-finding wit that games the rule and misses the point. 耍小聪明 (deploying petty cleverness) is what teachers accuse corner-cutting students of; its grown-up antonym is 大智慧, great wisdom.

English: this humble younger brother (self-deprecating first person)
Notes: Used by a male speaker to refer to himself deferentially, regardless of birth order. The formula downsizes the speaker relative to the listener. Also used literally for a younger brother. In gangster/triad contexts, 小弟 means a low-ranking follower , the hierarchy is explicit.
小 (xiǎo, small) + 狗. The everyday word for a puppy or any small dog. 小狗 is warm and affectionate, the term a child reaches for first.

小 xiǎo (small) + 孩 hái (child). The standard neutral word for a child. Related: 小朋友 xiǎopéngyou (young friend , the standard address for children, used by teachers and adults), 小孩子 xiǎoháizi (a slightly more affectionate variant with the diminutive 子).

Notes: 小 (xiǎo, small) + 鸡 (chicken). The fluffy yellow chick just out of the shell, a favorite in children's songs and picture books.

A father's way of referring to his daughter when speaking to someone of higher status. The 小 does not mean the daughter is young or small , it encodes the father's self-positioning as lesser. Compare 犬子 quǎnzǐ (my unworthy son , lit. "dog son"), the parallel self-deprecating term for sons.
Small qi: a constricted spirit, tight with money and with grace. The direct opposite is 大方 (dàfang, generous, poised). Milder than 小人; a friend can be teased as 小气 and remain a friend.

小 xiǎo (small) + 时 shí (time; hour). A small slice of time: one hour. The compound reflects a traditional view of time's granularity , the hour as the smallest standard unit. Contrast 小时候 xiǎoshíhou (childhood, "when one was small"), where 小时 carries the older sense of "young age."

Notes: 小 xiǎo (small; minor) + 说 shuō (speech; theory). Literally "minor talk" , the genre of fiction was long considered a lower form of literature compared to history and philosophy. The term was coined to contrast with 大道 "the Great Way" of classical learning.

English: small room; cabin; cottage; little shelter

小 xiǎo (small) + 心 xīn (heart; mind). A small heart is one drawn in, watchful, attentive to fine detail. The literal image captures the bodily experience of caution: the heart pulling back, contracting, alert to what is delicate or dangerous.

Notes: Small heart-aperture: a mind with a narrow gate, through which slights enter easily and never leave. The grudge-keeping cousin of 小气, aimed at temperament rather than wallet.

笑 xiào (laugh) + 话 huà (speech; words). Laugh-words: a joke, a funny story. As a verb it flips to "to laugh at, to make a fool of." 讲笑话 = to tell a joke; 闹笑话 = to make an embarrassing blunder that others laugh at.

English: smiling face; a smile worn for others
Notes: 笑 (laugh, smile) + 脸 (face). A face shaped into a smile, especially the welcoming one you put on for guests or customers. The opposite expression is 板着脸 (bǎnzhe liǎn), to hold the face stiff and stern.

Notes: 笑 xiào (to smile; to laugh) + 容 róng (facial expression). The smile as a look worn on the face, treated as a noun: something one has, shows, or loses. Where 笑 is the act of smiling, 笑容 is the expression itself, the way the face holds a smile.

English: said with a smile; said, smiling
Notes: The canonical attendant circumstance: 笑着 (smiling) + 说 (to say). The 着 links the two actions , the smiling frames and accompanies the speaking. This construction is the default way to describe facial expression or gesture accompanying speech in Chinese narrative.

English: to rest one's feet (during a journey); to take a break en route
Notes: 歇 xiē (to rest) + 脚. The classic verb for stopping during a long walk or trip , at a tea-house, an inn, a roadside pavilion. Carries the texture of pre-modern travel; still used for any pause on a long journey.

Notes: 写 xiě (to write; to depict) + 真. To depict the real. Originally a classical term for a lifelike portrait painting; in modern usage, a posed portrait photo (especially of a model or celebrity). In Japanese, the same word 写真 shashin simply means "photograph."

English: to write characters; to write by hand
Notes: 写 xiě (to write) + 字 zì (character). The fundamental literacy act: hand meeting surface, character taking form. Specifically implies handwriting rather than typing or printing. In Chinese civilization, handwriting is never merely functional.

English: in one's heart; in one's mind; emotionally
Notes: 心 (heart, mind) + 里 (interior). Functions as a locative: something is in the heart, occurs in the heart. Covers both cognitive interior (I understand in my mind) and emotional interior (I feel in my heart). More intimate and less clinical than 内心 nèixīn (inner heart , a literary register).

English: sincere words; what one truly means
Notes: 心里 (inside the heart) + 话 (speech, words). The words that come from the interior rather than from performance. Sharing 心里话 is an act of trust and intimacy , it signals that the speaker is not managing their presentation but revealing what is actually held inside.

English: to have a clear grasp; to know what's what
Notes: 心里 (inside the heart) + 有 (to have) + 数 (numbers, a count). To hold the numbers privately in one's interior , to have a clear reckoning of a situation that one carries internally.
心 xīn (heart) + 理 lǐ (logic; principle; grain of wood). "The logic of the heart." Used both as the general term for one's psychological state and as the root of 心理学 (psychology as a discipline).

心 xīn (heart) + 情 qíng (emotion; situation). The weather of the inner world. Where 情 alone is broad, covering emotion, circumstance, and romantic feeling, 心情 focuses it: the specific emotional atmosphere a person inhabits right now. It fluctuates by the hour.

English: thoughts; mental energy; what the mind is occupied with
Notes: 心 xīn (heart) + 思 sī (to think; thought). What the heart is currently thinking about, or whether it has the mental space to think about something at all.
From passage 7. 挂碍 guà ài means hindrance or obstruction in the literal sense of something snagging or hooking. 心无挂碍 describes the mind that, having seen emptiness, has nothing left to snag on.

English: School of Mind; Wang Yangming's Neo-Confucian tradition
Notes: The Neo-Confucian tradition associated with Wang Yangming. Holds that 理 is not separate from the mind; the moral faculty 良知 is the ground of both knowledge and action.

English: wits; smarts; (also) intent, motive of the heart
Notes: 心 xīn (heart) + 眼. The eye of the heart , the inner faculty of judgment and quick-wittedness. 心眼多 xīnyǎn duō "to have many wits" (clever, calculating, or scheming, depending on tone). 心眼好 xīnyǎn hǎo "to have a good heart-eye" (kind-hearted, well-intentioned).

English: intention; goodwill; the feeling behind a gesture
Notes: 心 xīn (heart) + 意 yì (intention; meaning). The feeling or thought behind an action: the sincerity and warmth that a gift, gesture, or visit carries. Often used when downplaying the material value of what you have brought: 这只是一点心意 ("this is just a small token of my regard").

Notes: 心 xīn + 脏 zàng (internal organ, the biological sense; same character used in 器官, organs of the body). In modern Chinese, 心 alone almost never refers to the biological organ; that role belongs entirely to 心脏. The standalone 心 is always the conceptual, emotional, and cognitive heart.

English: hard, toilsome; thanks for your trouble
Notes: 辛 (xīn), pungent or laborious, pairs with 苦 (kǔ), bitter, to name effort that wears you down. As a set phrase it doubles as warm thanks: telling someone 辛苦了 acknowledges the toil they just put in for you.

Acknowledges effort someone made for you: picking you up at the station, preparing samples, staying late. Factory staff hear it constantly from managers and appreciate it from a buyer. Answer with 不辛苦 or 应该的 (yīnggāi de, "it's what I should do").

新华 Xīnhuá (New China, the name of the official news agency and many state institutions) + 字典. The most widely-sold book in Chinese history and the standard reference for mainland Chinese students since its first edition in 1953. Simple, portable, and comprehensive for modern literacy needs.

新 (new) + 婚 (hūn, marriage). Newly married , in the fresh state of the new relationship. 新婚快乐 (congratulations on the marriage , Happy Newlywed); 新婚夫妇 (newlywed couple); 新郎 xīnláng (groom , new-man) and 新娘 xīnniáng (bride , new-woman) are the standard terms for a wedding couple.

English: the new replacing the old; transition between old and new
Notes: 新 (new) + 旧 (old) + 交替 (jiāotì, to alternate; to replace one another in succession). The pairing of 新 and 旧 as a compound unit , 新旧 , appears constantly in Chinese: 新旧对比 (contrast between old and new), 新旧交融 (old and new blending together), 新旧矛盾 (conflict between old and new).

新 (new) + 年 (year). The new year , the most basic New Year compound, usable for both the Gregorian New Year (January 1) and the Chinese Lunar New Year. 新年快乐 (Happy New Year) and 新年好 (New Year greetings) are the standard phrases.

English: Happy New Year , literally "new year happy
Notes: Happy New Year , literally "new year happy." The standard greeting for the solar New Year (January 1). For Lunar New Year, 新春快乐 (xīnchūn kuàilè) or 恭喜发财 (gōngxǐ fācái, "congratulations and may you prosper") are more appropriate.

新 (new) + 鲜 (xiān, fresh , especially of food; vivid; rare). Fresh in the sensory sense: 新鲜蔬菜 (fresh vegetables), 新鲜空气 (fresh air). Also used for novel experiences: 对我来说这是个新鲜事物 (this is something new to me). 鲜 alone means fresh-vivid; 新鲜 combines freshness with newness.
信 (xìn, letter) plus 封 (the sealing/wrapper): the paper sleeve that closes around a letter. The most common everyday word built on 封.

信 xìn (trustworthy communication; word) + 号 hào (sign; designation; mark; sound used as a signal). A signal is a word that has been stripped of language and reduced to a reliable mark: it carries only its presence or absence, its strength or weakness, rather than semantic content.

信 xìn (letter; trust) + 件 jiàn (a piece). A collective, somewhat formal term for letters and written correspondence. A single letter is 一封信 (using 封 fēng); 信件 names the whole category of correspondence, the kind of word a post office or office form would use.

English: trust; to trust; to have confidence in
Notes: 信 xìn (trustworthiness; to trust) + 任 rèn (to appoint; to entrust; to allow , 任 carries the sense of delegating responsibility to someone). To trust is to appoint a person as worthy of reliance. 信任危机 xìnrèn wéijī = a crisis of trust (institutional or personal). 建立信任 jiànlì xìnrèn = to build trust.

Notes: 信 xìn (trustworthy word; communication) + 息 xī (breath; rest; news , 息 contains 自 zì, nose, over 心 xīn, heart: breath as the sign of life; by extension, news and tidings). A word that travels and carries meaning , information as a form of 信. 信息时代 xìnxī shídài = the information age.

English: creditworthiness; credit; trustworthiness in financial conduct
Notes: 信 xìn (trustworthiness) + 用 yòng (use; to use; practical application). Trustworthiness made actionable , the record of a person or institution reliably standing by its commitments. 信用卡 xìnyòng kǎ = credit card. 信用评级 xìnyòng píngjí = credit rating.
星 (star) + 期 (period): the star period, from the seven-luminary week. Days attach numbers: 星期三 is Wednesday. Asking the day is 今天星期几? , one of the few questions where 几 needs no measure word.

English: Star, in the affectionate reduplicated form used in speech and songs. Single 星 does the compounding work: 星空 (starry sky), 星系 (galaxy, "star system"), 星座 (constellation, and the zodiac sign small talk runs on).

星 + 座 (seat): the seats of the stars. In young urban small talk it means the Western zodiac sign: 你是什么星座的? has largely displaced asking one's Chinese zodiac animal among the under-forty, an ironic import given the antiquity of native Chinese astral lore.

Notes: 行 xíng + 动 dòng (to move). The general word for action , both as a verb (to take action) and as a noun (an action, an operation). Used in everything from personal life (我们应该立刻行动 "we should act at once") to police and military operations (军事行动 "military operation").

English: market quotation; the going rate; market conditions
Notes: 行 háng + 情 qíng (situation; circumstances). The state of the trade. The going prices, the market mood, the supply-and-demand conditions in a particular industry. 股市行情 = stock market quotes; 看行情 = "to watch the market"; 行情看涨 = "the market is bullish."

English: to do good deeds; to practice virtue
Notes: 行 xíng (to practice; to carry out) + 善 shàn (goodness). Goodness made active , not merely possessed as a quality but enacted as conduct. Appears equally in Confucian moral discourse and Buddhist merit accumulation.

Notes: 行 xíng + 为 wéi (to do; to act). What one does, framed as observable behavior. The clinical/formal noun used in psychology, law, and ethics , 行为艺术 "performance art," 犯罪行为 "criminal behavior," 不文明行为 "uncivilized behavior."

Notes: 行 háng + 业 yè (occupation; enterprise). The trade as a category. Used for entire industries: 教育行业 the education sector; 服务行业 the service industry; 各行各业 "every trade, every profession" (the standard phrase for "all walks of life").

English: walking, standing, sitting, lying down — enlightenment in every posture
Notes: The four bodily postures covering all of waking life. Chan's radical claim: enlightenment is not a special state achieved in meditation and then lost in ordinary life , it is the natural condition of mind, available in every action.

English: to form; to take shape; to come into being
Notes: 形 xíng + 成 chéng (to become; to complete). To shape-into-being. The all-purpose verb for something forming through a process: 形成习惯 form a habit; 形成共识 reach (form) a consensus; 逐渐形成 gradually take shape. Used constantly in writing about how systems, opinions, and conditions arise.

English: to describe; to characterize in words
Notes: 形 xíng + 容 róng (appearance; countenance). To give a thing its look in words. The verb for describing, especially feelings and impressions that resist plain statement. 难以形容 = hard to describe; 无法形容的美 = indescribable beauty.

English: form; format: the outward shape, as opposed to content
Notes: 形 xíng + 式 shì (pattern; format). The form or format of something, set against its 内容 nèiróng (content). 各种形式 = various forms; 形式上 = in form only, nominally. 形式主义 = formalism, prizing appearance over substance. Do not confuse with 形势 (the situation): see the 辨析 section above.

English: the situation; the lay of forces; circumstances
Notes: 形 xíng + 势 shì (momentum; force). The configuration of forces at a given moment, weightier than 情形. Used for politics, war, economy, and any contest of momentum: 国际形势 the international situation; 形势严峻 the situation is grim; 看清形势 read the situation clearly. Do not confuse with 形式 (form vs. content).

形 xíng + 体 tǐ (body). The body as form: the physical figure of a person, often in contexts of posture, dance, and bearing. 形体训练 = physical/figure training; 形体优美 = a graceful figure. This is the bodily branch of 形, where shape means the shape of a living body.

English: garment structure; the form category of a historical garment
shape: the outward form of a thing
Notes: 形 xíng + 状 zhuàng (state; appearance). The everyday word for the shape of a physical object: what outline it has, what it looks like. 奇怪的形状 = a strange shape; 各种形状 = all kinds of shapes. This is the first 形-word a learner meets.

Evocative image: the poetic mode in which a natural scene opens a poem and resonates emotionally with the human subject to follow without being a direct comparison. The most distinctively Chinese of the three classical poetic modes.

兴 (aroused spirit, the xìng reading) + 趣 (inclination, delight). 对…感兴趣 ("to feel interest toward") is the essential pattern: 我对中国历史很感兴趣. 兴趣班 are the after-school enrichment classes filling Chinese childhood weekends.

杏 xìng (apricot) + 仁 (kernel). The seed inside the apricot pit , the everyday Chinese word also used for almonds in modern usage (e.g. 杏仁奶 "almond milk"). In Chinese medicine, 苦杏仁 is a classical herb used to "moisten the lung and stop coughing."

Notes: 姓 xìng (surname) + 名 míng (given name). The formal term for a full name. Note: Chinese names are surname-first, given-name-second, the reverse of Western convention. 你叫什么名字？= "What is your name?" (informal, just the name). 请问您的姓名？= "May I ask your full name?" (formal).

Notes: 幸 xìng (fortunate; lucky; to survive) + 福 fú (blessing). The compound for subjective happiness and well-being , what you feel when life is going right. 幸福感 = sense of well-being. 幸福生活 = a happy life. One of the most searched Chinese words globally.

Notes: Formal "fortunate meeting," said with the handshake on first contact. Pairs naturally with 久仰 (jiǔyǎng, "I've long admired you") when you know the person by reputation. Plain 很高兴认识您 is never wrong.

性 xìng (sex) + 别 bié (distinction, category). The category of male or female: 性别平等 "gender equality," the 性别 field on an application form. The standard, neutral word in both everyday and formal contexts for the sex or gender of a person.

English: human nature is bad — innately insufficient for morality without cultivation
Notes: Xunzi's foundational claim: 人之性恶，其善者伪也, "Human nature is bad; what is good in humans is their deliberately cultivated achievement." 性 xìng: what one is born with. 恶 è: bad, harmful, insufficient. 伪 wèi: artificial, deliberately made (not fake). Goodness is real but must be built, not grown.

性 xìng (nature) + 格 gé (standard, frame). The settled set of traits that make up who a person is: 性格开朗 "an open, cheerful character," 性格内向 "an introverted personality." The standard word for someone's overall character, often the answer to "what kind of person are they."

Notes: 性 xìng (property) + 能 néng (capability). The functional properties of a machine, device, or material: 性能稳定 "stable performance," 高性能 "high-performance." How well a thing does what it is built to do, the practical measure of its inherent quality.

性 xìng (nature) + 情 qíng (feeling). Temperament considered through the lens of mood and emotional reaction: 性情温和 "of a gentle temperament," 性情大变 "a sharp change in temperament." Warmer and more feeling-laden than the neutral 性格, closer to the heart's weather than its frame.

English: elder and younger sibling — fraternal respect
Notes: 悌 tì , fraternal respect , is the virtue governing sibling relations. The elder brother owes kindness and example; the younger owes deference and respect.

English: to revise, to amend, to edit
Notes: 修 (mend, trim) + 改 (alter). To go back over a text, plan, or law and revise it. The standard word for editing a document or amending a draft.

English: to build/repair the Great Wall; (slang) to play mahjong
Notes: 修 (xiū) means to build, repair, or construct. 修长城 in its literal sense describes the labour of wall-building. In colloquial slang, 修长城 is a playful way to say "playing mahjong": the rows of mahjong tiles arranged on the table look like sections of wall.

Notes: 羞 xiū: shame (about one's own moral failures). 恶 wù: dislike, aversion (to moral failure in others). Together: the capacity to feel shame about one's own wrong actions and moral distaste for wrongdoing in general.

English: the lowest examination degree; a local scholar
Notes: The degree produced by the local examination (童试), the entry point of the examination ladder. A 秀才 had cleared the first hurdle and earned a recognized scholarly identity, but stood far from power.

English: open-minded; receptive; humble in one's willingness to learn
Notes: 虚 xū (empty; hollow; receptive , the vessel with space in it) + 心 xīn (heart; the seat of thought and feeling in Chinese understanding). An empty heart , a mind that has not pre-filled itself with conclusions and so can genuinely receive what it encounters.

English: to study with an open mind; to learn receptively
Notes: A fixed phrase in educational and developmental discourse. The combination of 虚心 (open-minded) + 学习 (to study; to learn) makes the stance toward learning explicit: approach the subject without assuming you already know, without defending existing positions, with the mind empty enough to receive new…

English: to need; to require (necessity, not merely desire)
Notes: 需 xū (to need; to require, a more formal or objective necessity) + 要. 需要 focuses on objective need rather than personal desire. 我需要帮助 (I need help , genuinely require it) vs. 我要帮助 (I want help , requesting it).

English: to publicize; to promote; publicity; propaganda
Notes: 宣 xuān (to proclaim) + 传 chuán (to spread). To put out a message deliberately so it reaches the public: 宣传海报 "a promotional poster," 宣传活动 "a publicity campaign." Carries a sense of organized, purposeful spreading, and in political contexts the meaning of propaganda.

English: to read out formally (a statement, verdict, decree)
Notes: 宣 xuān (to announce; to proclaim) + 读. To read aloud in a formal setting , a court verdict, a wedding vow, an official document at a ceremony. The 宣 marks the public, declarative force.

English: Xuan paper, made in Jingxian, Anhui province
Notes: Xuan paper, made in Jingxian, Anhui province. The standard for Chinese calligraphy and painting. Made from wingceltis bark and rice straw. Comes in raw (生宣, highly absorbent) and sized (熟宣, controlled absorbency) varieties. Archival: properly stored examples survive over a thousand years.

了 with a duration complement signals an action sustained for a period of time and treated as a completed, bounded episode. This construction is essential for talking about study, work, residence, and sustained experience. The duration frames the action as a finished chunk of time.

学 xué (to study; to learn) + 生 shēng (one who is still "green"; a junior person). The student as someone still growing, not yet ripe. One of the most common nouns in Chinese , every school context relies on it.

Notes: 学 xué (to study) + 问 wèn (to ask). Knowledge built by studying and asking, the deep, earned kind. 很有学问 "highly learned." The word itself teaches that real knowledge grows from questions, not answers alone.

学 (to study) + 者. The standard modern word for a scholar or academic researcher. This compound has been in continuous use since at least the Han dynasty. A 学者 is someone whose work consists of systematic study , the word appears in book reviews, conference programs, and academic citations alike.

雪 xuě (snow) + 白 bái (white). The brightest, purest white, with snow as the standard of comparison, exactly parallel to English "snow-white." This is a productive pattern in Chinese: a vivid object plus a color word yields an intensified shade.

Notes: 眼 yǎn + 光 guāng (light). Literally eye-light. The kind of seeing a person has , their taste in art, their judgment in business, their ability to spot a good investment or a good partner. 有眼光 yǒu yǎnguāng "to have a good eye"; 没眼光 "to have poor judgment"; 长远的眼光 "long-term vision."

English: to have blurred vision; to be dazzled

English: horizon (of experience); breadth of one's outlook
Notes: 眼 yǎn + 界 jiè (boundary; realm). The boundary of what one's eye has taken in , how widely one has seen, traveled, read, lived. 开阔眼界 kāikuò yǎnjiè "to broaden one's horizons" is one of the standard reasons given in Chinese for travel, study abroad, and reading widely.

眼 yǎn + 睛 jīng (eyeball; pupil). The standard everyday word for "eyes" in spoken Chinese. Single 眼 alone almost never serves this role; for "her eyes are beautiful" you say 她的眼睛很美 not 她的眼很美. The 睛 is light and unstressed in pronunciation.

Notes: 眼 yǎn + 泪 lèi (tear). Standard word for tears. 流眼泪 liú yǎnlèi "to shed tears"; 擦眼泪 cā yǎnlèi "to wipe away tears." The classical/literary equivalent is just 泪 alone or 泪水 lèishuǐ.

眼 yǎn + 力 lì (strength). The strength of one's seeing , both literally (sharpness of vision) and figuratively (judgment, ability to spot quality or fakery). The skilled antique-dealer is praised for 眼力 in detecting forgeries.

眼 yǎn + 皮 pí (skin). Eyelid. The colloquial idiom 眼皮底下 yǎnpí dǐxià "right under one's eyelids" means "right in front of one, in plain sight" , usually used to describe something missed or stolen despite being right there.

English: the look in one's eyes; gaze; expression

English: sunlight; sunshine; (of a person) sunny, positive, and open

English: intention and plan: what someone is going to do
Notes: 要 before a verb marks intention or imminence: 我要回家 (I'm going home / I want to go home; context decides). 打算 dǎsuàn (to plan) and 准备 zhǔnbèi (to prepare, to be about to) make the plan explicit: 我打算明年去中国 (I plan to go to China next year).
要 (yào, to want, to need) + 紧 (tight). What is held tight is what matters. Most common in the negative 不要紧 (bùyàojǐn), meaning never mind, it doesn't matter, often said to reassure.

要 (want/will) + 是 shì (be/this). A colloquial conditional meaning "if; supposing that." Slightly warmer and more personally invested than the neutral 如果 rúguǒ. Implies the speaker has some stake in the condition. Typically paired with 就 jiù in the consequence clause.

English: a palm's worth of sweat — anxious, breaking out in a sweat
Notes: 把 can measure abstract quantities that could theoretically fill a cupped hand , a handful of something. 一把汗 (a palm of sweat) is an idiom for being anxious or nervous to the point of sweating. 一把泪 (a handful of tears) appears in literary contexts for weeping.

English: getting on in age; a certain age (often with mild reproach)
Notes: 一把年纪 literally "a handful of years" , used to describe someone who is getting on in age. Often carries a mildly reproachful or surprised tone: someone that age should know better, or it's surprising they're doing something. Common in colloquial speech and semi-formal contexts.

English: a chair (one handle-shaped piece of furniture)
Notes: 把 as a measure word applies to objects that have a handle or can be grasped, or that you can take in hand , chairs (by the back), tools, weapons, fans, keys, locks, umbrellas, guitars. The connection to the core meaning of 把 (to grip) is transparent.

English: a cup / glass of water — 杯 bēi
Notes: 杯 bēi (cup, glass) counts liquids held in cups or glasses. The container becomes the classifier. This is the most transparent type: the classifier is the vessel. A large class of classifiers work this way , 碗, 盘, 瓶, 桶, 壶 , each named for the physical container holding the substance.
一 yī (one) + 笔 bǐ (measure word) + 钱 qián (money). A definite, lump amount of money, the kind written down as a single entry: 一大笔钱 "a large sum," 这笔钱 "this sum of money."
一 yī (one) + 笔 bǐ (measure word) + 生意 shēngyì (business). One transaction or deal, counted as a single recorded piece of business: 做一笔生意 "to do a deal," 一笔大生意 "a big deal."
一 yī (one) + 部 bù (measure word) + 电影 diànyǐng (film). The standard way to count a film, treating it as a single complete work. The same 部 counts a 小说 (novel) or a 电视剧 (TV series).
一 yī (one) + 部 bù (measure word) + 手机 shǒujī (phone). 部 counts a phone as a self-contained device. You will also hear 一个手机 in casual speech, but 一部手机 is the proper classifier.

English: a novel; one work of fiction
Notes: 一 yī (one) + 部 bù (measure word) + 小说 xiǎoshuō (novel). 部 counts a full-length novel as one finished work. For a short story you would more likely use 篇 piān, the classifier for shorter writings.
Disposable chopsticks: the individually wrapped bamboo or wood pairs given at most restaurants. Billions are used annually; their environmental cost is a topic of ongoing public debate.
Productive frame for arrival-triggered actions. 他一到就开始工作 (He started working as soon as he arrived). Pairs naturally with 回来 huí lái (return) and 到家 dào jiā (get home): 一回来就 / 一到家就.

English: a little; a bit (post-verbal, neutral or positive)
Notes: 一 yī (one) + 点 diǎn (dot; bit). Appears after adjectives and verbs, typically in commands, requests, or comparisons. Neutral to positive in coloring. 便宜一点 (a little cheaper , as a request), 快一点 (a little faster), 多吃一点 (eat a little more). In comparisons: 比昨天冷一点 (a little colder than yesterday).

English: a little; a bit (neutral, often comparative)
Notes: After an adjective, 一点儿 makes a neutral comparison, "a little more X": 大一点儿 (a bit bigger), 快一点儿 (a bit faster), 便宜一点儿 (a little cheaper). After a verb, it means "a little / some": 喝一点儿水 (drink a little water), 说一点儿 (say a bit).

Notes: 一点儿 measures out a small amount of an uncountable substance: 一点儿水 (a little water), 会一点儿中文 (speaks a little Chinese). It pairs with mass nouns where 几 pairs with countables. 部分 bùfen slices a defined whole: 一部分学生 (a portion of the students), 大部分时间 (most of the time). The trap of 一点儿 vs.

English: must; be sure to; definitely will
Notes: The emphatic resolve-and-urging frame. For yourself it is determination: 我一定要赢 ("I'm determined to win"). For others it is earnest pressing: 你一定要照顾好自己 ("you really must take good care of yourself").
队 as a measure word counts people or animals moving in a formed line: a column of soldiers, a string of camels, a file of schoolchildren.

When 工作 means a discrete job or position, it is counted with the measure word 份 fèn, the same word used for a portion or a document. 一份工作 ("one job"), 两份工作 ("two jobs," as in working two jobs). When 工作 means work as an activity or workload, it takes no measure word: 工作很多 ("there's a lot of work").
封 also works as the measure word for letters and other sealed correspondence: each sealed packet counts as one 封. 一封信 is one letter; 一封电子邮件 (yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn), one email.

一 + 个 (general measure word). 一 before tone 4 (个 gè) → yí. The most frequent combination of 一 in everyday speech: 一个人 yí gè rén (one person), 一个问题 yí gè wèntí (one question), 一个地方 yí gè dìfang (one place). 个 gè is the default measure word when no specific one applies.

Notes: 一 yī (one) + 件 jiàn (measure word) + 礼物 lǐwù (gift; present). A present counts as a discrete object, so it takes 件. The same classifier extends to other countable belongings and pieces of luggage: 一件行李 (one piece of luggage), 一件作品 (one work of art).

English: a matter: one affair; one thing to deal with
Notes: 一 yī (one) + 件 jiàn (measure word) + 事 shì (matter; affair). 件 is the standard classifier for an affair, an errand, or a piece of business, anything that can be treated as a single, separable concern. You do not say 一个事 in careful speech; the matter takes 件.

English: an item of clothing: one garment
Notes: 一 yī (one) + 件 jiàn (measure word) + 衣服 yīfu (clothing). 件 counts upper-body and one-piece garments: shirts, coats, dresses, sweaters. Lower-body garments take 条 tiáo instead (一条裤子 a pair of trousers, 一条裙子 a skirt), so the measure word itself signals which part of the body is meant.
一 yī (one) + 节 jié (measure word) + 课 kè (class). 节 here is the counter for class periods, each a fixed segment of the school day. 上一节课 "to attend a class period," 两节课 "two periods."

English: one remark; a single sentence; in a word
Notes: 一 yī (one) + 句 jù (measure word) + 话 huà (speech). A single spoken remark, counted with 句. Used adverbially, 一句话 means "in a word, to put it briefly."

The prototype 一…就 sentence. Used to describe something immediately clear, a design that needs no instructions, or a person who grasps something with no effort. 这个图表一看就懂 (This chart is self-explanatory).

English: safe journey: the standard farewell to a traveler
Notes: 一 yī (one, whole) + 路 lù (road) + 平安 píng'ān (peace, safety). "May the whole road be peaceful." The phrase you say at the airport, the train station, or as the car pulls away. Slightly more formal than 一路顺风 yílù shùnfēng ("may the wind be with you").

English: one side; one surface; (measure) one flat object
Notes: 一 yī (one) + 面 miàn (measure word). 面 counts flat, surface-like objects: 一面镜子 (a mirror), 一面墙 (a wall), 一面旗 (a flag). As a noun 一面 also means "one side" of an argument or "one aspect."

English: all one's life; a whole lifetime; forever
Notes: 一生 yìshēng (one life) + 一世 yíshì (one lifetime). A doubled phrase for the entirety of a person's days, common in vows of love and loyalty: 我会爱你一生一世 "I will love you for the rest of my life." Warmer and more lyrical than the plain 一辈子.

一 yī (one) + 首 shǒu (measure word) + 歌 gē (song). 首 is the classifier for songs and poems: 一首歌 a song, 一首诗 a poem, 一首词 a lyric. Each piece is counted as one self-contained "head." 唱一首歌 "to sing a song."

一 yī (one) + 首 shǒu (measure word) + 诗 shī (poem). The same classifier counts poems. 写一首诗 "to write a poem," 背一首诗 "to recite a poem from memory." A classical anthology is described as so many 首 of verse.

English: one cow; a head of cattle
Notes: 一 yī (one) + 头 tóu (measure word) + 牛 niú (cow). Here 头 keeps its full tone as the classifier for large livestock: cattle, pigs, sheep, elephants. You count beasts by the head.

A related but distinct adverb: 一下子 means "all at once, in one go, suddenly," describing rapid or abrupt change rather than softening a verb: 天一下子黑了 ("the sky went dark all at once"). Do not confuse it with the verb-softening 一下: 看一下 ("have a look") versus 一下子看完了 ("finished reading it in one go").

English: all along; consistently; up to now
Notes: 一 yī (one; throughout) + 向 xiàng (facing back along). A habit or state held unbroken up to the present: 他一向如此 "he has always been like this." Marks long-standing consistency, not a one-off.

Notes: 一些 introduces an indefinite amount: 我买了一些水果 (I bought some fruit). 有的 and 有些 pick out a subset of a known or generic whole, and they live at the front of the sentence: 有的人喜欢，有的人不喜欢 (some people like it, some don't). The classic restriction: 有的 phrases resist the object position.

Marks two things as the same. The frame is A 跟 B 一样 (跟 gēn or 和 hé link the two). Add an adjective to compare a specific quality as equal: A 跟 B 一样 + Adj. Negate as A 跟 B 不一样 ("different") or A 跟 B 不一样 + Adj. 一样 alone can also modify a noun: 一样的衣服 ("the same clothes").
Tags: society connections meaning characters perception grammar conjunction communication spoken comparison syntax evaluation daily-life

Notes: 一 + 致 zhì (to reach; to arrive at). All arriving at one point. 意见一致 (unanimous opinion), 行动一致 (acting in concert), 保持一致 (maintain consistency). Higher register than 一样 yīyàng , used in formal and official contexts. 众口一致 (everyone speaking with one mouth = unanimous) is a near-chengyu variant.

English: to simply leave; to walk away from a problem
Notes: 一 + 走了之 , "just walk off and be done with it." A set phrase for leaving without dealing with the situation. Pejorative: the person who 一走了之 is abandoning responsibility. Used critically: 你不能就这样一走了之 (you can't just walk away like that).

The classical and Wu-dialect "she." In the 1917 debate, some intellectuals advocated reviving 伊 instead of coining 她, since 伊 already had a feminine reading in some classical poetry and avoided the male-default asymmetry.

Notes: 医 yī (medicine; to heal) + 生 shēng (practitioner). The standard word for doctor in mainland China. Note the 生 suffix , it originally meant "one who practices/studies" (compare 学生, 先生). 看医生 = "to see a doctor."

Notes: 遗 yí (to leave behind) + 传 chuán (to hand down). The biological passing of traits from parent to offspring: 遗传病 "hereditary disease," 遗传基因 "the genes one inherits." The body's own version of handing something down across generations.
疑 yí (to doubt) + 问 wèn (to ask). A question that arises from uncertainty: 毫无疑问 háo wú yíwèn "without the slightest doubt." Also the grammatical term, as in 疑问句 yíwènjù "interrogative sentence."

English: in order to facilitate; so as to make convenient; so that
Notes: 以 (in order to) + 便 (convenient; to facilitate). Introduces a purpose clause describing how the preceding action creates favorable conditions for what follows. Register: formal written Chinese.

Notes: Substitute tea for spirits: the accepted formula for toasting without drinking alcohol. The phrase is spoken while raising a cup of tea, acknowledging the substitution explicitly.

English: as a precaution against; in order to guard against
Notes: 以 (in order to) + 防 (to guard against; to defend). Often extended to 以防万一 yǐfáng wànyī , "in order to guard against the one-in-ten-thousand chance," i.e., as a just-in-case precaution. One of the most common 以 compounds in everyday written Chinese.
Tags: grammar classical syntax conjunction particle literary

English: after; afterward; in the future; from now on
Notes: 以 (positional marker) + 后 (behind; after). The paired counterpart to 以前. Stands alone for "in the future" or follows a time reference for "after X." Compare: 之后 zhīhòu (slightly more classical feel; often interchangeable) and 后来 hòulái (what happened next in a narrative , retrospective only).
Tags: direction time royalty grammar classical syntax conjunction particle literary daily-life cosmology

English: in order to avoid; so as to prevent; lest
Notes: 以 (in order to) + 免 (to avoid; to exempt from). Introduces a clause describing what the preceding action is intended to prevent. Appears in instructions, warnings, and formal recommendations.
Tags: grammar classical syntax conjunction particle literary

English: before; previously; in the past; formerly
Notes: 以 yǐ (by means of; from; at) + 前 qián (front; before). "From the front / from before": the time that stands in front of the present moment. The most versatile and common temporal use of 前. Used after a specific time phrase (三年以前, three years ago) or alone (以前, in the past, formerly).
Tags: direction time philosophy grammar classical syntax conjunction particle literary vocabulary daily-life cosmology

#fields:Hanzi: 以前 · 现在 · 以后
English: before · now · after: the relative frame
Notes: 以前 and 以后 attach to any reference point: 三年以前 (three years ago), 吃饭以后 (after eating), or stand alone to mean "formerly" and "from now on". 的时候 de shíhou (when …) frames simultaneity: 我小的时候 (when I was little).

English: above (a number); the above-mentioned; and more
Notes: 以 yǐ (from; by means of; at) + 上 shàng (above; higher). Used after a number or category to mean "and above" or "the following." Three uses: quantitative (三十以上 = thirty or more), sequential (如以上所述 = as stated above), and categorical (十八岁以上 = eighteen and older).

English: above / the above-mentioned · below / the following · more than / less than
Notes: 以上 yǐshàng (以 + 上 above): covers both spatial above and "more than a quantity" (十八岁以上 , 18 and above) and "what has been stated above" in written discourse (以上是本次报告的主要内容 , the above is the main content of this report). 以下 yǐxià mirrors it exactly in the opposite direction.
Tags: grammar classical syntax conjunction particle literary

Notes: 以 (taking) + 为 (to be; to regard as). In classical Chinese the construction meant "to regard X as Y." In modern speech, 以为 has narrowed to almost always imply that the assumption turned out to be wrong , making it a useful signal of correction or disappointment.
Tags: grammar classical taoism philosophy daoism wuwei syntax conjunction particle literary

English: self-centered; to place oneself at the center

Notes: 以 yǐ (from; from this point) + 下 xià (below; the following). Three uses mirror exactly those of its counterpart 以上: quantitative (十八岁以下 = under eighteen), sequential (以下是通知 = the following is an announcement), and organizational. The pair 以上/以下 frames all formal Chinese enumeration.
Tags: direction grammar motion politics history worldview

Notes: A bilingual contract needs a clause saying which version prevails if they conflict (如有冲突 rú yǒu chōngtū). Chinese courts and arbitrators work in Chinese, so the Chinese text is the one that will be read. Have it translated back to you independently rather than trusting that the two versions match.

English: a righteous act; a just cause; a deed done for principle
Notes: 义 (righteous) + 举 (act; move; deed; to raise up). A deed that rises to the level of a principled act , something done not for personal gain but for a cause recognized as right. Often used of charitable acts, acts of solidarity, or historical deeds that defended the weak or resisted injustice.

English: loyalty among friends; the code of doing right by your people
Notes: 义 (righteousness; what is right) + 气 (spirit; energy; disposition). The disposition to do right by the people bound to you , friends, brothers, colleagues, sworn companions. 义气 operates in a different register from 正义: where 正义 is institutional and universal, 义气 is personal and relational.
Tags: literature novels classics classical song rebellion confucianism ethics virtue philosophy wuxia culture society

English: a righteous person; a man of principle; one who sacrifices for a just cause
Notes: 义 (righteousness) + 士 (a person of standing; an educated or principled person). Someone whose defining quality is acting on principle rather than self-interest, particularly at personal cost. 义士 is a term of high historical admiration.

义 (what is right) + 务 (affair; task; work). The affair of doing what is right , the tasks that fall to you not because you chose them but because they are the right ones for someone in your position. 义务 spans the full range from formal legal obligation to moral duty.
Tags: confucianism ethics virtue philosophy social connections culture classical

English: One hundred million, the great unit above 万
Notes: One hundred million, the great unit above 万. China's population is 十四亿 (shísì yì, 1.4 billion), a figure every learner should be able to parse and produce.

English: to comment on; to talk about (often behind the scenes)
Notes: 议 yì (to deliberate, to propose) + 论. To comment on or talk about something, frequently with an undertone of gossip or unsolicited opinion. 议论纷纷 yìlùn fēnfēn describes a crowd buzzing with opinions. Also the name of a school essay genre: 议论文 yìlùnwén, the argumentative essay.

Notes: The single character at the heart of the entire system. The commentary tradition insists it holds three meanings at once: 变易 biànyì (the fact of change, everything transforms), 不易 bùyì (the unchanging principle behind change, the laws of transformation are constant), and 简易 jiǎnyì (the simplicity be…

The "Yi-an style": the distinctive lyric mode of Li Qingzhao (whose courtesy name was Yi-an 易安). Characterized by colloquial precision, physical specificity, and a technically innovative use of reduplicated binomes to convey emotional states.

Notes: 意 yì (notion) + 见 jiàn (to see; view). What the mind sees on a matter, that is, a considered opinion: 提意见 "to offer a view." It can lean negative, where 有意见 means to have a complaint or grievance.
Tags: perception knowing daily-life meaning mind emotion characters

English: the poetic realm — atmosphere, mood, and implied space
Notes: 意 yì (meaning; intention; feeling) + 境 jìng (realm; situation; space). The characteristic Chinese aesthetic concept of the space created beyond the words themselves: what the poem evokes rather than describes. Good poetry has 意境; pedestrian verse merely reports facts.
Tags: arts nature taoism aesthetics classical art culture visual literary history

English: the intention has arrived — the gesture is enough; the thought counts
Notes: Used to accept a gift graciously without demanding more, or to reassure a giver that their token gesture was sufficient and appreciated. Conveys: "I see your heart in this; the object is secondary." Also used reflexively by givers: 意思到了就好 , "as long as the intention is communicated, that's enough."

English: a token gesture; to make a symbolic offering; "just a little something"
Notes: Reduplication softens and miniaturizes the meaning , a universal Chinese pattern. 意思意思 as a verb phrase means "to make a token gesture, to acknowledge the relationship symbolically." It signals effort without demanding reciprocal debt.

意 yì (notion; expectation) + 外 wài (outside). Outside what the heart anticipated, hence unexpected: 意外的消息 "surprising news." As a noun it names an accident or mishap that fell beyond anyone's reckoning.
Image, imagistic motif. Tang criticism valued the evocative image (意象) over explicit statement , show, don't tell, carried to its highest refinement.

意 (intention) + 义 (righteousness; principle). More serious and weighty than 意思. 意义 refers to significance in the deeper sense , the kind that requires reflection. Used for historical significance, life meaning, moral weight. 人生的意义 (the meaning of life) uses 意义, never 意思.

Notes: The intention precedes the brush: the principle that a painter must have fully conceived the work before beginning to paint, because ink on xuan paper cannot be corrected. Applies equally to calligraphy.

Notes: Therefore or "for this reason." More formal than 所以, common in written and considered spoken contexts. Often used to introduce a conclusion drawn from preceding points: 因此, 我们决定… ("therefore, we decided…").

Notes: 因 yīn (because of) + 而 ér (and so). A written connective that draws a result from a stated cause, close to 因此 but smoother in flowing prose: 准备充分，因而很顺利 "well prepared, and so it went smoothly."
Tags: conjunction cohesion classical characters logic meaning

Notes: 因 yīn (cause) + 果 guǒ (fruit; result). The cause-and-effect pair as a single concept, from the everyday 因果关系 "causal relationship" to the Buddhist law of karma, where every act ripens into its fruit.
Tags: religion buddhism culture logic cohesion meaning characters transmission history philosophy cosmology classical fate life

Notes: 因 yīn (cause) + 素 sù (element). One of the contributing causes that feed into an outcome, used of the many partial causes behind a complex result: 经济因素 "economic factors," 不安全因素 "safety hazards."

因 yīn (cause; reason; because of) + 为 wèi (for; on account of). The most important conjunction in the language for expressing cause. Pairs with 所以 suǒyǐ (therefore) to form the standard causal construction: 因为 X，所以 Y (because X, therefore Y).

English: the lunar calendar; the traditional Chinese calendar
Notes: 阴 yīn (moon; lunar) + 历 lì (calendar). The traditional calendar reckoned by the phases of the moon, as opposed to the 阳历 (yánglì, the sun-based Gregorian calendar). Strictly the Chinese traditional calendar is 阴阳合历 (a combined lunisolar calendar), but in everyday speech 阴历 is what people call it.
Tags: history calendar time characters cosmology nature weather

English: shady and cool; a shaded cool spot
Notes: 阴 yīn (shade) + 凉 liáng (cool). Shaded and pleasantly cool, the welcome shade of a tree on a hot day. Here the shadow is entirely positive, the relief the shaded slope offers in summer.

English: conspiracy; sinister plot; scheme operating in darkness
Notes: 阴 yīn (dark; covert; hidden) + 谋 móu (to plot; to scheme). A plan that operates in shadow, unseen , the hidden face that 阴 takes when it manifests as human deception. The contrast with open, legitimate action (which would be 阳) is built into the word.

阴 yīn (shaded; clouded) + 天 tiān (sky; day; weather). A day when clouds cover the sun, the most concrete everyday use of 阴. This is the original geographic shade made meteorological: the whole sky becomes the shaded slope.

English: yin deficiency — the yin coolant is insufficient; yang heat dominates
Notes: 虚 xū = deficient; empty; insufficient. Classic 阴虚 symptoms: heat sensations in the palms and soles of feet (五心烦热), night sweats (盗汗 dào hàn), dry mouth and throat, redness of the cheeks in the afternoon, irritability, insomnia.
Tags: cosmology philosophy binary tcm body culture

English: harmony of yin and yang; the ideal state of health and well-being
Notes: 调 tiáo (to tune; to harmonize; to adjust) + 和 hé (harmony; peace). The goal of all Chinese medical practice: not the maximization of either force, but their active, dynamic harmony. 调和 is active , it is a verb about process, not a noun describing a state.

English: balance of yin and yang; the state of dynamic equilibrium
Notes: The core goal in 阴阳 thinking is not the elimination of one force or the dominance of the other , it is 平衡 pínghéng: dynamic balance between them. This is not static equilibrium (like a scale perfectly level) but living balance (like a tightrope walker, constantly adjusting).

English: yin-yang and the Five Phases — the paired cosmological framework
Notes: The two systems developed in parallel during the Warring States period and were synthesized into a unified framework by the Han dynasty, particularly in the 黄帝内经 (Yellow Emperor's Classic, compiled ca. 200 BCE–200 CE).
Tags: wuxing five-phases cosmology philosophy tcm nature yin-yang history ancient

English: shadow; a shadow over the heart; a lingering trauma
Notes: 阴 yīn (shade) + 影 yǐng (shadow; image). A literal shadow, the dark shape cast where light is blocked, and also a medical shadow on an X-ray (肺部阴影, a shadow on the lung).

Music + 会 (gathering), usually implying the classical hall; a pop star's arena show is a 演唱会 (yǎnchànghuì, "performed-singing gathering"). Tickets for either are 票, and 抢票 ("snatching tickets") describes the purchase experience accurately.

音乐 yīnyuè (music) + 家 jiā. Implies serious, dedicated musical mastery: a composer, a concert performer, a conductor rather than a casual musician. Distinguished from 歌手 gēshǒu (singer/pop artist) by the 家 suffix, which implies depth, discipline, and classical standing.
音 yīn (sound; word) + 信 xìn (message; letter). News or word of someone far away. Most common in the negative: 没有音信 "no word at all," and the idiom 杳无音信, vanished without a trace.
银 (yín, silver) + 河 (river). A silver river across the night sky. Chinese named the galaxy as a river of stars long before it was a galaxy, and the metaphor stuck.

银 yín (silver) + 行 háng. The silver-row , originally a row of money-changers along a market street, then by extension the modern banking institution. The single most-tested 行-háng word: students who default to xíng on every 行 will read this wrong forever.

English: to introduce; to bring in (technology, talent, methods)
Notes: 引 yǐn (to draw; to lead) + 进 jìn (to take in). To bring something in from outside, typically from abroad: 引进技术 "introduce technology," 引进人才 "bring in talent."

English: yum cha; going for dim sum; drinking tea

Notes: 饮食 yǐnshí (food and drink, diet) + 文化 (culture). Chinese food culture is one of the most discussed topics in 文化 discourse , not just cuisine but the entire social system of eating: banquet etiquette, regional identity, seasonal eating, the pairing of food with medicine and philosophy.
Seal paste: the vermilion medium used to ink seals. Made from cinnabar 朱砂 (mercuric sulfide), sesame oil, and mugwort fiber. The highest-quality seal paste is made in Zhangzhou, Fujian.
